title: NFL clears the air on field condition concerns for Ravens-Cowboys Week 3 matchup in Brazil
summary: Baltimore and Dallas will kick off from Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, Sunday on CBS
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys are in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and set to kick off their Week 3 matchup at Maracana Stadium on Sunday. In the lead-up to this international contest, concerns surrounding the field conditions at Maracana Stadium have been one of the central storylines. However, on the eve of the matchup, the league says the field good to go for play, with NFL field director Nick Pappas telling reporters in Brazil on Saturday that there is "no need to worry."
"We have an independent inspector that comes in, walks with myself, walks with a member of the NFLPA," Pappas said, via Pro Football Talk . "They were here yesterday. Performed that test. Things check out. We've made additional improvements to the field that we think were helpful."
Maracana Stadium's field has been considered to be in poor shape due to the wear and tear of the Brazilian soccer season. Both Flamengo and Fluminense, two local clubs, play on the field at least once a week, per the Associated Press . Flamengo midfielder Giorgian De Arrascaeta even noted after a recent game that, "We've been struggling a lot in these last few games, and the field keeps getting worse."
Specifically, there are concerns about the turf's traction and stability, and the NFL even needed to reinforce the field's stitching.
NFLPA executive director JC Tretter took to social media on Friday to voice the players' union's concerns about the playing surface. Tretter also advocated for universal "field standards" and raised concerns about international expansion, noting two of the three games played in Brazil have had field-related issues.
"We've been in regular communication with the league about the field," Tretter wrote on X . "Both the NFLPA's and the league's field experts have been on the ground in Brazil for days, monitoring conditions and working to make the surface as safe and playable as possible for Sunday.
"Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability. They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff."
Sunday will be the NFL's third game in Brazil since 2024, but the first at Maracana Stadium. The first two were played at NeoQuimica Arena in São Paulo. In the first game played at that arena, the field conditions were widely criticised, as players from both the Philadelphia Eagles and Green Bay Packers were seen changing their cleats to try and reduce slipping.

title: Deion Sanders puzzled by Travis Hunter's role with Jaguars: 'I have no idea what's going on'
summary: The Colorado coach is keeping up with his former player in the NFL
full_text:
From winning the Heisman as college football's top two-way threat at Colorado to being used as a decoy of sorts offensively in his second NFL season, Travis Hunter's role with the Jaguars has yet to be defined this fall.
The former first-round pick recorded 28 receptions for 298 yards and a touchdown as a rookie over seven games and started in the secondary before a season-ending knee injury in 2025.
Now? Jacksonville's barely using Hunter on offense and he's been a rotational player on the other side of the football. Colorado coach Deion Sanders is baffled by his former player's usage in what's been an undefined role thus far heading into Sunday's game with the Patriots.
"I don't ask questions because I'm not there," Sanders said this week on his coaches show . "I don't know what transpires when we're not looking. I have no idea what's going on. I know who he was and who he is right now. I know what he's capable of. I do know that."
During last week's loss to the Broncos, Hunter only played 60% of Jacksonville's total plays on defense.
"Any time you struggle offensively, you look at the totality of it all," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said this week . "Travis is a big part of that obviously. We're looking at continuing to find different ways to get him involved. You're also looking at the other side of the ball. … We're gonna look at giving him some more this week."
Hunter's on-field snaps offensively last season dwindled as the year progressed prior to injury. At Colorado, Hunter averaged more 113 snaps per game during his final campaign and rarely came off the field.
Sanders said last September during Hunter's rookie season that Coen and the Jaguars weren't using him enough and questioned the lightened workload.
"I've seen it with my own eyes on an everyday basis for three straight years, so I know what he's capable of, and I know how you've got to take care of him," Sanders said during a New Heights podcast episode . "He never practices on Tuesday. He practices on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. He was ready to play a hundred and some snaps on Saturday, so you didn't need to use him on a Tuesday or a Monday. You don't use him like that."
Earlier this offseason, Sanders said he was surprised the Jaguars didn't reach out about game planning and how to utilize Hunter's full skill set.
"I've had him of rate last three (years)," Sanders said on The Barbershop podcast in May . "Don't you think you would want to talk to me to let me know, to ask me how — what gets him going and what backs him off and, and what, like, you wouldn't want to know that?"
Coen expects Hunter to play more total snaps agains the Patriots and said the cornerback rotation was all part of his team's plan early this fall.
"We did it for the most part last season as well before Travis got hurt," Coen said this week. "It's something we have to continue to do. We have corners we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us.
"They've been in the system now. We have to play it better, but we also have to get to the quarterback to help those guys out as well in the back end. It's a rotation based on pregame. We have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It has been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."
Hunter has not complained about his role after two games and said following the loss to the Broncos that he was simply following the coaching staff's plan for him.

title: Is Zay Flowers playing vs. Cowboys in Week 3? Ravens WR could be on pitch count if he suits up, per report
summary: Flowers is officially listed as questionable due to a hamstring injury
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are down in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, for their Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys . While there is buzz for their international regular-season showdown, there is uncertainty looming over the offense, specifically when it comes to wideout Zay Flowers .
The 2023 first-round pick has been dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered in the Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts , which forced him to miss Week 2 against the New Orleans Saints . Flowers did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but did participate in a limited capacity on Friday. The team has officially listed him as questionable for the contest.
ESPN reports that Flowers is expected to test the hamstring injury pregame. If he does end up playing, he would likely be on a pitch count for the contest. Earlier this week, head coach Jesse Minter mentioned Flowers among the players who "have a real opportunity to maybe help us in the game," via the official team website .
Before exiting the season opener against Indy, Flowers was going nuclear in first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system. He caught five of his six targets from Lamar Jackson for 150 yards and a touchdown. Those 150 yards receiving set a new career high for the 26-year-old.
If Flowers is able to play (even in a limited capacity), he has a juicy matchup against a Cowboys defense that is allowing the fourth-most yards per game (391.5) in the NFL this season.
On top of this uncertainty for Baltimore's offense, Flowers' status is also a key concern for fantasy football managers. Even if he does play, this latest report suggests that Flowers could see limited action due to being on a pitch count, making the decision to play him even if he is active that much more difficult.
To make matters even more befuddling, the Ravens won't kick off from Brazil until 4:25 p.m. ET, meaning that we won't hear about his status until midway through the early slate. That could leave managers needing to make a decision early and without the full scope of his status if their other options play at 1 p.m. ET.
Because of the injury status, CBS Sports fantasy experts do not have Flowers ranked in Week 3, while consensus currently has fellow Ravens wideout Rashod Bateman listed as WR20 in PPR leagues and WR21 in standard leagues.

title: Giants quarterback trade rumors: New York has made calls this week with a move possibly imminent
summary: Jaxson Dart underwent season-ending knee surgery this week
full_text:
The New York Giants were delivered a punch to the gut this week after tests revealed that Jaxson Dart's knee injury that he suffered on Monday night will, in fact, end his season. The second-year signal-caller has already undergone surgery to repair the injury, and the Giants suddenly find themselves in a state of disarray under center. Jameis Winston , who came in under duress for Dart in Week 2, will start on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans , but New York does appear to be in the market to bolster the depth of the quarterback room.
In the aftermath of Dart's injury, the Giants have spent the week making calls on quarterbacks, according to The Ringer. Sources told the outlet that they believe it's a matter of when, not if, New York makes a move to acquire a quarterback, and it could come as soon as Monday.
Winston, who signed a two-year, $13 million extension earlier this month, is currently the only quarterback on the active roster, but Jake Haener will most likely be elevated from the practice squad for Week 3. That leaves them remarkably thin at the position even if they are content with Winston as the starter going forward.
However, it's worth noting that there is a clash in styles between Dart and Winston, which could give us a clue into what kind of quarterback New York may be on the hunt for. This latest report notes that offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and his staff spent the offseason crafting the offense around Dart's mobility and physical play style. That's not Winston's forte, as he's more of a traditional dropback passer.
With that in mind, the game plan for Week 3 is expected to be altered quite a bit against Tennessee, but if the Giants want to return to something close to the philosophical approach they had with Dart, they'd need to bring someone else in who has the ability to make plays with his legs.
While listing several available quarterbacks, The Ringer's report adds that Minnesota's J.J. McCarthy is an intriguing option, especially with the front office previously doing extensive work on him during the pre-draft process in 2024. While not as physical of a runner as Dart, McCarthy has some mobility to his game and is still only 23 years old. His tenure with the Vikings has gone sideways, and he finds himself as the third-string option behind Kyler Murray (starter) and Carson Wentz (top backup), making him potentially available via trade. He also played for John Harbaugh's brother, Jim Harbaugh, at Michigan, so there is somewhat of a connection there.
While he's never played for the Giants or John Harbaugh before, New York does have some familiarity with current Chiefs backup quarterback Justin Fields thanks to the presence of Nagy. The Giants OC worked with Fields during his rookie season in 2021, when he was the head coach of the Chicago Bears . Acquiring Fields would certainly unlock the rushing component of Nagy's offense, averaging 48.2 rushing yards per game over his career. That said, the rub on Fields has been his inconsistency as a passer, so the Giants would be taking a step back in that regard. Kansas City acquired Fields from the Jets this offseason as insurance in the event that Patrick Mahomes (recovering from a torn ACL and LCL) wouldn't be ready for the start of the year. However, Mahomes has been able to return with flying colors, which could make Fields expendable. That's especially true if K.C. is comfortable elevating rookie Garrett Nussmeier as their top backup.

title: Cardinals Kei’Trel Clark fined for using eye black message
summary: Arizona Cardinals cornerback Kei’Trel Clark was fined $6,651 for wearing eye black with a message inscribed after last week’s 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The NFL does not play with uniforms. There are a ton of rules and regulations regarding cleats, sweatbands, undershirts, helmets, and the uniform itself. RELATED: CARDINALS PLACE WILL JOHNSON ON […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kei'trel Clark #13 of the Arizona Cardinals enters the stadium prior to a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona Cardinals cornerback Kei’Trel Clark was fined $6,651 for wearing eye black with a message inscribed after last week’s 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The NFL does not play with uniforms. There are a ton of rules and regulations regarding cleats, sweatbands, undershirts, helmets, and the uniform itself. RELATED: CARDINALS PLACE WILL JOHNSON ON IR Clark’s message stated: “GLORY BE (peace symbol) 2 GOD.” The NFL takes a lot of pride in keeping the presentation of its league professional and clean. If Clark writes in paint pen on his eye black a message, then somebody else takes that cue and writes their own message. Then it is writing on socks or sweatbands, unauthorized logos, paint pen on a cleat, or the tail of a T-shirt hanging. “Happy Birthday, Tashaun!” would become a weekly message seen on national TV. Another reason the NFL is so determined is its sponsorships. Uniform makers pay quite a bit to display their logo. Oakley does as well. The NFL doesn’t want painted messages on cleats stating, “Shoe Palace has great deals!” The league does not make any money off of these types of messages, so they outlaw everything. Clark went to his Instagram account and stated: “I need answers. 6.6K for giving God the Glory.” No, 6.6K for not following the league’s uniform code. The NFL does not care about a sack of dried butter beans that you want to promote your faith. Clark has from Monday until Saturday to preach to as many folks as possible about finding God and praising Jesus. But Clark will need to do this within his own space. And it’s not like Clark is a superstar on the Cardinals roster. He currently backs up Denzel Burke at the left cornerback spot. The specific financial terms and dollar amounts that Oakley pays the NFL are not publicly disclosed, which means it must be pretty lucrative. And all 32 NFL teams get a slice of that deal. The current contract was extended until 2030. Those are messages on NFL uniforms that pay handsomely. Eye black today is no longer a traditional roll-on stick. They are like fabric Band-Aids that peel off with glue underneath. They can be written on with silver paint pens very easily before being installed. While playing for the University of Florida, QB Tim Tebow always had a scripture written on his eye black that was seen by millions every game. But once he suited up in the NFL, the written messages ceased. And it is not like fining Clark is a one-off. The NFL has been consistent about this for years: No writing of any kind on face prints. What is odd are the circumstances. At every NFL game, there are uniform cops, called NFL uniform inspectors, on each sideline. They patrol the field during pre-game warmups and remain on the sidelines throughout the entire game, switching sidelines at the end of each quarter to monitor both teams fairly. They are paid by the league instead of through the Cardinals, which makes them act as neutral, league-appointed officials representing the NFL Compliance Department. They are usually two former players of the team itself. If the inspectors see any discrepancy, they will approach the player and tell them what is wrong, then expect the athlete to correct the situation and are usually cool about the infraction, giving ample time to fix the issue. If the player persists, the uniform cops write it up and submit it to the league. Players are paid via direct deposit every two weeks. Clark’s deposit will simply be short by $6,651. The second offense of the standard uniform code is $17,911. A third offense can result in game suspensions, for which the player does not get paid whatsoever for each game he is out. The source of the fine is included in Rule 5, Section 4, Article 8 of the NFL’s 2026 rulebook. It states that Clark cited the unauthorized personal message on his eye black regardless of what the message was. LINK: LIST OF NFL FINES Clark seems to be in attack mode ever since he received his fine letter in the mail. He followed it with a string of memes aimed at the fine and also shared a picture of himself wearing eye black marked “INSHALLAH.” He stated: “I got to report to God at the end of my days on the day of judgment!” I’ll always give God the glory out loud 😎 All good.” That is perfectly fine and good. But the league does not care for one minute whether Clark plays in their league or not. His cap hit this year is $1.2 million. Maybe he can get his real estate license and make that kind of money. This is not Clark’s first run-in with the NFL’s uniform rules. In October 2025, he was fined $5,797 after wearing what the league described as a “black streamer towel” during Arizona’s game against the Indianapolis Colts. Only white licensed towels are approved. So, bow up all you want, Clark. It’s your money to lose, and you aren’t going to buck the league rules. You want answers? It is pretty simple: Don’t write on your eye black. Period. Or you will find work as a substitute school teacher in your future very soon.

title: Falcons Draft 2027: 10 Prospects to Watch in Week 4 of College Football
summary: The crazy number of upsets was just an appetizer before college football went into full tilt, with six Top-25 matchups and five other games involving Top-25 teams that could also turn into upsets. That’s 17 AP Top-25 teams that have to lock in a bit more than usual, not to mention plenty of other games […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images The crazy number of upsets was just an appetizer before college football went into full tilt, with six Top-25 matchups and five other games involving Top-25 teams that could also turn into upsets. That’s 17 AP Top-25 teams that have to lock in a bit more than usual, not to mention plenty of other games to keep your eye on throughout the day, like Colorado-Baylor (12 pm EST, ESPN2), UCLA-Maryland (1:30 pm EST, Big Ten Network), TCU-UCF (3:30 pm EST, FS1) and Oklahoma State-West Virginia (7 pm EST, FS1). But you’re not here to hear me badger about which games to watch. You’re here to find guys who may be wearing red and black next April, and 10 2027 NFL Draft prospects are in this loaded Week 4 slate of college football that Atlanta Falcons fans should keep an eye out for. Kayin Lee, CB, Tennessee vs. Texas Neyland Stadium – Knoxville, TN 12 pm EST – ABC You’ll be hard pressed to find many corners with the natural fluidity and quickness of Tennessee CB Kayin Lee. Everything looks easy with him. Loose hips, quick feet and very little wasted movement when he has to transition. pic.twitter.com/R3PsFmmK7i — Jack Brentnall (@Jack_Brentnall) September 2, 2026 Kayin Lee and Cam Coleman, the sensational wide receiver at Texas, were teammates at Auburn last season. This week, they face each other in Knoxville to kick off a jam-packed day of college football. Lee, at 5’11”, 190 pounds, was a force at Cedar Grove High School and brought that same physicality to Auburn and now to Tennessee. He hasn’t had a great start to the season, but an impressive showing against Coleman, Ryan Wingo, and this talented Texas receiver room could be huge for his draft stock. Katin Houser, QB, Illinois vs. Ohio State Ohio Stadium – Columbus, OH 12 pm EST – Fox Going into their game against Ohio State on Saturday, Illinois QB Katin Houser (4) has been putting NFL throws on tape all season. And WR Collin Dixon (17) now leads college football in receiving TDs. He's got a solid catch radius and ability to work through contact. pic.twitter.com/OYlFqBrayP — Anthony Russo (@Anthony_Russo97) September 21, 2026 This is the week. Katin Houser has been one of the favorites of the draft community in that next tier of quarterbacks behind Arch Manning, Dante Moore and Darian Mensah. Houser has an NFL-caliber arm and enough ability to move outside the pocket where he should be a problem for college defenses. After years of discourse, Houser and Ole Miss’ Trinidad Chambliss may bring back the bet on Day Two quarterbacks. Wayne Knight, RB, UCLA vs. Maryland SECU Stadium – College Park, MD 1:30 pm EST – Big Ten Network Wayne Knight ran all over Purdue 🔥 18 CAR, 177 RUYDS, 2 TDS First Bruin with multiple rushing TDs in three straight games since DeShaun Foster in 2001. pic.twitter.com/CZrhjdPS5s — CFB Performances (@performancesCFB) September 20, 2026 Hello, Newman. Wait, wrong guy. This Wayne Knight is tied with Florida’s Jadan Baugh for the most rushing touchdowns in the country. After four years at James Madison, Knight jumped to P4 ball and immediately made an impact for the Bruins. He is a smaller back at 5’7”, 193 pounds, but he has all the qualities that help backs of that size translate to the NFL. He runs with tenacity; the first contact struggles to bring him down; he has the agility to make people miss in phone booths and he has the vision to find daylight where there may not be one. Peyton Bowen, S, Oklahoma vs. Georgia Sanford Stadium – Athens, GA – 3:30 pm EST – ESPN Oklahoma S Peyton Bowen #22 is a certified ball player. Does a great job on this backside pursuit to run the angle correctly and square up the ball carrier. Shuts the door on him emphatically pic.twitter.com/vyKnVT7BhA — Daniel Harms (@InHarmsWay19) September 18, 2026 Atlanta should continue to look to the Oklahoma program for safeties. At 6’0”, 201 pounds, Bowen is a more seamless fit on the back end than Bowman may be as a true safety. That’s not including his ability in man coverage or his ability to come down in the run game from deep in the secondary. Brendan Bett, DL, Florida vs. Ole Miss Ben Hill Griffin Stadium – Gainesville, FL 3:30 pm EST – ABC Brendan Bett is going to be the leader for the #Gators on the interior in 2026, but I think Jeramiah McCloud has a chance to be a Caleb Banks type difference maker down the road for Florida. Flashed plenty in 159 snaps as a true freshman and was a standout this spring. pic.twitter.com/8Bo3vXEloG — Dylan Olive (@DylanOlive_UF) May 4, 2026 Despite his reputation after his incident against South Florida last season, Bett is still one of the better athletes you’ll find on a defensive line this season. At 6’4”, 312 pounds, Bett’s lateral quickness and strength are welcome additions to one of the more athletically gifted defensive lines in football. Trevor Lauck, OT, Iowa vs. Michigan Michigan Stadium – Ann Arbor, MI 3:30 pm EST – CBS Iowa LT Trevor Lauck (#59) continues to give me Jake Matthews vibes. Nothing flashy but he just wins reps in pass pro. Solid in the run game. pic.twitter.com/zdLUvPncog — Ryan Roberts (@RiseNDraft) September 18, 2026 With the Falcons playing a bit better than in those first two weeks, the Falcons may be able to address other non-quarterback needs in the first round. If they can, Jake Matthews’ replacement could be sitting in Iowa. There isn’t anything Lauck does that will jump off the page, but he is a very good tackle who doesn’t allow pressures and blocks well in the running game. Nyck Harbor, WR, South Carolina vs. Alabama Bryant-Denny Stadium – Tuscaloosa, AL 7 pm EST – ESPN Nyck Harbor is 6’6, 243lbs and the FASTEST player in the country He’s also improved incrementally in each of his three years at South Carolina, and finished 2025 with 4 TDs and 340 yards in the final four games. He still has a long way to go, but he’s on a better trajectory… pic.twitter.com/qGqUH0Eq9q — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) August 12, 2026 With LaNorris Sellers’ struggles, the sun is starting to set on the Nyck Harbor agenda. However, I’m not ready to give up on it just yet. At 6’6”, 243 pounds, and world-class speed, Harbor has a chance, in primetime, to make a big impact on a massive stage. With guys like Zabien Brown and Bray Hubbard in Alabama’s secondary, South Carolina has to get a spark from somewhere if they want to pull off the upset. Why shouldn’t that spark come from Harbor? Justin Bowick, WR, Oklahoma State vs. West Virginia Milan Puskar Stadium – Morgantown, WV 7 pm EST – FS1 Oklahoma State WR Justin Bowick yesterday 🤠 9 REC 🤠 178 YDS 🤠 2 TD Oklahoma State defeats Murray State 59-0 pic.twitter.com/eNpeNN7qYG — Rafters (@RaftersHQ) September 20, 2026 One of the better stories in college football is the resurgence of Oklahoma State under quarterback Drew Mestemaker. His favorite target thus far? Wide receiver Justin Bowick. At 6’5” and 209 pounds, Bowick’s vertical ability, plus his knack for finding yards after the catch, Bowick could have a huge impact on their game against the West Virginia Mountaineers. Ty Benefield, S, LSU vs. Texas A&M Tiger Stadium – Baton Rouge, LA 7:30 pm EST – ABC LSU S Ty Benefield’s forceful pressure is the tale of the Trinidad Chambliss INT The Boise State transfer has Day 2 NFL Draft potential pic.twitter.com/q1VOCtJekH — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) September 20, 2026 If the Falcons end up addressing safety in the draft, one of the guys they should really target is LSU safety Ty Benefield. According to PFF, Benefield is allowing a 39.6 passer rating when targeted so far this season. Insert the fact that he’s been all over the defense (43 box safety snaps, 87 free safety snaps, 25 slot cornerback snaps), and Benefield has the opportunity to add real versatility to an NFL secondary next season. He’s also 6’3” and 215 pounds, some length and mass that would be much-needed in the Falcons’ secondary. Bear Alexander, DT, Oregon vs. USC Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum – Los Angeles,…

title: 3 Keys to Victory for Ravens-Cowboys Week 3
summary: The honeymoon period ended last week for Jesse Minter and the staff in Baltimore. A fourth-quarter collapse for the first loss of the season was all too close to losses of seasons past that the organization was hoping to leave behind. Now the Ravens travel to Brazil for a high-octane matchup against the Dallas Cowboys […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Devontez Walker #81 of the Baltimore Ravens completes a catch against Martin Emerson Jr at M&T Bank Stadium. #22 of the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The honeymoon period ended last week for Jesse Minter and the staff in Baltimore. A fourth-quarter collapse for the first loss of the season was all too close to losses of seasons past that the organization was hoping to leave behind. Now the Ravens travel to Brazil for a high-octane matchup against the Dallas Cowboys as the NFL plays in Rio de Janeiro for the first time. The Ravens hope to travel back to Baltimore 2-1 with the first NFL win in Rio. Here are some keys to the game. Utilize your weapons In Week 2, while missing Zay Flowers, over half of the Ravens’ plays went to Rashod Bateman, Mark Andrews, and Derrick Henry. It’s not a terrible formula. Bateman finished with 88 yards and a touchdown, Andrews was a clean safety valve and finished with 49 yards, and Henry ran for 4.3 yards per carry. The only issue is it didn’t end with a win, and the offense stalled. They only had eight total drives, including the last drive searching for a miracle with no timeouts. Against the Cowboys, those players are going to have to be relied on again, specifically speaking about Bateman and Henry. Those are the two best weapons right now. But the Ravens have to spread the ball more. Devontez Walker had the biggest play of the day against the Saints with a long 47-yard bomb. He wasn’t targeted again. Rookie tight end Matt Hibner has been talked up a lot this offseason and showed explosiveness during the preseason that the veteran tight ends don’t have. LaJohntay Wester is electric with the ball in his hands and could stress a defense when in motion if given the chance. The Cowboys are likely to key in heavily on Henry and give Bateman their best cover guy and some extra shading. The Ravens need to have other answers ready. Pressure Dak Prescott The Cowboys offense is a high-flying unit starring one of the best wide receiver duos in the NFL with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Captained by Dak Prescott, it’s expected to be one of the best offenses in the NFL this year, and they looked like it against the Washington Commanders last week. Prescott 26/31 for 279 yards and four touchdowns, with 179 of those yards and all four of the touchdowns coming when he was kept clean. Pressure didn’t really knock Prescott off his game against the Commanders, but he wasn’t as good. Against the New York Giants in Week 1, however, Prescott went 0/8 when pressured nine times during the game. Historically, that’s been the key to containing Prescott. The Cowboys are missing their best offensive lineman, left guard Tyler Smith, and the weakest point on the line has been right tackle Terence Steele, according to PFF. Just like the Saints game, the Ravens can expect Trey Hendrickson to receive extra attention while he lines up over the left tackle. That’s going to put the onus on whoever lines up opposite Hendrickson, Mike Green or Tavius Robinson, both of whom had a sack last week. The other aspect will be interior pressure. The Ravens are expecting to get Nnamdi Madubuike back for this one. He’ll be on a pitch count, and I imagine most of his pitches will be pass rush attempts. It’s the defensive line we dreamed of this summer: Trey Hendrickson, Nnamdi Madubuike, Travis Jones, and Mike Green getting home by just rushing four. Be on the lookout for Aeneas Peebles rushing the passer too, next to Madubuike. He’s been winning his rushes at a high clip this year so far. The Ravens secondary simply won’t be able to hold up against Lamb and Pickens for extended periods time and time again. The Ravens pass rush knocking Prescott off his spot and giving him problems all day will be imperative to the defense having success. Run Henry I know I just said before to spread the ball around and utilize the weapons on this team and that is true. But we can’t ignore how bad the Cowboys’ run defense has been this year. They are currently in the bottom three in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game. And now Derrick Henry is coming down the track. Henry wrecked this team in 2024, and the Cowboys are going to be desperate to not let that repeat and fix their poor run defense this season. They are going to load the box, key in on Henry, and do everything in their power to ensure that he is not the reason they lose. The Ravens can’t fall into that trap. Henry could start slow, maybe only getting two or three yards a carry. He might even finish the game this way. He shouldn’t finish this game with fewer than 20 carries. The Ravens have to keep the Cowboys honest and keep plunging Henry throughout the game. It should hopefully make space for Lamar Jackson to run; the Cowboys have given up a ton of quarterback rushing yards, and give the passing game space to operate while the Cowboys load the box on them.

title: Ravens Week 3 injury report: all eyes on Zay Flowers vs. Cowboys
summary: The Baltimore Ravens confirmed that defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan would make their long-awaited 2026 debuts on Sunday in Brazil. Both were taken off the team’s final injury report for their Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Wide receiver Zay Flowers, however, is listed as questionable with a lingering hamstring injury […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on prior to the game against the New Orleans Saints at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens confirmed that defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan would make their long-awaited 2026 debuts on Sunday in Brazil. Both were taken off the team’s final injury report for their Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Wide receiver Zay Flowers, however, is listed as questionable with a lingering hamstring injury that held him out of practice for most of the week. He only participated in a limited capacity on Friday, as he did last week before missing the loss to the New Orleans Saints. We held a walkthrough on Friday, the report is a practice estimation. pic.twitter.com/xPltqxJBK9 — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) September 25, 2026 Questionable field conditions at Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro further complicated Flowers’ potential to play. His hamstring been bothering him for about a month now; will the Ravens want to risk aggravating the injury knowing there are concerns about the playing surface? As a result, Flowers appears to be a true game-time decision on Sunday afternoon. He will likely go through a pre-game warm-up on the field and, in concert with the Ravens’ medical team, evaluate his ability to play. His absence would deprive Baltimore of their best receiving threat, but injuries in the Cowboys’ secondary could mitigate the loss. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley was unsurprisingly ruled out after missing practice all week. He will be replaced by 2025 fifth-round pick Carson Vinson, who will make his first career NFL start. That will leave the Ravens without a clear swing tackle; 2024 third-round pick Emery Jones played right tackle at LSU and could step into that role on Sunday.

He joined the team as an undrafted free agent out of Miami (FL) following the 2024 NFL Draft. He has never appeared in a regular season game for the Bills, but he has been with the team’s practice squad for each of the last two seasons. In seven preseason games with Buffalo, Couch has 19 tackles, one sack, four pass breakups, and an interception. The Bills made a roster move on Friday, as well, placing defensive back Jordan Hancock on injured reserve thanks to a hamstring injury. Hancock is mainly used on special teams, but he also plays both slot corner and safety. Couch is similarly versatile, so he could directly replace Hancock on the gameday roster on special teams and as a reserve. The Bills also have rookie safety Jalen Kilgore on the 53-man roster; Kilgore has been a healthy scratch for each of the first two games this season. As a member of the Hurricanes, Couch started 32 games, totaling 156 tackles and four interceptions in his NCAA career.

title: 5 Los Angeles Chargers to watch at the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers take on the Buffalo Bills this week, and both teams appear to be on totally different trajectories in the early going of the 2026 NFL season. The Chargers are 0-2 and struggling mightily on offense. The Bills are 2-0 and are absolutely cruising on offense. Will those trends continue, or will […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Chargers take on the Buffalo Bills this week, and both teams appear to be on totally different trajectories in the early going of the 2026 NFL season. The Chargers are 0-2 and struggling mightily on offense. The Bills are 2-0 and are absolutely cruising on offense. Will those trends continue, or will each team creep closer to the mathematical mean? One impedement for the Chargers this weekend is health, as Los Angeles is dealing with a slew of injuries at key positions. They are without six players this weekend—and that’s not counting players like tight end David Njoku, who is already on injured reserve. With a gauntlet of a schedule upcoming, and including, this week, Los Angeles knows just how much it needs a win. How can the Bills prevent a desperate team from stealing a win in their house? They can start by taking advantage of some of those backups while limiting the Chargers’ key players. Here are five Chargers to watch in Sunday’s game. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Justin Herbert The Chargers’ quarterback has not taken the steps forward most fans and pundits expected. Although it’s a small sample size, Herbert is completing just 59% of his passes through two games; he has two touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he’s already taken six sacks. With a new offensive coordinator, Mike McDaniel, calling the plays, we could point to the growing pains of a new offensive system, but poor protection from an injury-ravaged offensive line also likely has something to do with it. If Buffalo can continue to generate pressure with just four rushers, it’s going to be a long day for Herbert and the Bolts. McDaniel would be wise to call some quick-hitters early and often, forcing Buffalo’s underperforming secondary to make tackles early and often. Using motion to create miscommunication could help, as well, since we’ve seen plenty of communication breakdowns on the back end for the Bills. However, if Herbert is under duress and Buffalo can continue to limit the run like they have through two weeks, it’ll be a good Sunday for Buffalo. WR Ladd McConkey Keon Coleman’s 2024 NFL Draft mate was the apple of some fans’ eyes, and while he’s had some success, he’s also dealt with his share of disappointment. After an excellent rookie season (82/1,149/7 on 112 targets), McConkey struggled last season as dealt with a number of nagging injuries. While he saw nearly the same number of targets (106), he caught just 66 passes for 789 yards and six scores. So far, McConkey is LA’s leading receiver, as he’s caught eight passes for 117 yards and a score. He’s a shifty route-runner who can cause matchup problems from multiple alignments, and while Buffalo has had top corner Christian Benford traveling with opposing No. 1 wideouts this season, that strategy hasn’t come with a great deal of success so far. The trouble for Buffalo is that slot corner Dee Alford has also been hit-or-miss, and more miss than hit, so containing McConkey could become difficult if the Chargers find a matchup they like. I’d like to see Maxwell Hairston on him this week, as the second-year man’s speed and athletic profile give him an edge over the Bills’ other options. Benford could then deal with the more physical Quentin Johnson on the outside. However the Bills choose to defend McConkey, they’ll need to take him away, as he’s really Herbert’s best receiving option. The Interior Offensive Line Tyler Biadasz is on injured reserve. Trey Pipkins III and Kayode Awosika are out. The Chargers’ interior line has been decimated by injury thus far, which likely will limit now only their ability to protect Herbert, but their ability to open holes in the running game for Omarion Hampton. Buffalo’s defensive line has been sharp this year, and while Greg Rousseau and Bradleey Chubb have combined for 5.5 sacks so far, arguably the most impressive player up front has been nose tackle Deone Walker. If Ed Oliver is able to suit up, it will make it that much more difficult to handle Walker, who has quickly ascended to one of the best interior defensive linemen in football. The game is won in the trenches, and on paper, the Bills have a huge advantage in the middle of the line. They need to exploit it. LB Del’Shawn Phillips Phillips is a real success story, as he has taken the long way to a role as a starter. After signing with the Atlanta Falcons as a rookie free agent following the 2019 NFL Draft, Phillips was waived and joined Buffalo’s practice squad. He did not appear in a game for the Bills that year, but he signed a reserve/futures deal and remained with the club the following season. After failing to make the 53-man roster, Phillips signed with Buffalo’s practice squad. He made his NFL debut on special teams for Buffalo, as he was elevated twice during the 2020 season. He did not register a tackle, but he showed enough to warrant further looks around the league. After stops with the New York Jets in 2021, the Baltimore Ravens in 2022 and 2023, and the Houston Texans in 2024, he seems to have found a home in Los Angeles. He was named Second-Team All-Pro as a special teams player last season, notching a league-leading 24 tackles in the third phase of the game. This season, he has 13 total tackles and he has started both of the Chargers’ games. Not bad for a guy who entered the league as a UDFA way back when. It’s always cool to see a player stick with it and earn the opportunity he’s longed for since he was young, and whether it’s with the Bills or not, I love to see a former Buffalo player overcome those long odds. NCB Tarheeb Still Buffalo should be able to find quality matchups against a Chargers’ secondary ranked No. 28 against the pass so far this season, but given some of the injury issues Buffalo’s receiving corps is dealing with at present, this matchup might be a big one. Safety Derwin James is likely to deal with tight end Dalton Kincaid, so I assume that Stll will see a healthy dose of Khalil Shakir this weekend. Shakir is one of quarterback Josh Allen’s favorite targets, and he’s put together a solid, if unspectacular, start to the season by catching seven passes for 88 yards on twelve targets. If DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) both play, it’s safe to assume they’ll be a bit limited by their injuries. If either of them sit, it will be that much more imperative to keep Shakir contained. As it stands, I like this matchup for Buffalo whether the Bills’ top outside options play or not.
author: Sean Murphy

title: Buffalo Bills tailgate: Pancho’s Army brings the party and a purpose to the Mafia House
summary: There are plenty of reasons Bills fans start showing up in Orchard Park hours before kickoff. The food. The drinks. The music. Seeing old friends. Making new ones. And, depending on where you wander, perhaps watching someone get covered in ketchup and mustard. But some Bills Mafia traditions have grown into something much bigger than […]
full_text: There are plenty of reasons Bills fans start showing up in Orchard Park hours before kickoff. The food. The drinks. The music. Seeing old friends. Making new ones. And, depending on where you wander, perhaps watching someone get covered in ketchup and mustard. But some Bills Mafia traditions have grown into something much bigger than football. For the third stop in our Buffalo Rumblings Tailgate Series, we’re heading to the Mafia House to visit Pancho’s Army, where the tailgate comes with a pretty simple philosophy: Come ready to have a good time. And, if you can, help them do some good along the way. Welcome back to the Buffalo Rumblings Tailgate Series Throughout the 2026 season, we’re highlighting the different tailgate experiences available to Bills fans around Highmark Stadium. That’s especially important for the thousands of fans who travel to Buffalo from across the country and around the world. Not everyone can throw a grill, tent, table and several coolers into the back of a truck before heading to Orchard Park. Sometimes you just need to know where you can go. Our first stop was the Bills VIP Tailgate, a ticketed, all-inclusive experience where virtually everything is taken care of for you. Next came the Red Pinto Tailgate at Hammer’s Lot , one of the most recognizable grassroots tailgates in Bills Mafia, complete with Pizza Pete, bowling-ball shots, the ketchup-and-mustard ceremony with Pinto Ron, and decades of Bills tailgating history. Our third stop offers something different again. Pancho’s Army at the Mafia House Located at 60 Fay Street in Orchard Park, the Mafia House has become home base for Pancho’s Army on Bills game days. Pancho’s Army has a new setup this season, moving the tailgate out back into its own dedicated tent area. There’s no ticket to purchase and no admission charge. Everything served at the tailgate is donated. The only ask? If you’re able, make a donation to Pancho’s Army. That’s it. Meet some fellow Bills fans, enjoy the pregame atmosphere and contribute what you can. For traveling fans in particular, it’s exactly the kind of tailgate this series was created to highlight. You don’t need your own grill or an elaborate game-day setup. You don’t need to purchase an expensive hospitality package. You can simply show up and become part of it. But who was Pancho Billa? For newer Bills fans, there’s an important story behind the name. Ezra Castro, better known throughout Bills Mafia as Pancho Billa, became one of the most recognizable Buffalo Bills fans. The Texas native was unmistakable on game day, appearing in his signature sombrero and lucha libre mask while passionately supporting a team located more than a thousand miles from home. But Pancho became much more than a recognizable Bills superfan. His battle with cancer became known throughout Bills Mafia, and the fan base rallied around him. His relationship with the Bills organization grew as well, including one particularly memorable moment when Pancho was given the opportunity to announce Buffalo’s third-round selection of Harrison Phillips during the 2018 NFL Draft. Pancho died in 2019 at just 39 years old. His impact didn’t end there. The community that grew around him continued carrying his name and, more importantly, the spirit behind it. That’s where Pancho’s Army comes in. Carrying the legacy forward Pancho’s Army has helped turn the memory of one beloved Bills fan into opportunities to help others. And that’s what makes this tailgate different from the first two we’ve visited. It’s still a Bills tailgate. But the gathering also provides an opportunity for Bills Mafia to contribute to the charitable work Pancho’s Army continues throughout the year. There isn’t a required donation at the door or a minimum amount attached to your arrival. Give what you can. And if you can’t give much? You’re still welcome. That’s a pretty good representation of Bills Mafia at its best. The party doesn’t stop with kickoff The donations and support Pancho’s Army receives aren’t simply about putting on another Sunday tailgate. Their work continues throughout the season, and Bills fans will have a couple of additional opportunities to help. Beginning at the end of October and continuing through mid-November, Pancho’s Army will hold an ongoing Winter Coat Drive. Then, from late November through mid-December, the focus shifts to the holidays with a Toy Drive benefiting Ronald McDonald House. That means if you’re planning a trip to Orchard Park later this season, you may want to leave a little extra room in the suitcase or car. Bring your Bills gear…and depending on when you’re visiting, maybe bring a coat or a toy to donate too. Why this one belongs on the tailgating fan’s list I’ve attended 103 consecutive Buffalo Bills games, home and away, and one of my favorite things about this fan base is how quickly strangers stop feeling like strangers. You see the same faces in different cities. Someone recognizes your Bills gear at an airport. You walk into a tailgate knowing three people and somehow leave knowing 30. That same feeling exists here. Bills fans travel incredible distances to get to Buffalo. Some are making their annual trip. Others are walking into a Bills home game for the first time. If you’re one of them, walking into an established tailgate can occasionally feel intimidating. Don’t let it. At Pancho’s Army, the whole point is community. So walk around back to the tent and introduce yourself to the guy in a sombrero and an army surplus jacket “El Presidente”, Anthony, Panchos Army’s president. Then ask someone how they became a Bills fan. You’ll probably have a story in return before you know it. Because one of the things I’ve learned over those 103 games is that you’re rarely truly on your own when you’re among Bills Mafia.
author: Sara Larson

title: Dalton Kincaid is not transforming into a receiver, Buffalo Bills using him like a genuine tight end
summary: To many, Dalton Kincaid is receiver-tight end hybrid, and Joe Brady is making a statement about his true position early on in the 2026 season. Max Toscano, who specializes in tight end evaluations, recently posted an amazing thread on Twitter/X regarding Buffalo’s specific utilization of Kincaid (and other receiving specialists at tight end) to begin […]
full_text: To many, Dalton Kincaid is receiver-tight end hybrid, and Joe Brady is making a statement about his true position early on in the 2026 season. Max Toscano, who specializes in tight end evaluations, recently posted an amazing thread on Twitter/X regarding Buffalo’s specific utilization of Kincaid (and other receiving specialists at tight end) to begin the 2026 season. It’s highly recommended reading. Before the season, I wrote an exploration of the chances Buffalo’s offense becomes tight-end centric this season. Through two games, it undoubtedly has been . Sprinkled throughout the original article were hints about Kincaid’s positional label actually being closer to receiver than tight end. I concluded that piece with this paragraph: “And, heck, if internally the Bills don’t view him as a tight end, maybe simply a sizable jump in workload for Kincaid this season will actually make Buffalo believe its one of the more “receiver-heavy” offenses in the NFL.” In his first three seasons, Kincaid never hit 27% of his snaps in-line (attached to the line of scrimmage, a classic tight end pre-snap alignment), and in 2025, he was positioned out wide at nearly the same percentage as he was in-line (22.1% vs. 23.5%). So, yeah, he kinda-sorta felt like a receiver. Through two games in the Joe Brady era, the Bills have made it clear — Kincaid is a tight end. His in-line snap percentage has sky-rocketed to 50.9% while his out wide percentage has plummeted to 12.3%. He’s been in the slot on only 35.1% of his snaps thus far, easily the lowest of his professional career. In each of Kincaid’s first three seasons in Buffalo, his slot percentage was over 52.0%. How about this too — Kincaid was never asked to pass block on more than 2.2% of his snaps in any of his first three years as a member of the Bills. In the first two games, he’s stayed in to pass block 8.8% of the time. Kincaid is producing like a receiver. But he’s being deployed a lot more like a classic tight end, which has made it nearly impossible to opposing defenses to decipher whether a run or pass is coming from the Bills through two games this season.

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. Los Angeles Chargers
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Chargers are set to square off this weekend in a matchup of old AFL foes on totally different paths in 2026. The Bills are riding an offensive hot streak so far, sprinting out to a 2-0 start thanks in part to an NFL-leading 38.5 points per game. The Chargers, […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Chargers are set to square off this weekend in a matchup of old AFL foes on totally different paths in 2026. The Bills are riding an offensive hot streak so far, sprinting out to a 2-0 start thanks in part to an NFL-leading 38.5 points per game. The Chargers, meanwhile, have struggled to find rhythm on offense, dropping both of their games so far by the same score, 26-14. With the New England Patriots coming to town next week, this week’s matchup has all the makings of the quintessential trap game. The Chargers desperately need to avoid an 0-3 start, while the Bills will be plenty motivated to stay on top of what should be a very competitive AFC playoff picture as the fall turns to winter. This week’s edition of “five players to watch” has us taking some liberties. We really have four players and an entire chunk of the defense to discuss this week, and while those may be the ones we’ve chosen, they aren’t the only keys to victory for the Bills this week. Without further ado, here are five Bills—and then some—to watch this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR Khalil Shakir DJ Moore showed out in his Week One debut with the team. Keon Coleman picked up the slack in Week Two when Moore went down with an injury. Given that both Moore (shoulder) and Coleman (ankle) are dealing with injuries this week, there is some level of uncertainty as to what Buffalo’s receiver group will look like on Sunday. Moore has already said that he’ll play, as he termed his injury a matter of pain tolerance, but Coleman has yet to practice this week. If we assume that Moore will suit up, albeit in a limited capacity, and Coleman will sit, that means that Buffalo will need No. 10 to step up. Shakir has put together two modest games, combining for seven catches and 88 yards on 12 targets. All of those numbers trail tight end Dalton Kincaid, and he’s behind Kincaid and Moore in receiving yards. If there were ever a day to wager that Shakir will see an uptick in targets, this is the one, as Los Angeles enters play ranked No. 28 in passing defense with a nickel corner in Tarheeb Still that can be beaten by strong slot play. WR Joshua Palmer Speaking of wideouts who might see more targets this week, the former Charger could be in line for some more work if Moore is limited and Coleman is out. Palmer has made the most of his five targets this season, catching two long touchdown passes—a 34-yard strike to win the game against the Houston Texans and a 43-yard hookup to give the Bills a two-score lead against the Detroit Lions. While Palmer has been boom-or-bust, he’s only played 35% of the team’s offensive snaps this year. I’d expect a slight increase this week, and the Bills might look to extend his season-opening touchdown streak given that he’s playing against his old team. DL DeWayne Carter Whether Ed Oliver plays or not, I’m interested in seeing whether Carter can continue his solid level of play. Admittedly, I thought he was going to be a late-summer cut after a poor first season and a second year spent on injured reserve thanks to an Achilles tear; however, Carter has come in and proven to be a valuable part of the defensive line rotation so far. Sure, he’s only made three tackles on 49 defensive snaps, but at his position, it’s about doing the dirty work to ensure that the players at the next level of the defense have room to make plays. Buffalo’s run defense looks to be much improved this season in the early going, and Carter has contributed positively to that improvement. Hopefully, he can rotate in with Oliver this weekend, but if Ed can’t go, Carter has proven that he can pick up the slack. CB Christian Benford Yes, I’m looking at him again. It hasn’t been a great start for Buffalo’s top corner, which is something that we said last season, as well. Does it just take Benford some time to settle into a new year? Or, is the switch to Jim Leonhard’s defensive scheme forcing Benford to play in a way that isn’t his strength? The Chargers’ offense has struggled mightily, but they have some talented receivers, including Quentin Johnson and Ladd McConkey. McConkey, in particular, is someone who could give Benford trouble, as he can line up in the slot or outside, and he relies more on his twitchy route-running and quickness than he does straight-line speed. I’m interested to see how Buffalo defends the pass this week, and I’m looking for big improvements after a mini-bye to self-scout. Part of that improvement involves Benford playing up to his standard. Coverage and Communication Okay, maybe this is a bit of a cop-out, but I really want to see improvement from the entire back-end of the Buffalo defense in both coverage and communication. Truthfully, I think that most of the problems with the latter are a result of the former, and with time, these are issues that will resolve as the players gain more familiarity in the new scheme. As much as the Chargers have struggled on offense, they have talented personnel. Justin Herbert is a good NFL quarterback. Omarion Hampton is a solid NFL running back. We’ve already mentioned some of the talent at receiver, as well. Injury issues on the offensive line should allow Buffalo’s pass rush to thrive, which is something that the team has already experienced this year; if the rush and coverage can finally start to marry, then Buffalo’s defense could take a giant leap forward. I don’t expect perfection, but I’d like to see fewer coverage breakdowns this week. Make the Chargers’ pass-catchers win as a result of winning the physical matchup rather than giving them free space as a result of mental mistakes. One of Buffalo’s defensive backs needs to make a play on the ball, and my proverbial money is on second-year man Maxwell Hairston pulling in the team’s first interception of 2026 this week.

full_text: Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were expected to be among the dangerous teams to watch in the AFC, but so far, through two weeks, Herbert and the offense have been massive disappointments, and the Chargers find themselves 0-2 after surprising losses against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders. title: Bills vs. Chargers predictions: Buffalo’s offense may dominate in Week 3
summary: The Buffalo Bills are on a heater right now, with quarterback Josh Allen playing incredible football at a clip that has him as the current odds-on favorite to win NFL MVP honors for the 2026 NFL season. Now 2-0 and with impressive offensive showings against both the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions, the Bills are […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the football during the second half of the NFL game against the Detroit Lions at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are on a heater right now, with quarterback Josh Allen playing incredible football at a clip that has him as the current odds-on favorite to win NFL MVP honors for the 2026 NFL season. Now 2-0 and with impressive offensive showings against both the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions, the Bills are set to welcome the woebegone Los Angeles Chargers to cozy Highmark Stadium. Things could get out of hand quickly if recent game history is an indication. Will Buffalo’s offense continue its dominant ways in Week 3? It’s trending that way, especially if Allen, running back James Cook III, and tight end Dalton Kincaid continue playing elite football. Many consider this a trap game for the Bills given the situation. However, Buffalo is a much better team than either the Arizona Cardinals or Las Vegas Raiders, which both defeated the Chargers by identical 26-14 scores. That said, Buffalo has its own less-than-ideal identical pair from its first two wins: the defense gave up 31 points in each matchup. Will current trends prevail or is Buffalo headed for a trap? Below, we dive into a few bold predictions for Bills vs. Chargers in Week 3 using data and odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook . Josh Allen features early and often Week 3 Through two games, Josh Allen has nine total touchdowns, which includes five passing scores. He’s off to a land-speed-record pace this season, but is it sustainable? It should be at least through Week 3 thanks to a reeling Chargers team. Los Angeles has given up a combined 46-of-66 for 530 yards with four touchdowns and one interception to quarterbacks Jacoby Brissett and Kurt Cousins. I like Allen to surpass that two-game average of 265 yards and two passing touchdowns, perhaps even besting the 23-of-33 pass/attempts average. As of publishing, FanDuel Sportsbook lists Allen’s passing yards total at over 238.5 (-115)/under 238.5 (-115). That over feels like a given this week. Yes, simply picking Allen to surpass what are essentially two-game average marks against LAC isn’t a bold prediction. Instead, I like the odds of Allen throwing for north of 300 yards (+350 at FanDuel), with at least three passing touchdowns (+250 at FanDuel) and at no less than one rushing score (anytime -140 | +450 to score 2+ at FanDuel). I also think Allen will again claim the game’s first score (not a passing TD) as a rusher with a tone-setting touchdown (+550 at FanDuel). Despite the potential for wide receivers DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to both sit out Week 3, there will be plenty of touchdown options, all of whom Allen is well-versed with at wide receiver, tight end, and running back. that includes the expected return of dynamic dual-threat running back Ty Johnson, who’s proven to be a third-down specialist as a receiver. If Buffalo wins the coin toss, look for them to take the ball on offense again — perhaps a nod to the ‘90s Super Bowl Bills teams that sought to bury opponents with an early lead. Head coach Joe Brady has decided to let Josh cook early this season, and it’s worked with aplomb. Expect to see Allen featured early and often in Week 3. Dalton Kincaid dominates in Week 3 You might not see this as a bold prediction, especially if Moore and Coleman are sidelined, however Buffalo does have numerous, sometimes overlooked, options to play a featured role as receiver. Week 1, Dalton Kincaid was second on the team in targets (6), co-led the team in catches (5), and led all pass catchers in yards with 130 through the air. Kincaid followed that up with a Week 2 performance featuring seven catches on eight targets for 95 yards — all three serving as team leads — plus his first touchdown of the 2026 season. In Week 3, Kincaid should feast again as a receiver. Kincaid has the fifth-best odds as a touchdown scorer (non-passing), with anytime odds of +185 at FanDuel. Concerning receiving yards, Kincaid’s O/U with FanDuel sits at O 56.6 (-114)/U 56.5 (-114). It would be far more shocking to seem him flirt with that under. I’d roll with the odds that Kincaid surpasses 100 yards in Week 3 (+470 at FanDuel) and 7+ receptions (+400 at FanDuel). As a deep threat, Kincaid has been a serious problem for defenses of late. In fact, as of publishing, Kincaid has the best odds through FanDuel of hauling in a 15+ yard reception (-550), a 20+ yard reception (-210), and a 30+ yard reception (+190). So far this season, when you think of Kincaid, you envision long receptions downfield no matter who’s covering him. James Cook 1st RB to humble LAC in 2026 There’s been a lot of forgettable football out of the Chargers through two losses, but their rushing defense has been fairly stout. Games against the Raiders’ Ashton Jeanty (21 carries, 48 yards; 4 catches, 15 yards) and Cardinals RB1A Tyler Allgeier (17 carries, 61 yards; 2 catches, 9 yards) and rookie RB1B Jeremiyah Love (11 carries, 41 yards, 1 TD; 2 catches 9 yards) prove that Los Angeles’ front seven is serious about stopping the run. That’s good defense against very capable backs, however, James Cook is on a different level as the reigning NFL rushing champ. Still a somewhat overlooked player in the league, Cook has had a decent start to his 2026 season. I expect him to get plenty of touches in Week 3, which should lead to a bunch of yards and a score or two as one of the most dynamic dual-threats in today’s game. Cook is a featured back, but someone who has seen his workload reduced simply due to the team’s third-down preference to roll with Ty Johnson. As mentioned earlier, Johnson should be back this weekend. Will that eat into Cook’s snap count and, ultimately, his touches? I see a lot of that depending on how diverse a game plan the offense deploys for Cook against LA. Cook seems primed for an explosion of offense on Sunday, perhaps totaling a new season high in carries. Interestingly, Cook has the current best odds with FanDuel of scoring 2+ touchdowns (+310), which sounds like others also believe he’s going to be a big part of Sunday’s game. To that end, Cook also has the most favorable odds of scoring a touchdown at any point in the first half (+135 at FanDuel) and also the second half (+160 at FanDuel). Like many of his teammates, it’s true that Cook could head to the sideline early if Buffalo builds a huge lead in the second half. I’m still willing to bet that he gets a lot of run on Sunday, in an effort to really test how good the Chargers are at stopping the ground game. Remember, Cook is always one cut away from a house call, which means he gets top billing as the favorite to finish with the most rushing yards (-185 at FanDuel). Is it too bold to say that Cook should flirt with 90+ rushing yards (+132 at FanDuel) against the Chargers? Again, one carry always has the potential to get Cook better than halfway there. Fair warning: As of publishing, Cook sits at O/U 79.4 total rushing yards (-114). Los Angeles’ run defense is not to be so easily dismissed. Pointing back to the RB receiving stats above, the Chargers are also equally adept at keeping backs in check as a pass-catching threat. Currently through FanDuel, as a receiver Cook is O 1.5 (-154)/U 1.5 (+116) for receptions and O/U 10.5 (-114) for receiving yards. Do you like the odds that one screen pass goes the distance? Maybe you also like the odds that Cook accumulates 50+ receiving yards (+1280 at FanDuel). The trick on Sunday comes if Brady and Allen find a better path toward utilizing Cook as a receiver. All told, I say Cook bests FanDuel’s current projection for his combined rushing and receiving yards at O/U 94.5 (-114). Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now to put it to…

title: If Buffalo Bills want to explore a Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, they should have the inside scoop on him
summary: Are the Buffalo Bills going to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.? Heck, none of us know if the Cardinals are even going to be willing to trade him, and at this juncture, we certainly have been given no indication by the Bills — or any NFL insiders — that a trade is being explored. Speaking […]
full_text: Are the Buffalo Bills going to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.? Heck, none of us know if the Cardinals are even going to be willing to trade him, and at this juncture, we certainly have been given no indication by the Bills — or any NFL insiders — that a trade is being explored. Speaking of exploring, if you’re even mildly intrigued by this idea — or totally despise the thought of it — I highly encourage you to read Matt Byham’s thorough breakdown of the pros and cons of it all . As Harrison Jr. trade speculation percolates, and it feels like it will, as any of it pertains to the Bills, it’ll be critical to remember the Bills should already have plenty of intel this young wideout. Why? Buffalo’s new receivers coach, Drew Terrell, was the pass game coordinator and receivers coach in Arizona the past three seasons, two of which of course correspond with the beginning of Harrison Jr.‘s NFL career with the Cardinals. A former receiver himself, who’s only 35 years old, Terrell started in the NFL in 2018 with the Panthers as a quality control coach and spent 2020-2022 with the Commanders as an assistant receivers coach and the regular wide receiver coach in the 2021 and 2022 campaigns. Of course, Harrison Jr. hasn’t appeared on special teams, but the Bills’ special teams coach Jeff Rodgers was in Arizona from 2019-2025 coaching special teams and with the title of assistant head coach, so he’d clearly know Harrison Jr. reasonably well too. And we have no idea what Terrell and Rodgers think of Harrison Jr., but their close knowledge of the young wideout may either be what spurs the Bills into action on the trade front or provides the inside info to the front office that keeps the Bills away.

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Defensive Coordinator Dennis Allen of the Chicago Bears looks on during the third quarter of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears suffered a tough loss last week in sloppy, wet conditions at Soldier Field, and the weather certainly slowed their high-powered offense. But Brian Flores’ blitz-happy Minnesota Vikings’ defense gave Chicago’s offense fits too. The Bears had their chances, and knowing the makeup of this team and head coach Ben Johnson, they’ll learn from the 9 to 3 loss. That loss, coupled with the Caleb Williams injury, dropped our confidence poll by 20 points this week, down to 74%. The Bears face another top-tier defensive coordinator this week, but the Philadelphia Eagles’ Vic Fangio is blitzing only 24.2% of the time. When compared to Flores’ 75.9%, this will feel like a drastic difference. Fangio’s creativity isn’t always up front and will show more on the back end, as he’ll most often show a two-high safety look, then rotate to disguise coverages. The weather on Monday night in Chicago will be mild, but this defensive matchup is another tough one for Ben Johnson. With the Bears likely starting Case Keenum at quarterback ( although Tyson Bagent is questionable ), the spread from our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook is currently Bears +3.5, with the over/under at 42.5. Chicago’s offense will need to bounce back after a rough outing last week, and they’ll have to do with Johnson calling plays for a back up quarterback for the first time ever. While in Detroit, his QB was always Jared Goff, and this is the first game Williams will be out. Chicago’s defense made some strides last week, and we’ll see if that was due to the weather and Carson Wentz’s quarterbacking, or if that was due to some scheme specific and improved defensive coordinating from Dennis Allen. My guess is a litle bit of both. On Monday night, Allen’s defense has a tough chalenge ahead of them. They’ll face one of he best running backs in the game, three time Pro Bowler Saquon Barkley, and Philly has a three time Pro Bowler at quarterback in dual hreat Jalen Hurts. This last Reacts’ result didn’t come from Bears fans, it was a poll on SB Nation’s Feed section, so it was presented to a national audience. What does Caleb Williams getting 39% of the vote here mean to you?

full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears drops back to pass during the first half of Week 3 preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears and the Philadelphia Eagles meet up on Monday Night Football, and each team has revealed its final injury report for the game. As expected, the Bears will be without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, but the door is open for Tyson Bagent. Bagent entered concussion protocol earlier this week, but today he advanced enough to be able to get on the field and practice in a limited capacity. He’s officially listed as questionable, and if he’s cleared, he could dress on Monday night. Case Keenum still seems likely to get the start, but the Bears have a walk-through tomorrow, and all day Monday, so there’s time. Linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles) and defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee) are listed as out, which rounds out Chicago’s injury report. Sewell and Turner were limited all week and are in their 21-day practice window recovering from the PUP list, so before they can play, they’d need to be activated. Kicker Cairo Santos missed practice on Thursday and Friday with a hip injury, but was back today and has no injury designation. Also free of a designation is cornerback Tyroque Stevenson, who missed some time earlier this week with a hamstring issue. As for Ozzy Trapilo, who has practiced in full for a second consecutive week, head coach Ben Johnson was asked if he’d be an option to start at left tackle on Monday night, and he said, “No.” We’ll know 90 minutes before kickoff if he’s active, and being active in a game or two for some game reps would be a precursor to him taking over as the starter. The Eagles will be without starting tight end Dallas Goedert, reserve receiver Marquise “Hollywood” Brown, and backup offensive tackle Fred Johnson. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard is questionable with a knee injury that limited him all week. Running back Saquon Barkley, who was limited earlier in the week with a stinger, is not listed at all. Wideout DeVonta Smith also has no injury designation after missing Thursday’s practice with a hamstring issue. Both practiced in full today.

summary: The NFL season is always evolving. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles and Makai Lemon #9 celebrate after game winning touchdown during the second half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season is always evolving. We enter week 3 with unique perspective and ample concern for many teams as injuries and unexpected poor performance have impacted the league across the board. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team’s success. I’ll also try and mix in a few under the radar players from time to time. Let’s start with the Philadelphia Eagles offensive player that I will be focused on. Offense: Makai Lemon, #9 – WR If Saquon Barkely was unavailable for this game, this spot more than likely would have gone to backup running back, Tank Bigsby, whom I still expect to make his mark in this game – but Lemon gets the nod here for a few reasons. The first one being he was my favorite WR coming out of this draft. I say that knowing full well how disappointing the start of his career has been in just the first two games. But, the way he attacks the ball like he attacks would-be tacklers and moves down the field like a man possessed is quite reminiscent to a WR we are all too familiar with around these parts – Amon Ra St. Brown. With AJ Brown shipped off to New England and Devonta Smith nursing a hammy, Lemon should get his most robust snap share yet. Combine that with some questions in Chicago’s secondary with Tyrique Stevenson unlikely to play which could cause a ripple effect with their DBs, we might be seeing Cam Lewis or Nick McCloud lined up over Lemon in the slot with rookie stud Malik Muhammed II moving out to the boundary CB spot. If Philly is having trouble running the ball with their injured offensive line and hobbled running backs, look for QB Jalen Hurts to get rid of the ball quickly. And with starting TE Dallas Goedert also hurt, expect Lemon to get plenty of opportunities. Defense: Andrew Mukuba, #24 – S Another young player that I was extremely high on coming out of college, Mukuba was my favorite Safety in last years class that also featured Xavier Watts, Malaki Starks and Nick Emmanwori. The way he showed up in big games for Texas both as a tackler and pass-defender were most impressive to me. Mukuba is a safety not afraid to lay the wood in ball-carriers and plays much bigger than his 5’11”, 190lb fram might suggest. And his range on the back end is dangerous. With Quinyon Mitchell, Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean locking up WRs in coverage, Case Keenum needs to be careful of a roaming Mukuba in the secondary. Hopefully Chicago can control the LOS and run the ball effectively, opening up passing lanes, but Mukuba is a young player in Vic Fangio’s defense that I would have loved to see in Chicago and am excited to see him compete against our pass catchers. What about you? Which Philadelphia Eagle is sure to capture your focus on Monday Night?
