title: Chicago Bears Week 3 Flashbacks: Minnesota Miracle, Windy City Flyer, and More
summary: It’s week 3, and as always, we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Vikings: McMahon’s Miracle in Minny The 1985 Bears season is filled with memorable moments, but one of the first came on a Thursday night in Minnesota. Jim McMahon was dealing with back spasms and an […]
full_text: CHICAGO - SEPTEMBER 27: Devin Hester #23 of the Chicago Bears returns a punt 62-yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on September 27, 2010 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s week 3, and as always, we have some hallmark games from the past to uncover! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Vikings: McMahon’s Miracle in Minny The 1985 Bears season is filled with memorable moments, but one of the first came on a Thursday night in Minnesota. Jim McMahon was dealing with back spasms and an infection in his right leg, leaving Steve Fuller to start with Chicago looking to improve to 3-0. The offense struggled without McMahon, and midway through the third quarter the Bears found themselves trailing 17-9. Mike Ditka finally turned to his injured quarterback. McMahon’s first pass went 70 yards for a touchdown to Willie Gault. His second went 25 yards to Dennis McKinnon for another score. Seven pass attempts into his night, McMahon connected with McKinnon again for a 43-yard touchdown. Just like that, a 17-9 deficit had become a 30-17 Bears lead. McMahon finished 8-of-15 for 236 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, while Gault recorded 146 receiving yards and McKinnon added 133 yards and two scores. Chicago held on for a 33-24 win. The victory moved the Bears to 3-0 on their way to a 15-1 season and, eventually, a dominant run through the playoffs and a Super Bowl XX championship. Before all of that, though, an injured Jim McMahon came off the bench and completely flipped a game in a matter of minutes. 2.) 2010, Bears vs. Packers: Devin Hester is still ridiculous By 2010, the NFL had learned a pretty simple lesson when it came to Devin Hester. Don’t kick him the football. Hester entered Chicago’s Monday Night Football matchup with Green Bay without a return touchdown in nearly three years. With both teams sitting at 2-0, the Packers built a 10-0 lead before Jay Cutler found Greg Olsen late in the first half to get Chicago back into the game. The Bears still trailed 10-7 entering the fourth quarter. Then Hester finally broke through. He fielded a punt and raced 62 yards for a touchdown, giving Chicago its first lead of the night and recording his first return score since 2007. Green Bay answered and retook the lead, but Robbie Gould tied the game at 17 before the Bears defense came up with one more opportunity. Brian Urlacher stripped James Jones late in the fourth quarter, with Tim Jennings recovering the fumble in Green Bay territory. Gould eventually drilled a 19-yard field goal with four seconds remaining to give Chicago a 20-17 victory. The Packers did plenty to hurt themselves, committing a franchise-record 18 penalties for 152 yards, but the lasting image from the night was Hester looking like the most dangerous return man in football once again. Chicago improved to 3-0 and eventually finished the season 11-5, winning the NFC North and reaching the NFC Championship Game. For one night at Soldier Field, the formula was pretty simple. Give Devin Hester the football and see what happens. 3.) 2013, Bears @ Steelers: The defense takes over For years, Chicago’s defense had built its identity around one thing. Taking the football away. That trend continued into Marc Trestman’s first season as head coach, and Week 3 against the Steelers was one of the best examples. The Bears jumped out to a 17-0 lead, helped by a D.J. Williams strip-sack that set up an early touchdown. Then the defense started scoring points of its own. Major Wright intercepted Ben Roethlisberger and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown, giving Chicago a 24-3 advantage. Pittsburgh battled all the way back, eventually cutting the lead to 27-23 in the fourth quarter behind 406 passing yards from Roethlisberger and 196 receiving yards from Antonio Brown. Chicago finally answered with a Jay Cutler touchdown pass to Earl Bennett. 𝐒𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝟐𝟐, 𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟑 The Bears put up 𝐅𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐘 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh on SNF! @JayHasTweets with the truck stick 😤 pic.twitter.com/kbZ5lIB2SV — This Day in Chicago Sports (@ChiSportsDay) September 22, 2021 Then the defense put the game away. Lance Briggs knocked the ball free while sacking Roethlisberger, and Julius Peppers picked it up and rumbled 42 yards for another Bears defensive touchdown. Chicago left Pittsburgh with a 40-23 victory and a 3-0 record. The final numbers tell the story. Pittsburgh outgained the Bears 459-258, but Chicago forced five turnovers, committed none and scored 23 points off Pittsburgh giveaways. It may not have been the cleanest win, but it was a familiar formula for Bears fans. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: CBS tabs Bengals as Super Bowl ‘contenders’
summary: For the first time in Joe Burrow’s career, the Cincinnati Bengals are off to a hot start with both sides of the football playing at a high level. The Bengals started 2-0 for the second straight season, but this time Burrow is healthy heading into week 3. The front office invested heavily on the defensive […]
full_text: For the first time in Joe Burrow’s career, the Cincinnati Bengals are off to a hot start with both sides of the football playing at a high level. The Bengals started 2-0 for the second straight season, but this time Burrow is healthy heading into week 3. The front office invested heavily on the defensive side of the football this offseason, and it has shown so far to kick off the new year. Cincinnati is 1 of 8 teams that are undefeated heading into week 3 alongside the Chiefs, Seahawks, Bills, Vikings, Eagles, 49ers, and Raiders. CBS Sports recently shared their ‘contenders’ and ‘pretenders’ list , which breaks down the confidence level for each team that is undefeated. Bryan DeArdo of CBS Sports has the Bengals 2nd on the contenders list behind the Seahawks, writing, “Guilty as charged in terms of drinking the Bengals Kool-Aid after two games. A big reason for the optimism is Cincinnati’s revamped defense (including former Giants Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence), which has complemented Joe Burrow and the team’s high-flying offense. In fact, the Bengals’ defense is actually ranked ahead of their offense through two games. Cincinnati’s schedule is another reason for optimism. They’ll play five games against teams that are currently 0-2. The Bengals also play in an AFC North division that appears to be having a down year.” The Bills and 49ers are the remaining contenders, while the Chiefs, Vikings, Eagles, and Raiders were listed as the pretenders by CBS Sports. We will see how the next few weeks go, but history has shown that Joe Burrow and the offense find their stride after the first two weeks of the season, which only makes the start even more exciting.

title: Zac Taylor recalls Steelers DC Patrick Graham being an option for Bengals before hiring Al Golden in 2025
summary: Connections in the Bengals vs. Steelers rivalry run deep. Look no further than current Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. With a 2-1 record in three games against the Bengals, Zac Taylor interviewed Graham after firing former defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo following the 2024 season. Taylor ultimately hired Notre Dame defensive coordinator Al Golden, but the […]
full_text: Connections in the Bengals vs. Steelers rivalry run deep. Look no further than current Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. With a 2-1 record in three games against the Bengals, Zac Taylor interviewed Graham after firing former defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo following the 2024 season. Taylor ultimately hired Notre Dame defensive coordinator Al Golden, but the head coach came away impressed with what Graham brings to the table. “You interview him because you are impressed with the scheme and the problems you face when you go against him,” Taylor said this week to Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson . “When you meet him, incredibly personable … Thought highly of him before. Thought highly of him even more so afterwards.” Graham is 47 years old and was the New England Patriots’ linebackers coach when they won Super Bowl XLIX in February of 2015 against Seattle. The Patriots are where Graham got his start in NFL coaching. He’s been a defensive coordinator since 2020 with the New York Giants, spending two years in New York before going to Las Vegas for four years with Maxx Crosby and the Raiders’ defense. The Bengals were mentioned in trade rumors for Maxx Crosby way back earlier in the offseason. More importantly, Graham knows Dexter Lawrence well. He was in New York during Lawrence’s second and third seasons with the Giants. This connection adds another intriguing layer to Sunday’s matchup in Pittsburgh, where the 2-0 Bengals will look to improve to 3-0 behind another strong defensive performance. Meanwhile, the Steelers will lean heavily on their defense, which has allowed just 33 points in two games. That’s the same number of points the Bengals have allowed, though seven of those came off a Joe Burrow pick-six. Sunday could be a defensive struggle that will see the winner be whoever reaches 20 points first.

full_text: Dec 28, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Andrei Iosivas (80) celebrates with tight end Tanner Hudson (87) after a play during the first half against the Arizona Cardinals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Preceding their big matchup against the Steelers on Sunday, the Bengals made a few roster moves . A couple were not surprising, but the Bengals are tweaking things before they hit the field in Pittsburgh Saturday afternoon. Wide Receiver Andrei Iosivas landed on injured reserve after injuring a ligament in his thumb and having surgery. While he’s expected back in 4-6 weeks, it’s definitely a downer for a guy looking for a bounce-back season in a contract year. Meanwhile, Cincinnati elevated linebacker Joe Giles-Harris to the active roster. He is a third-year player out of Duke University and has bounced around the league a bit. His first stint with the Bengals was back in 2024, but he returned a year after playing with the Jaguars. He was on the practice squad last year but was called up on October 30 and played in 10 games. He was on the team’s practice squad again to start this season. Hudson was released by the team following final cuts, but promptly re-signed to their practice squad. He played in Week 1 against the Buccaneers and had a reception, but reverted to the practice squad. This will be the case once again following the conclusion of Sunday’s Week 3 game.

summary: Zac Taylor is in a unique position. He’s the head coach of the Bengals and their offensive play-caller. In his position, Taylor, like a CEO, is also in charge of managing this team’s personalities. Most of those personalities have been on offense in Taylor’s tenure. Now, the defense has some. Not only is the Bengals’ […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Cornerback Dax Hill #23 of the Cincinnati Bengals and defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II #97 of the Cincinnati Bengals have fun during warmups before the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals on September 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Zac Taylor is in a unique position. He’s the head coach of the Bengals and their offensive play-caller. In his position, Taylor, like a CEO, is also in charge of managing this team’s personalities. Most of those personalities have been on offense in Taylor’s tenure. Now, the defense has some. Not only is the Bengals’ defense revived. It has personality , especially up front and with Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence is the tone-setter of the Bengals’ defense. That comes in the form of on-field production, but it also comes with having a little fun on the field trash-talking. “He just loves it. I think he’s contributed to the personality of our defense,” Taylor said after Friday’s practice. “Not only are they talented and confident, and playing with this really good chemistry, but they’ve got a really big personality as a whole, and he’s obviously a big part of this, and that’s what’s fun.” Lawrence was mic’d up during the Bengals’ 20-6 win over the Houston Texans in Week 2. It was incredible to listen to, with Lawrence demonstrating elite trash-talking abilities. It’s something we haven’t really seen from a Bengals’ defense in quite some time. The S.W.A.T. Team had personality back in the 80s, but Bengals’ defenses since really haven’t it… until now. “With the mic’d up stuff, everybody gets to see kind of what we see from him, (defensive tackle) Jonathan Allen, and everybody kind of combining together,” Taylor said. “And it probably gets a couple of the other guys out of their shell a little bit.” Don’t be surprised if you see other mic’d-up segments and soundbites from the Bengals or NFL Films showcasing Lawrence and the Bengals’ defensive line trash-talking their opponents. The Bengals’ defensive line is getting a lot of attention. They have talented players, but they also have players with personalities.

title: Orlando Brown Jr. believes the 2026 Bengals are a Super Bowl team
summary: The expectations and pressure were at an all-time high for the Cincinnati Bengals entering the 2026 season after missing the playoffs for three straight years. Although it is still incredibly early, the Bengals’ revamped roster has shown up and executed at a winning level. The Bengals are 2-0 with a healthy Joe Burrow for the […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, CA - SEPTEMBER 14: Orlando Brown #75 of the Cincinnati Bengals stands on field prior to the first half of an NFL game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The expectations and pressure were at an all-time high for the Cincinnati Bengals entering the 2026 season after missing the playoffs for three straight years. Although it is still incredibly early, the Bengals’ revamped roster has shown up and executed at a winning level. The Bengals are 2-0 with a healthy Joe Burrow for the first time in the Zac Taylor era, and the defense has been lights out through the first two weeks. One of the biggest reasons for the early success is the new additions on the defensive side that are not only veterans but also Super Bowl champions. The front office brought in Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook, two guys that have won Super Bowls at their previous stops in the NFL. The Bengals also have another guy on the roster who has Super Bowl experience as well, and that is left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. Brown recently had an interview with Casino.org and shared that he believes this is a Super Bowl-caliber roster and a roster that is even better than the one he was a part of on the Chiefs. “To be honest, this is nothing like I’ve ever been a part of,” Brown said. “We are very unique in so many different ways when I look at our offense, defense, and special teams units. I’ve never been a part of anything like this.” As I said earlier in the article, the expectations are at an all-time high this season, and it is clear the players on the roster feel the exact same way.

title: The 3 key Browns-Panthers players that could decide Week 3 matchup
summary: After starting the season 1-1 on the road, the Cleveland Browns return home to take on the Carolina Panthers in Week 3. The Panthers are also 1-1 coming into this game, and both teams will be looking to leave this week with a winning record. Several key matchups will likely determine which team leaves with […]
full_text: After starting the season 1-1 on the road, the Cleveland Browns return home to take on the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 . The Panthers are also 1-1 coming into this game, and both teams will be looking to leave this week with a winning record. Several key matchups will likely determine which team leaves with the win. Bryce Young has gotten off to a productive start this season, making it crucial for the Browns’ secondary to limit his effectiveness in the passing game. Additionally, the defensive line will need to have success in getting pressure on Young to help limit the Panthers offense from getting explosive plays. Quinshon Judkins’ production has been limited in the first two weeks of the season. With 33 rushing yards in Week 1 and just 21 in Week 2, the Cleveland offense will be hoping for more production from him this week. Carolina has allowed the most rushing yards per game so far this season, so this will be a big opportunity to capitalize on that weakness. Harold Fannin Jr. may be another key to the Browns offense in this matchup. He is coming off of a solid 5-reception, 54-yard performance against the Buccaneers and has started to establish himself as a reliable target for Deshaun Watson. With the Panthers’ struggles on defense, Fannin Jr. could be very active in this game. Let me know what you think in the comments – What are the 3 matchups that could decide Sunday’s game?

full_text: The Cleveland Browns are at home against the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season this Sunday, September 27, at 1:00 pm ET. The Browns are 2.5-point underdogs against the Panthers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Here are my favorite player prop bets from the Browns’ perspective in Week 3. Last week, we hit on 2 of our 3 picks: We took the over on TE Harold Fannin having 36+ receiving yards. He had 54. We took the over on QB Deshaun Watson having 176+ passing yards. He had 238. The one we lost was that we also had the over on RB Raheim Sanders having 9+ rushing yards. We might have been a little too cute with that one, as he only finished with 4 rushing yards. Browns vs. Panthers Best NFL player prop bets Quinshon Judkins First TD Scorer (+500) We’re starting bold this week. To clarify, if you take this bet, it means that not only will RB Quinshon Judkins score a touchdown, but it will also be the first touchdown scored by either team in the game. With the Panthers’ run defense having been gashed a bit over these first two weeks, and Cleveland showing a trend of taking the ball first on offense, it’s not a bad gamble that Judkins will find his way into the end zone for the first time this season. The risk here is the fact that the Browns’ offense has historically struggled to get points in the first half of games under Watson. Quinshon Judkins Most Rushing Yards (+130) We’re really riding the Judkins’ breakout game hard this week. Chubba Hubbard hasn’t lit it up for Carolina either. Even though Deshaun Watson has been the Browns’ leading rusher this season, the idea here obviously is that Judkins can get close to the 100-yard rushing mark. For practical senses, this bet comes down to who you think will have more rushing yards between Hubbard and Judkins. Quinshon Judkins Over 59.5 Rushing Yards (-113) Why not keep it simple? This is probably the first time that I’ve ever done the hat trick of having three best bets on the same player. But if Judkins is going to achiever either of the first two, then logic says he’ll also hit the over on 60+ yards rushing. For reference, four players in two games against the Panthers have had 60+ yards rushing. Browns fans, let us know which player prop bets you’re looking at this week against the Panthers.

title: Browns: Grinding on defense, running the ball, and booing the QB
summary: The Cleveland Browns calmed the storm surrounding the team with last week’s victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.  The defense stepped up when it mattered in the fourth quarter, stopping the Buccaneers on their final drive. The run game was still a mess – just 1.9 yards per carry – but quarterback Deshaun Watson made […]
full_text: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns calmed the storm surrounding the team with last week’s victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The defense stepped up when it mattered in the fourth quarter, stopping the Buccaneers on their final drive. The run game was still a mess – just 1.9 yards per carry – but quarterback Deshaun Watson made up for it by not being a complete disaster, which has to be labeled as a positive. Speaking of Watson, he made good use of his playmakers, as 16 of his 24 completions went to Denzel Boston, Harold Fannin Jr., and KC Concepcion. That is a solid plan for a quarterback who, to use a once-unpopular phrase for a Cleveland quarterback, clearly has “diminishing skills” since arriving in town. Cleveland opens the home portion of its schedule on Sunday when they host the Carolina Panthers, who come to town with a surprisingly effective offense that is averaging 35.5 points a game with quarterback Bryce Young running the show. There is no such thing as an easy day at work for the Browns, especially if the defense can’t keep the Panthers out of the end zone, so here are a few takeaways from the coaches about the upcoming game. The grind is real on defense. Carolina is averaging 312.5 passing yards and has 10 pass plays of 20 or more yards, which is the second most in the league. Cleveland will counter with a defense that has not allowed a 300-yard passer in 47 consecutive games, but one that has also been burned by the big play (six completions of 20 yards or more) through the first two games. If the Browns are to contain Carolina’s offense, they need to keep grinding, according to defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg : “I think everybody’s got to have a foundation, right? And for us, our defensive foundation is heart, mind, fist. And I’ve talked about it, and the heart and the fist were there, and we made a commitment to constantly improving the mind, coaches and players. And when you can look in the mirror and say, I can do better, it’s week to week, whether you get your ass kicked or whether you have a win. “It’s about all of us working our asses off each week, grinding, making this Thursday better than last Thursday, making this meeting that we’re coming up to better than the last meeting, getting this game better than the last game. And it’s about our style of play and the level of execution. That’s the truth about the way this league goes. It’s such a marathon, and we’re in week three of that marathon right now, and our whole goal is to play better than we did last week and hopefully do enough to help the Browns win.” When will the run game take off? Cleveland averaged a workable four yards per carry against Jacksonville in Week 1 before bottoming out in Week 2 against the Buccaneers. Watson is the team’s leading rusher, which is completely unsustainable, while No. 1 running back Quinshon Judkins is averaging just 2.3 yards per carry. With nothing really working, offensive coordinator Travis Switzer said he is looking at every aspect of the run game for answers : “The first two weeks, we’re not where we want to be, so we’re looking at everything that goes into that, and everyone involved. I have to look at it schematically. Certainly, there was a play too, from the game the other day where I’m looking at it like, you know what, I didn’t put us in a great position there. And then we’re looking at just the execution of it by all parties, right, the blockers and the fundamentals and the things that we’re working at up there, the runners and just trusting their eyes and seeing it. But yeah, we’re looking at all parts of that. “But certainly, we’re going to have to run the ball into loaded boxes at times. If you want to be a dominant team and a good running team, you’re going to have to do that. So, yeah, there are different things schematically you can do, whether it’s different run schemes, whether it’s opening it up, whether it’s using the quarterback like we’ve been talking about, there’s different things you can do there, but we’re going to need to run the ball into those looks.” To boo or not to boo. That is the question. Sunday will mark Deshaun Watson’s first start in a regular-season game in front of the home fans since October 20, 2024, the day he suffered the first of two Achilles tendon injuries. There has been a lot of talk about how the home fans will greet Watson when he hits the field for the first offensive play, and how he will react to the response if it is a negative one. The surest way to avoid any unpleasantries, or at least limit them, is to simply play well. And after his performance against Tampa, Watson’s confidence should be on the way up, according to head coach Todd Monken : “He’s had his best week (of practice), you know, he really has. And I think that’s been building; I think that’s been building from becoming the starter after the first week being disappointed and the second half that he played last week. And I think, I mean, you’d have to speak to him, but I think his confidence should be at an all-time high, you know, and the excitement of an opportunity, a third opportunity to continue to just grow and develop as a player. Because again, he’s just scratching the surface, the last couple of days, couple weeks.” The Browns and Panthers kick off Sunday at 1 p.m. from Huntington Bank Field. full_text: The future of the Cleveland Browns defensive line after the trade of DE Myles Garrett has been all about DE Jared Verse and DT Mason Graham . Verse, as the key part of the Garrett deal , needs to have a big Week 3 after a disappointing start to his Browns career. Graham has two sacks this year and has continued his development from his rookie year. DT Mike Hall Jr. could take the group to the next level. Hall, who has played some defensive end as well, was Cleveland’s second-round pick in 2024 . Hall has dealt with injuries that limited him to 17 games in his first two seasons. His 2.5 sacks are disappointing given his draft position, but production for interior defenders does not always lead to sacks. In 2026, Hall has shown flashes of disruption while playing in close to 50% of the team’s defensive snaps: If #Browns DT Mike Hall can string together more performances like the one Sunday against the #Buccaneers , they have a fun, young defensive interior. pic.twitter.com/1QZgSbxGNN — Josh Edwards (@EdwardsCBS) September 25, 2026 The above play is a great example of an impact play that doesn’t show up in the stat sheet. Former Browns OL LeCharles Bentley also noted : Mike Hall is another player whose impact will not be fully explained by the box score. Hall was a difference-maker Sunday. His superpower is his get-off. Bentley showed this example of Hall’s quickness off the snap: With Cleveland’s edge rushers struggling to get pressure, Hall and Graham can get penetration up the middle can create quicker disruptions for opposing offenses. While good pass rushers are rarer from the inside, penetration up the middle can have an even bigger impact on both the run and pass games. Hall’s development, even if it doesn’t show up in the box score, can help make up for the loss of Garrett and give Verse and company a better chance to make an impact from the outside. title: Browns legend Brian Brennan talks to DBN before his Legends induction in Week 3
summary: For the Cleveland Browns, Week 3 is shaping up to be a big one on the sidelines, and a chance to be an exciting one on the field. Three former Browns will be inducted into the Browns Legends club: WR Brian Brennan, OL Alex Mack, and OL Lou Rymkus. On top of that, Cleveland welcomed […]
full_text: For the Cleveland Browns, Week 3 is shaping up to be a big one on the sidelines, and a chance to be an exciting one on the field . Three former Browns will be inducted into the Browns Legends club : WR Brian Brennan , OL Alex Mack , and OL Lou Rymkus . On top of that, Cleveland welcomed back RB Nick Chubb , who signed a one-day contract and will be honored during Sunday’s contest . Brennan, one of my (Jared) favorite players growing up , spoke with our Barry Shuck in advance of his induction into the Browns Legends this weekend Q1: Take us back to the phone call from the Browns about you being inducted into the Browns Legends A1: I have been working out of my residence lately here in Cleveland. And I was working at my desk when JW Johnson, who is the president of the Haslem sports group, called. I thought we were going to catch up on the assistance he needed with alumni. We never made it that far. He surprised me that I would be inducted into the 2026 class of the legends. I was surprised, overwhelmed, and grateful. And I told him that I loved being a Cleveland Brown. That era in which I played had so much success and great players on the roster. To be included as part of that meant a lot to me. Q2: Who was the first person you told? A2: My wife. We’ve been married 42 years. She has been there for all the successes and all the struggles I’ve had as a person, a player, and as post career. Any success I’ve had, she was a part of. As soon as I got the call, I hung up, and I called her. Q3: Playing in an actual NFL game must’ve been the easy part after practicing against Frank Minnifield and Hanford Dixon. Every day, how did these two guys impact your growth as a receiver at this level? A3: We had a really strong receiver group with Webster Slaughter, Clarence Weathers, Reggie Langhorne, and myself. We were a tight-knit group. We had to battle every day against Frank and Hanford. We challenged them as much as they challenged us. I learned a lot about getting off the line of scrimmage, which was so prevalent when I played. Working against those two helped all of us against game opponents. We saw elite defensive back play every day. Q4: In your entire career, you played with a lot of great quarterbacks, including Boomer Esiason with Cincy and under exceptional coaching. If you could suit up for one more game, pick a quarterback and a coach. A4: Bernie Kosar and a combination of Marty Schottenheimer and Lindy Infante. Both I loved. Bernie was a student of the game, and he was great with the football; we had great chemistry, we trusted each other, and he was just so smart in the position. He was one of the first pioneers to consistently use audibles that other quarterbacks got a reputation for using, like Peyton Manning. Marty was a great defensive coach, while Infante was an offensive mind like no other that has never gotten the credit he deserves. Q5: You are not an Ohio native, although you played for both the Browns and later the Bengals. After you hung up your cleats, you decided to stay in the Cleveland area with KeyBank, although they had offices in New York, Connecticut, Alaska, and Colorado. Yet you decided to stay in the Cleveland area. Why? A5: I had success in culture as a Brown. The culture at KeyBank is very solid. To win in the challenging financial arena is part of that culture. And the headquarters is located in Cleveland. I was happy being in Cleveland, love the area, and thought I knew the people. So I felt comfortable around the character of the people here. Q6: There were plenty of NFL receivers who were a lot taller than you, had more weight, faster than you, and drafted higher than in Round 4. Are you the poster child for perseverance in pro football? A6: There are a lot of people who aren’t the prototypical player at their positions. I felt I was always a great athlete and could still play today if I was in shape. I was the 11th or 12th receiver drafted in 1984. Receiver Irving Fryar was the number one overall pick and caught more passes than me, and that was it. I always thought I had the ability, and I’m glad the Browns saw it. Q7: What does it mean for you to be included in the legends? A7:The Browns are now putting me in a high place of team achievement. I am grateful and as a player have no choice but to be overwhelmed at how they view my playing career while in Cleveland. To be included as part of this means a lot to me.

title: Browns fans think Cleveland will beat Carolina: how things change after a week
summary: A win can be the medicine fans need to get re-invested in the product. That’s a new season high. Panthers fans are not […]
full_text: A win can be the medicine fans need to get re-invested in the product. After last week’s fan confidence in the direction of the team had dipped to 21%, after the Browns’ win over the Buccaneers, fan confidence increased by 39 percentage points up to 60%. That’s a new season high. Panthers fans are not lacking confidence either, as 90% of fans are confident in the direction of their team. Having QB Bryce Young looking good no doubt contributes to that high percentage, since both teams are 1-1. What about this week’s game, though? We asked one question, and it focused on what Browns fans expect the outcome of this Sunday’s game against the Panthers will be. Overall, 57% of Browns fans think the Browns will win, with most of those fans projecting a close win. 25% of fans think the Panthers will edge out a victory, while 18% of fans think last week’s game by the Browns was a mirage and that Carolina will dominate their way to victory. We’ll see how things pan out. If QB Deshaun Watson had played poorly against the Buccaneers and Cleveland had dropped to 0-2, you can believe that the pitchforks would be out if he was starting under those circumstances. In that case, people thought QB Shedeur Sanders would have to start. But the script has changed, for at least a week. Because after that performance by Watson, there’s no defendable reason to now bench him. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 2.5 point underdogs against the Panthers this week, with the over/under being 41.5.

title: Cowboys, Ravens strengths/weaknesses make for  interesting matchup
summary: It’s not very often two teams square off against one another and the strengths and weaknesses of both ball clubs align as they do in the Week 3 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens. Whichever team can best exploit this will likely be the one that walks away with the “W”. The Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images It’s not very often two teams square off against one another and the strengths and weaknesses of both ball clubs align as they do in the Week 3 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens. Whichever team can best exploit this will likely be the one that walks away with the “W”. The Cowboys and Ravens currently find themselves in similar situations through the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Both teams are 1-1 with a disappointing and unexpected loss under their belts, and yet, both still have Super Bowl aspirations. But there is still a lot of football left to play. As we all know, the Cowboys biggest weakness so far through the first two weeks of the season this year is their run defense. They are currently ranked 30 th in the league allowing 173.5 rushing yards per game. On the flipside, the Ravens rushing attack is ranked fifth in the league, averaging 155 yards per game. Baltimore’s rushing attack, headlined by QB Lamar Jackson and RB Derrick Henry, could very well decide the outcome of this game. This is a tough duo to try to contain, especially Jackson, who may be arguably the best dual-threat QB in the history of the league. If Dallas can limit their production though, it could lead to victory. The best chance for the Cowboys securing back-to-back wins is by exploiting the Ravens biggest weakness, their pass defense. Baltimore’s currently allowing 191 passing yards a game, ranking 11 th in the league. That’s not too shabby, but they have as of yet faced a team with the caliber of weapons Dak Prescott has at his disposal. In CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, the Cowboys All-Pro WR duo is arguably the best in the entire league. Then throw in Jake Ferguson and Ryan Flournoy, both of whom have strong chemistry with Prescott, and it becomes one of the more lethal units in the entire league. That could help even the playing field against the Ravens potent rushing attack. Add it all up and this is one of those strengths versus weaknesses matchup’s that could potentially go either way depending on which team is better exploits their opponent. And, considering both teams are playing at a neutral venue in Brazil, neither one has the edge of home field advantage, making this strength/weakness matchup all the more interesting.

title: 5 things to watch when the Cowboys play the Ravens
summary: The time is near for a big international showdown as the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens travel to South America for a crucial Week 3 matchup in Brazil. The last time the Cowboys had an international game was in 2014 when they beat the Jaguars 31-17 at Wembley Stadium in London. Foreign soil or not, […]
full_text: Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images The time is near for a big international showdown as the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens travel to South America for a crucial Week 3 matchup in Brazil. The last time the Cowboys had an international game was in 2014 when they beat the Jaguars 31-17 at Wembley Stadium in London. Foreign soil or not, it’s a big game for both teams as each of them is off to a 1-1 start and would like to return to the States with a winning record. The Cowboys are trending up after a regroup win over the Commanders, while the Ravens started the season hot, but fell victim to a second-half letdown to the Saints last week. This matchup will feature the top two vote-getters for the MVP race in 2023, Dak Prescott and Lamar Jackson, who will have to shake off significant jet lag and navigate potentially poor field conditions. This could come down to which team best adapts to the elements, but how will they pull it off? Here are five things to watch when these two battle it out in Rio de Janeiro. 1. Battling the field conditions The biggest opponent on Sunday might not be wearing a jersey. All the talk in recent weeks has centered around the significant issues with the field in Maracanã Stadium. It could be bumpy, it might be mushy, but whatever the conditions, it will be something the players will have to muddle through. Hopefully, the Cowboys bring the right shoes to grip the turf, but we should prepare ourselves for what could be a messy affair. Poor field conditions favor more straight-line power runners and physical downfield defenders who don’t rely on sudden changes of direction to make plays, so it could neutralize the Cowboys offensive playmakers and empower the Ravens more physical ones. 2. Wrap it up Bad footing or not, the Cowboys’ defense will see a heavy dose of the Ravens’ ground attack. Prepare for an avalanche of rushing from running back Derrick Henry. Nobody produces a more linear power rushing attack than the ageless veteran, who has averaged over five yards a carry in each season he’s been in Baltimore. And so far, this year is no different. Not only will the Cowboys have to deal with Henry, but quarterback Lamar Jackson is the crème de la crème of rushing quarterbacks, which is unfortunate considering how the Cowboys defense struggled in the first two weeks against Jaxson Dart and Jayden Daniels. Stopping these two offensive weapons will be key for Dallas, and it could come down to fundamentals. There won’t be any room for mistakes, so proper gap discipline, squaring up on ball carriers, and strong tackling will be paramount. Failure to do so could turn a routine play into a catastrophic, game-changing chunk play. 3. Run game mitigation Last week, the Cowboys’ offense successfully worked around a committed run-stopping Commanders defense by unleashing an efficient passing attack. That’s a good plan, but it may not be as effective while subjected to treacherous field conditions. This means the Cowboys must find ways to run the ball better. Improved blocking and more creative schemes are vital to at least have some presence of a ground attack. They’ll also need clever ways to use the short passing game to supplement the rushing game. Look for swing passes, quick slants, and misdirection plays to help keep the chains moving. 4. Up for grabs A sloppy field isn’t conducive to crisp routes. That should mean a lot of the big passing plays could come courtesy of yards-after-the-catch. While both teams will look to exploit that, the Cowboys also have an x-factor in George Pickens. In a game where creating separation won’t be easy, the Cowboys have one of the best contested pass catchers in the league. The team’s other star receiver has been quiet so far, but he could become an international hero if he can populate the highlight reel by coming up with some impressive 50/50 balls. We know he has it in him. 5. Protect the ball Keeping with the bad elements theme, a sloppy field is a breeding ground for loose balls. Whether you have muffed exchanges, deflected passes, or just straight-up slippery footballs, failure to take care of the ball could be a difference-maker. Teams that lose the turnover battle usually lose the game. This could play in the Cowboys’ favor as the offense has done a great job securing the ball with a pristine zero fumbles through two games. Conversely, the defense has forced six fumbles already. Their cautiousness on offense and aggressive, physical nature on defense could push the needle in their favor when it comes to turnovers.

title: Large percentage of Cowboys fans feel a big loss coming against Ravens
summary: Let’s cut straight to the point. Dallas Cowboys fans are not feeling confident about this game against the Baltimore Ravens. The trip to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil has Dallas as the home team, but away from AT&T Stadium is not the best ground for the Cowboys. In fact, the ground is a big piece of […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Let’s cut straight to the point. Dallas Cowboys fans are not feeling confident about this game against the Baltimore Ravens. The trip to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil has Dallas as the home team, but away from AT&T Stadium is not the best ground for the Cowboys. In fact, the ground is a big piece of contention as the field surface could be tricky. But what Cowboys fans probably have the biggest worry about is the combo of Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry running wild against a defense that has been unable to stop the run for a while now. Christian Parker’s new defense, with Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams anchoring the middle, was supposed to reverse the trend. It hasn’t happened yet. The second place vote was 31% who backed the Cowboys to win a close one. Even though a majority of Cowboys fans feel a loss coming, 65% of fans feel the team is headed in the right direction. title: Cowboys vs Ravens: Score predictions for Week 3
summary: Dallas heads to Rio de Janeiro for one of the most unusual games on its schedule, facing the Baltimore Ravens at Maracanã Stadium in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Rio. Both teams arrive at 1-1, but in very different moods after Dallas beat Washington 37-20 and Baltimore let a fourth-quarter lead disappear in a […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images Dallas heads to Rio de Janeiro for one of the most unusual games on its schedule, facing the Baltimore Ravens at Maracanã Stadium in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Rio. Both teams arrive at 1-1, but in very different moods after Dallas beat Washington 37-20 and Baltimore let a fourth-quarter lead disappear in a 24-17 loss to New Orleans. With injuries on both sides and questions surrounding the playing surface, this matchup could demand plenty of adjustment as the game develops. When Baltimore has the ball Baltimore’s game-plan for Dallas should be straightforward. Derrick Henry has already rushed for 212 yards and four touchdowns at 5.3 yards per carry, while Lamar Jackson adds another running threat to the Cowboys’ offence. This is a significant concern for Dallas, especially after allowing Washington to rush for 182 yards last week, with Jayden Daniels also gaining 69 yards before leaving the game. Baltimore can exploit Henry’s strength between the tackles and then use Jackson’s play-action and option concepts to keep the Cowboys guessing. Dallas’s goal should be to control first downs and force Jackson into passing situations rather than allowing Baltimore to dictate the game through the running game. When Dallas has the ball Dallas found the passing offense it was seeking against Washington. Dak Prescott completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns, while CeeDee Lamb scored two touchdowns with 153 yards. This performance should serve as a starting point for their upcoming game against Baltimore. Last week, New Orleans demonstrated their ability to attack against the Ravens, completing 27 of 34 passes for 252 yards and converting eight of 15 third downs. They eventually scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter. Dallas has a strong trio of receivers – Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson – who can spread Baltimore’s coverage across the field. This should allow Prescott to make quick passes and intermediate routes, keeping the ball moving and avoiding holding it for too long. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (0-2) Aren’t we a gloomy bunch? Or perhaps we’re just facing reality. Clearly if the Cowboys play defense the same way they have the first two games, they have little chance of winning. And I don’t think it will be close. Ravens 30, Cowboys 19. Brandon Loree (1-1) If this game were hosted by Baltimore, I’d pick the Ravens to win. If this game were at AT&T Stadium, I’d probably also pick the Ravens to win. But the fact that it’s on a neutral field in a different country certainly keeps things closer to 50-50. The Cowboys offense is playing at a top-five pace right now, but the defense still hasn’t earned my trust yet to go against top-level competition and be dominant. The jump from week one to week two was certainly encouraging, but not enough for me to pick Dallas in this game. I think it comes down to a last-second field goal or a touchdown drive that wins the game by Lamar Jackson, and the Ravens walk out of Rio with a 30-24 victory over Dallas Dyllan Rivers (1-1) The Cowboys have had a difficult time defending against mobile quarterbacks through two weeks. Now in Rio, they’ll face the king of mobile QBs in Lamar Jackson, paired with an elite runner in Derrick Henry. That does not bode well for this Cowboys defense. This strength on weakness matchup is too much for Dallas to overcome. The Cowboys keep it close, but ultimately fall to the Ravens, 23-20. Matt Holleran (2-0) Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry against the Cowboys spotty run defense is a recipe for disaster. I see this game playing out very similarity to Dallas matchup at Detroit last season. The Cowboys’ high-powered offense keeps them in this game for three quarters, but the defenses inability to get stops late sinks their chances. Give me the Ravens, 38-27. Mike Poland (1-1) There are plenty of reasons to be positive and believe Dallas can leave Brazil with another win. The biggest one is Dak Prescott. After the offense finally found its rhythm against Washington, Prescott looked completely in control, and when Dallas can protect him and allow CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Jake Ferguson to work across the field, this offense becomes extremely difficult to defend. Baltimore has talent everywhere, but its defense has already shown that it can give up long drives and big plays. If Dallas starts quickly and keeps Prescott out of obvious passing situations, there should be opportunities all afternoon. Follow the Saints blueprint last week with quick passing and that keeps the chains moving. Dallas wins 34-28

title: College football’s top Cowboys draft targets in Week 4
summary: We are once again taking a look at potential draft targets for the Cowboys in 2027 from the biggest games on Saturday. Texas at Tennessee Texas begins SEC play with a difficult trip to Neyland Stadium, where both teams enter with 3-0 records. The Longhorns have already beaten Ohio State, while Tennessee has scored at […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are once again taking a look at potential draft targets for the Cowboys in 2027 from the biggest games on Saturday. Texas at Tennessee Texas begins SEC play with a difficult trip to Neyland Stadium, where both teams enter with 3-0 records. The Longhorns have already beaten Ohio State, while Tennessee has scored at least 42 points in every game. This will be the first meeting between the programs on either school’s campus and should give several highly rated prospects their strongest test since the opening weeks of the season. Key Dallas Targets: Texas: Cam Coleman, Wide Receiver Coleman arrived at Texas after two seasons with Auburn and has quickly become one of Arch Manning’s most dangerous targets. So far this season he has 11 receptions for 178 yards and four touchdowns through three games. His average of 16.2 yards per catch shows that Texas is using him to create explosive plays rather than relying on short, easy completions. His size and body control stand out immediately. Coleman can reach passes outside his frame and win against tight coverage. He also accelerates well for a taller receiver, allowing him to threaten defensive backs deep before stopping or breaking across the middle. Four touchdowns from only 11 catches show how dangerous he already is near the end zone. Why The Cowboys Care Coleman could give Dallas another large target without removing speed from the offense. His ability to win near the sideline would fit Dak Prescott’s willingness to give trusted receivers opportunities against one-on-one coverage. Putting Coleman opposite Lamb could also make it much harder for defenses to concentrate their coverage on one side of the formation. He is likely to receive first-round consideration. Tennessee: Arion Carter, Linebacker Carter returned for his senior season after withdrawing from the 2026 NFL Draft. He led the SEC with 7.6 tackles per game last year, finishing with 76 tackles and 1.5 sacks in ten appearances. He has accumulated 161 tackles and 13.5 tackles for loss during his Tennessee career. Carter plays with speed and arrives at the ball with force. He reads running plays quickly, moves through traffic without taking a wide route and has enough acceleration to close on a runner before a small opening becomes a large gain. He can also attack as a blitzer or move into short-zone coverage. His main test will be showing greater control when changing direction against quicker players in space. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas handed rookie Jaishawn Barham the green-dot helmet and the responsibility of communicating the defensive calls, but one young linebacker does not complete the position. DeMarvion Overshown has experienced major injury problems and has shown availability is an issue. That makes linebacker a big need next year. Carter would bring experience, physical tackling and leadership to the middle of the defense. He could play alongside Barham on early downs, help defend mobile quarterbacks and add value as a blitzer. His ability to remain on the field in more than one defensive package would make him more valuable than a linebacker limited to stopping the run. Oregon at USC Oregon travels to the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum for a major Big Ten game against unbeaten USC. The Trojans are scoring more than 40 points per game, while Oregon’s defense is allowing only 110.7 rushing yards per contest. Key Dallas Targets: Oregon: Matayo Uiagalelei, Edge Rusher Uiagalelei is a 6-foot-5, 272-pound defender with the size to play with his hand on the ground or from a standing position. He recorded 34 tackles, 9.5 tackles for loss, six sacks, four pass breakups and two forced fumbles in 2025. He has added another two sacks through Oregon’s opening three games this season. His combination of length and power makes him difficult for offensive tackles to control. Uiagalelei can extend his arms into a blocker’s chest and then decide whether to attack inside or around the edge. He is also strong enough to hold his position against the run rather than becoming a player who only helps on passing downs. Why The Cowboys Care Uiagalelei has the frame to fit Dallas’ defensive front without becoming a weakness against the run. He could rotate initially and even move inside in certain passing situations. His versatility would allow the Christian Parker to change the front without replacing several players. USC: Elijah Paige, Offensive Tackle Paige is a 6-foot-7, 315-pound left tackle who has been starting for USC since the end of his true freshman season. He earned Freshman All-American recognition in 2024 and returned healthy in 2026 after surgery ended his previous season early. His length makes it difficult for pass rushers to take the shortest route towards the quarterback. Paige can make contact before the defender reaches his body and use his size to guide speed rushers beyond the pocket. USC’s experienced offensive line allowed only one sack per game in 2025, and Paige remains one of its most important pieces. Why The Cowboys Care Offensive tackle will come up here every week until Terence Steele gives us a reason not to. The Cowboys need more competition and better depth around Dak Prescott, especially after injuries have already tested the offensive line this year. Paige has starting experience at left tackle, but his size could allow a team to test him on either side. Dallas could bring him in as competition rather than forcing him into the lineup immediately, giving the coaching staff time to improve his balance and hand placement.

title: Cowboys vs. Ravens: Matchups to watch in Week 3
summary: Both the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens hit the road this week, traveling all the way to Brazil for this Week 3 matchup. Although they are thousand miles from home, this is technically a home game for America’s Team, but we shouldn’t expect any kind of home field advantage. It could be quite the opposite […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images Both the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens hit the road this week, traveling all the way to Brazil for this Week 3 matchup. Although they are thousand miles from home, this is technically a home game for America’s Team, but we shouldn’t expect any kind of home field advantage. It could be quite the opposite with questionable field conditions. Anyway you want to look at a this is a tough matchup for the Cowboys. The Ravens are one of the better teams in the league despite losing to the Saints a week ago. This is a game chock-full of matchups that could sway the outcome of the game one way or another. Below we discuss which ones we will be watching closely. Cowboys’ run defense vs. Ravens’ rushing attack The Cowboys made an effort to improve their run defense this offseason by bringing in Christian Parker and outside players to help, but as of yet there hasn’t been any sign things have changed. In fact, they are still currently one of the worst against the run in the league, allowing 173.5 yards per game, ranking 30 th in the league. That doesn’t exactly inspire much confidence they’ll be able to contain Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry this week. They both headline the fifth-ranked rushing attack so far this year and are averaging 83.5 rushing yards per game. WR CeeDee Lamb vs. Ravens’ CBs CeeDee Lamb is coming off a huge game last week against the Commanders and will certainly demand attention from the Ravens cornerbacks in this Week 3 matchup. The last time these two teams played No. 88 had just four catches for 67 yards with no touchdowns and a fumble. This time around Baltimore can’t focus the majority of their attention on him though with George Pickens having to be factored in. Moving Lamb around could create favorable matchups for him or provide one-on-one opportunities for Pickens. It could be a win-win. Cowboys’ pass rush vs. Ravens’ OL This is a matchup that could heavily favor the Cowboys considering the Ravens OL is currently allowing a 44% pressure rate through the first two weeks, ranking third-worst in the NFL. The interior of their OL is particularly vulnerable after letting All-Pro C Tyler Linderbaum walk in free agency. Neither Kenny Clark or Quinnen Williams have played up to their typical standards so far, but could both excel in this matchup. And, Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence could find some success as tackle Ronnie Stanley will be out.

title: Cowboys news: Dallas wants to set the tone against Baltimore

full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images The Cowboys are gearing for a formidable test versus the Ravens in Brazil, and their focus is to come out strong and play well. Both teams are dealing with injuries to key players, but a few of them on the Baltimore side could swing the momentum to Dallas. When comes to preparation for this contest, the Cowboys are keeping a tight ship around the team. Field concerns have been brought up for the game, but Dallas is unphased about how things will play out. Dak Prescott, Cowboys want to ‘be the aggressors’ vs. Ravens in Rio – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys face a big challenge on both sides of the ball against the Ravens in Week 3. They want to control the pace of the game and have it played on their terms. “We’re excited about our game plan, we’ve got answers for whatever they’re going to do. He had missed multiple practices during the week but returned to some individual drills on Friday, suggesting he could also be a game-time decision. 5 final thoughts about Cowboys-Ravens: Facing Derrick Henry, getting Quinnen Williams going – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Both the Cowboys and Ravens are looking to improve to 2-1. Jerry Jones Admits Ravens Are ‘Bad Matchup’ For Cowboys & Dallas’ Fatal Flaw Prove Why – Mike Moraitis, SI.com Cowboys’ owner Jerry Jones made his weekly appearance on the radio on Friday. When speaking about playing the Ravens, he’s sees them as a tough opponent. Jones was a guest on 105.3 The Fan on Friday morning and wasn’t shy about pointing out how tough things could be for the Cowboys this Sunday in Brazil against the 1-1 Ravens . “That’s a bad matchup. We got our work cut out for us. title: Ultimate Fan: Inside linebackers will be the key to beating L.A.
summary: WHEW! Starting 0-2 would not have been the end of the world (obviously) but going 1-1 sure feels a lot better as the Broncos host the Rams this Sunday night, a team many analysts believed (and still believe) to be a heavy favorite for Super Bowl champion. But the Broncos, and our UFGer, intend to […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 7: Justin Strnad (40) and Alex Singleton (49) of the Denver Broncos celebrates after bringing down Cam Ward (1) of the Tennessee Titans during the third quarter at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, September 7, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) WHEW! Starting 0-2 would not have been the end of the world (obviously) but going 1-1 sure feels a lot better as the Broncos host the Rams this Sunday night, a team many analysts believed (and still believe) to be a heavy favorite for Super Bowl champion. But the Broncos, and our UFGer, intend to show the world that the Rams ain’t all that — at least not in Denver. Both teams will be missing key players — Jonah Coleman for Denver and Puka Nacua for LA — and both teams will be looking to get on the good side of a 1-1 start. DNVRNortwoods is confident that’s going to be the Broncos, and I’m with him. Mile High in prime time will be too much for those pretty boys in LA. Plus, with hype man Malcolm Roach out there, how can we lose? you to your friends everyday 😤 @broncos pic.twitter.com/FeQzBxEjky — NFL (@NFL) September 24, 2026 Week 3: Rams at Broncos MHR – Now that’s better. A win! It wasn’t necessarily the most dominant but wasn’t “ugly” either. How did you feel watching the Broncos beat a very good Jaguars team? DNVRNortwoods: Winning feels great! Nobody looks back after winning a Super Bowl and worries about what kind of win each week was. As a fan this win was extra sweet! Redemption from last year, redemption from an atrocious Week 1. Nothing feels better than a get-right win… especially over a small market team. MHR – With the win over the Jaguars in a fourth-quarter rally, Bo Nix has led a league-leading nine 4thQ comebacks. As fun as that is, is it sustainable? And because I’m sure you’re going to say no, tell me why it’s not. DNVRNortwoods: For the fanbase and my cardiovascular health it’s most definitely not sustainable. Logic would dictate this isn’t sustainable, but let’s have some fun here – eff logic! The Broncos CAN sustain the 4thQ comebacks. Why, you ask? BO…. FREAKING… NIX!!! Haha okay now that the blue and orange flu is over with, I do think looking at the schedule this year, and the pure grit and makeup of this team, it can be sustained. It’s a perfect storm – TOUGH opponents making up the rest of the schedule, Bo Nix (who I think might actually be from Antarctica with that much ice in his veins), a defense that will be a top 3 unit, new play caller still getting in his rhythm. If Denver is going to have a good season, these fourth-quarter comebacks will have to be sustained. MHR – The Broncos’ defense last week made a huge improvement over Week 1 (though that wouldn’t have been tough given their abysmal showing on MNF) but this is the Rams offense we’re talking about. In general terms, who wins this – the Broncos D or the Rams’ O? DNVRNortwoods: That will be decided by the performance of Strnad and Singleton. I think they rise to the occasion and the Denver D edges out Rams’ O. The entire defense needs to show up, and I think they will. PS2 will do PS2 things; Sack Allen and Nik are going to do their things. If I’m McVay, I’m attacking those middle linebackers early and often, so it will come down to those two. MHR – Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay make a dangerous combination. What’s the best way for Vance Joseph to disrupt their offense – bring pressure? disguise coverage? Triple team Davante Adams? DNVRNortwoods: I think PS2 will do his PS2 thing and we won’t hear much from Adams, so let’s call that “double” coverage. I think the way we win is showing a lot of Mug looks on the line to disguise what our linebackers are doing. Strnad and Singleton better be quick, find out the right depths on their drops, and be in a position to stop the run early and often. I really think this game will come down to how the middle of the field, 10 yards and in is won. Vance is really good at hiding his looks and mixing things up, so let’s see that translate to that small area of the field where LA wants to exploit. MHR – Both of these teams had terrible Week 1 showings followed by nice bounce-back Week 2s. Now they both look to create momentum with a prime-time victory in Week 3. Between the crowd and the altitude, how much of a factor could the home field advantage be for Denver? DNVRNortwoods: 20-7 at home under Sean Peyton, 14-3 at home with Bo Nix, 8-3 when underdogs at home over the last 5 years… There’s no home field advantage like Mile High (I wish I was there for any game this year). May the odds forever be in our favor! MHR – Davante Adams is coming off a 195-yard, two-touchdown performance. How much of a threat do you think he will pose to Denver, specifically Pat Surtain II? If Puca Nacua is playing, how confident are you in Riley Moss to stop either one of those receivers? DNVRNortwoods: I think at the end of the season when this team is hoisting up the Lombardi the story of the season is going to be redemption. I think Sean Peyton has “he too young, he ain’t there! He’s not there yet! He’s not there yet!” playing on repeat in the building. PS2 is going to have a game where he can (but he’s a class act and won’t) say “he’s too old, he ain’t there anymore, he’s past his prime.” I think Riley Moss is playing some of the best ball at his position in the league. For all his issues last year, he’s earning that payday! If LA wins this game it won’t be by exposing the boys in the back. #BroncosCountry , bring the noise this Sunday 🗣️ @snakestakes & @NathanSerious break down the impact of crowd noise on a brand-new Outside The Pocket » https://t.co/hEtbneIoyz pic.twitter.com/eh0sLjEs1n — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 25, 2026 MHR – Despite Adams’ big night against the Giants, it was LA’s run game that probably had the biggest impact on their opponent. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 164 yards on the ground. How confident are you in Denver’s run defense to keep those two from rolling? DNVRNortwoods: I think they cleaned a lot up from week 1. That being said, we have a lot of room to grow. It’ll all come down again to the ILBs and how Roach, Innie, and Jones play. Let’s say I’m at a 6.5/10. MHR – Bo Nix looked better last week, but it was still a slow start for the offense (something that has become Denver’s M.O. too often). Can the offense afford a slow start against this Rams’ defense, led by 82-year-old Aaron Donald? DNVRNortwoods: haha, an 82-year-old Donald is better than 80% of 22 to 32-year-old DTs. But no Denver can’t afford anymore slow starts (neither can the fans). The team will need all the advantages at their disposal. Fast start to score points and put the pressure on LA, fast start to keep the fans ROARING! All around we need to start off on the right foot. MHR – The Broncos’ running backs are already taking too many turns on the injury report, which does not bode well against this defense. How confident are you in one (or three?) of these guys being able to have a big day with the run game. DNVRNortwoods: 9.5/10. As long as we have a little thunder (JK or Coleman) and lightning (Harvey) the run game should come together and be electric. It has to be… MHR – It was amazing to see Jaylen Waddle have the kind of game in Week 2 that we all expected in Week 1. Better late than never. Can he be the X-factor this week again for the Broncos offense? What about Courtland Sutton’s role? In general, how are you feeling about the WR and TE rooms for Denver? DNVRNortwoods: I’m not concerned. Again Davis Webb has called 8 quarters of meaningful football in his career…. 8! For reference Sean Payton has called ~1,248. Waddle is going to continue to be a difference maker here. Court is going to keep being Court – a class act, professional, team-first guy, and when his number is called he’s going to ball out and deliver. Overall I think the guys catching the ball are better prepared and will be better utilized…

They had an open roster spot available after placing rookie running back Jonah Coleman on the short-term IR due to a high ankle sprain. Klis is also reporting that the Broncos […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 28: Kolbe Katsis (81) of the Denver Broncos warms up before the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 28, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are signing veteran long snapper Mitchell Fraboni from their practice squad to their 53-man roster. They had an open roster spot available after placing rookie running back Jonah Coleman on the short-term IR due to a high ankle sprain. Klis is also reporting that the Broncos are elevating veteran fullback Adam Prentice and rookie wide receiever/returner Kolbe Katsis from the practice squad. Per wire, Broncos are promoting long-snapper Mitch Fraboni from their practice squad to 53-man roster. Denver also elevating FB Adam Prentice for third and final time and also elevating undrafted rookie kickoff returner Kolbe Katsis as Marvin Mims is questionable with foot injury… — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) September 26, 2026 The Broncos had to make room for Fraboni and Prentice on the 53-man roster after this week, with them hitting the three-game max of practice squad elevations this week anyways, so it made sense to add one of them to the 53-man roster. They will have to open up a 53-man roster spot for Prentice this week if they want to use him moving forward. Fraboni and Prentice, who did not have to go through waivers, were added to the practice squad during final cuts to allow the Broncos to keep a few extra players on their 53-man roster. They would then elevate them a max three times before adding them back to the 53-man roster. We have seen them use this roster gymnastics in the past, and it is likely something they will continue to do moving forward With All-Pro returner/wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. listed as questionable, undrafted rookie Kolbe Katsis will get the nod this week. The explosive rookie showcased his return skills throughout the summer, training camp, and the preseason, and could make his debut on Sunday Night Football vs. the Los Angeles Rams. This is a big opportunity for Katsis to prove he belongs on the Broncos roster. Marvin Mims is in the final year of his deal, and Katsis could show that he can be their returner of the future with a big performance vs. the Rams on primetime. It is possible we see all three of these players play key roles on Sunday Night. Fraboni as the long snapper, Prentice as the starting fullback, lead blocker, short-yardage specialist, and special teams contributor, and undrafted rookie Kolbe Katsis as the Broncos’ kick/punt returner.

title: Broncos place rookie RB Jonah Coleman on the short-term IR due to a high-ankle sprain
summary: Well, this sucks. According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Denver Broncos are placing rookie running back Jonah Coleman on the short-term IR due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered during their Week 2 victory over the Jaguars. Schefter states that Coleman is only expected to miss the mandatory 4 games and […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, this sucks. According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Denver Broncos are placing rookie running back Jonah Coleman on the short-term IR due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered during their Week 2 victory over the Jaguars. Schefter states that Coleman is only expected to miss the mandatory 4 games and is expected back for their game vs. the Arizona Cardinals in late October. Source: With a high-ankle sprain, Broncos RB Jonah Coleman now will miss the next few games and be placed on short-term injured reserve today. Coleman is expected back for the Broncos’ game against the Cardinals in late October. pic.twitter.com/sZqFPX8TDo — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 26, 2026 Coleman left the game early vs. the Jaguars, but would later return and have a big role in the offense after veteran running back JK Dobbins left the game with a hamstring injury. He would go on to play through the high ankle sprain, score his first career rushing touchdown, and ice the game late for the Broncos. It was an impressive showing at the time, and now that it’s known he played through a high ankle sprain, it’s even more impressive. After his showing this past Sunday, many, myself included, wondered if Coleman should be named the starting running back. He played well and gave the Broncos a much-needed threat on the ground and allowed them to ice the game late, which is something they struggled to do in the past. Now, Coleman will be sidelined for four games, and now the Broncos must rely on their remaining backs to lead their run game. Veteran JK Dobbins will lead the way and will look to bounce back after a slow start to the season. He was removed from the injury report this week and appears good to go for Sunday Night. Second year back, RJ Harvey missed last Sunday’s game due to a hamstring injury, but like Dobbins, he is off the injury report and good to go. We saw Harvey play a significant number of snaps in Week 1, and now with Coleman sidelined, I anticipate that to continue vs. the Rams and moving forward. Look for Tyler Badie to come in on third downs as a pass blocker, and occasionally contribute as a pass catcher, as he did vs. the Jaguars when he had a 27-yard gain. Preseason star Cody Schrader remains on the practice squad as depth. The Broncos will need all three of these backs to play at a high level moving forward. A consistent run game will make their play-action pass game more dangerous while also allowing their defense to get some much-needed rest. This sucks for Coleman, but thankfully, it is only a four-week absence, and the rookie will be back and likely contribute to their postseason run as we head deeper into the season.

title: 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury and could miss next week’s game vs. the Broncos
summary: According to ESPN’s lead league insider Adam Schefter, 49ers five-time Pro Bowl defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury during practice this week and is expected to miss a “few weeks,” and the team is determining whether Bosa will land on the injured reserve or not. This is relevant to the Broncos because they […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 09: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during a San Fransisco 49ers Practice Session at AAMI Park on September 09, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider Adam Schefter, 49ers five-time Pro Bowl defensive end Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury during practice this week and is expected to miss a “few weeks,” and the team is determining whether Bosa will land on the injured reserve or not. This is relevant to the Broncos because they will head to Santa Clara next week to take on Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers, who could be down their star pass rusher for this key matchup. Five-time Pro-Bowl DE Nick Bosa pulled his calf during Thursday’s practice and now is expected to miss “a few weeks”, including Sunday’s game vs. the Cardinals, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The team is figuring out whether or not Bosa needs to be placed on injured reserve. pic.twitter.com/eQIb7JBKut — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 25, 2026 The Broncos have caught some injury breaks in recent weeks, with Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua both unlikely to play on Sunday Night. Now, their opponent next week, the 49ers, could be down their star pass rusher Nick Bosa while continuing to suffer injury blows throughout their roster. Now, things can change in a week, but it does sound unlikely that Bosa will be back and healthy in a week due to the wording of Schefter’s tweet. The Broncos’ offensive line is considered one of, if not the best units in the NFL. However, they struggled with the rest of the team in Week 1 but did bounce back and perform better in Week 2. They will face a tough Rams front 7 on Sunday Night before heading to Santa Clara to take on a banged-up 49ers roster, potentially being down their star pass rusher. For now, the Broncos have to take care of business on Sunday Night vs. the Rams and hopefully improve to 2-1 on the season with back-to-back impressive wins against two of the better teams in the NFL. If they can do that, they can turn their attention to the potentially Bosa-less 49ers with the hopes of improving to 3-1, or if all goes wrong on Sunday Night, getting back to .500 at 2-2. Since Sean Payton has taken over the Broncos, they have been the least injured team in the NFL, which is a big reason for their success. They need to continue to stay healthy while also taking advantage of teams not being at full strength. Do that, and the Broncos will be one of the best teams in the NFL once again this season.

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua is listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos
summary: It appears the Broncos could catch a major break on Sunday Night. According to Sarah Barshop, who covers the Los Angeles Rams for ESPN, star WR Puka Nacua did not practice for a third straight day on Friday and was later listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos by the Rams. Nacua […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs during an NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images It appears the Broncos could catch a major break on Sunday Night. According to Sarah Barshop, who covers the Los Angeles Rams for ESPN, star WR Puka Nacua did not practice for a third straight day on Friday and was later listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos by the Rams. Puka Nacua will not practice and will be listed as doubtful for the game against the Broncos. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) September 25, 2026 Nacua is dealing with a hip/groin injury and was trending this way all week and now is listed as doubtful and seems unlikely to play on Sunday Night. This is a major break for the Broncos, who will avoid playing star edge rusher Myles Garrett and star wide receiver Puka Nacua. Both players are among, or in the case of Garrett, the best player in their position group, so the Broncos will need to capitalize on this opportunity against a Rams team that will not be 100%. With that said, this is still a talented Rams team that dominated the New York Giants on Monday Night without both players. Veteran wide receiver Davante Adams turned back the clock and had a vintage, dominant performance vs. the Giants, and the Rams still have the returning Aaron Donald and a talented Rams front 7 even without Garrett. Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian will be tested on Sunday Night. Even without Nacua, the Rams and reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford are expected to throw the ball. They also have a strong running game and love to utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Those two things have been an area of weakness in the past for the Broncos’ defense, and I expect the Rams and head coach Sean McVay to try to exploit that. While it looked murky at the start of the week, the Broncos will have veteran starter JK Dobbins and second-year back RJ Harvey back from injuries. Both were dealing with hamstring issues but are good to go for Sunday Night. However, talented breakout rookie Jonah Coleman has been ruled out due to a sprained ankle, which has, for the time being, slowed down that hype train. The Broncos will look to lean on their run game early on and hope quarterback Bo Nix and explosive wide receiver Jaylen Waddle can get them going and have a rare fast start to the game. This should be a fun game between two teams with Super Bowl hopes, and hopefully, the Broncos can continue their dominance at Mile High and improve to 2-1 on the season with a victory over the Rams.
