title: Broncos vs. Rams: 3 Players to Watch in Week 3
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams for their Week 3 gridiron matchup in primetime on Sunday Night Football. In order for the Broncos to achieve their second victory of the season, these are three players need to stand out in a big way tomorrow evening. Zach Allen — Defensive Lineman It was a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars is pursued by Zach Allen #99 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams for their Week 3 gridiron matchup in primetime on Sunday Night Football . In order for the Broncos to achieve their second victory of the season, these are three players need to stand out in a big way tomorrow evening. Zach Allen — Defensive Lineman It was a night and day difference for the Broncos’ defense when comparing their execution in Week 1 versus Week 2. One player who really stood out to me in their comeback win over the Jaguars was defensive lineman Zach Allen. Allen may have not been a monster on the traditional stat sheet, but he was consistently applying pressure on Trevor Lawrence all game long. He made their interior offensive line look bad (especially rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon) and was a key reason Lawrence had a poor performance through the air. The eighth-year pro has been a tremendous player for the franchise since coming over alongside Vance Joseph from the Arizona Cardinals in 2023. There’s no doubt he is one of Denver’s best players, and certainly one of the most underrated defensive linemen in the National Football League. In order to slow down Matthew Stafford and aerial attack of the Rams, Allen’s pass rushing prowess will have to be on display. Over the past few seasons, Los Angeles has done a good job protecting Stafford and giving him plenty of time to hit his array of weapons from the pocket. I’m optimistic Allen will rise to the occasion and cause issues on Sunday night. Riley Moss — Cornerback The secondary performed well last Sunday against the Jaguars. Outside of a few busted plays, their coverage was sound and their starting trio at cornerback did an incredible job limiting Trevor Lawrence’s impact through the air. I felt all of them had some great plays throughout the game. After a few bad plays in Week 1, cornerback Riley Moss came back with a vengeance. His second half interception was a crucial play in the game. It served as a big momentum shift that helped earn the Broncos their first win of the season. The Rams boast two great receivers in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Though it does seem unlikely that Nacua is going to play due to injury. Regardless, I do expect there to be situations where Moss has to go up against Adams—unless the Broncos opt for a defensive gameplan that permanently fixates Patrick Surtain II on him. Either way, I expect Moss to be targeted often. This offseason, Moss discussed the importance of getting stronger and being more physical at the catch point going up against big receivers. He’ll certainly have an opportunity to do that in primetime. The Broncos will need him to be at his best to keep the Rams’ passing attack from taking off at Mile High. Luke Wattenberg — Center The Broncos’ offensive line faces another big test this going up against defensive front seven of the Rams. They have a handful of quality players that have to be kept in check. Denver’s big men up front are going to have to do well to protect Bo Nix. Additionally, they will need block well to jumpstart their running game to have a shot at winning. Through two games, I think there is certainly improvement to be had from Denver’s offensive line unit. Routinely ranked as one of the NFL’s best heading into the season, they haven’t been firing on all cylinders thus far. One particular offensive lineman that I will be keeping a close eye on is center Luke Wattenberg. Wattenberg has struggled with some of his snaps this season. He has also been susceptible to giving up interior pressure and dealing with blitzes and stunts. There will be times Aaron Donald is likely isolated on him in one-on-one matchups. Despite coming out of retirement and not playing for several years, Donald had nearly a 28-percent pass rush win rate against the New York Giants. The fifth-year center is going to need to perform well on Sunday Night Football to keep the future Hall of Famer in check. Denver can’t afford to get beat up the middle if they want to let Nix step up into the pocket and rip it and establish their running attack.

title: Future Broncos: 2 Rising Prospects to Watch in Week 4 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Another weekend, another installment of Future Broncos. In the first three weeks, we have highlighted nine prospects from entirely different position groups. Moving forward, there will certainly be overlap at certain positions. In the comments section, a few people talked about more tight ends and linebackers. That’s why two rising prospects will be on the […]
full_text: BLACKSBURG, VA - SEPTEMBER 12: Virginia Tech Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds (85) hauls in a pass the runs upfield attempting to evade Old Dominion Monarchs linebacker Ja'Mez Drummer (32) during a college football game between the Old Dominion Monarchs and the Virginia Tech Hokies on September 12, 2026, at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg, VA. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Another weekend, another installment of Future Broncos . In the first three weeks, we have highlighted nine prospects from entirely different position groups. Moving forward, there will certainly be overlap at certain positions. In the comments section, a few people talked about more tight ends and linebackers. That’s why two rising prospects will be on the radar this week for discussion. Without further ado, here is my duo of prospects for Broncos Country to watch today in Week 4 of the college football season. Luke Reynolds — Tight End — Virginia Tech Oregon standout Jamari Johnson was the first tight end I mentioned as a potential first-round target for the Broncos next April. Truth be told, I wasn’t planning to do another tight end so early on in the season. However, after his dominant performance against Maryland last week and start to the ‘26 season, Virginia Tech standout Luke Reynolds is worth mentioning. Reynolds began his collegiate career at Penn State. As a freshman in 2024, he played in sixteen games and had just nine catches for 111 yards and one touchdown. That’s not impressive production, but it’s worth nothing he was backing up future first-round pick Tyler Warren. As a sophomore, he split time with two other players in a heavy rotation at the position. His production as a receiver went up a smidge and finished the year with 26 catches for 257 yards. He was also a key inline blocker for running backs Nicholas Singleton and Kaytron Allen to bolster Penn State’s rushing attack. A coaching change with the Nittany Lions coupled with many of their key offensive starters going to the 2026 NFL Draft were big reasons Reynolds transferred to Virginia Tech this year. The decision looks to be wise with respect to his draft stock which is now soaring. In three games with the Hokies thus far, he has 25 catches for 265 yards and 4 touchdowns. He is coming off a 12 catch, 107-yard, and one touchdown performance against the Terrapins. It took a few years, but everyone watching is beginning to see why he was the nation’s top potential recruit several years ago. He may not be a top-tier athlete but is savvy finding spots against zone coverage and has the toughness to break tackles and create yards after the catch. Prospects who can move the chains, be a threat in the redzone, and propel the run game with good blocking are in high demand across the league. If Reynolds keeps this level of play up, he should easily be a Top 50 selection next Spring as an early declarant. In my opinion, he is a terrific fit for Head Coach Sean Payton’s offense. Reynolds can do it all. You can catch the junior in action when the undefeated Hokies head on the road take on Boston College for an ACC matchup this morning. Ben Roberts — Linebacker — Texas Tech Last year, readers of Future Broncos were definitely high on linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. Watching him, you would have undoubtedly seen his teammate Ben Roberts making his fair share of plays too. One of the best off-ball linebacker prospects in the nation, Roberts is hoping to build upon a junior season where he posted 90 tackles and 4 interceptions. Entering his fourth year as a starter for the Red Raiders, Roberts is an imposing prospect at 6’3” and 245 pounds. That’s NFL ready size. If prospects who force turnovers are high on your list, the fifth-year senior is one of the best prospects this cycle. Over his collegiate career, he has half a dozen interceptions to his name and nearly an identical number of forced fumbles. Quite simply, #13 is a turnover magnet. For those wanting to see better coverage chops from Denver’s linebacking corps, Roberts really stands out. He was a multi-star athlete in high school and played defensive back. With his safety background, it shouldn’t be a s surprise he touts top-notch coverage skills as a linebacker. That being said, no prospect is perfect and there are a few things he needs to work on. This season, I’m hoping to see some improvement and consistency in the run game. He added weight and strength this offseason to do better at shedding blocks. He has over 300 career tackles, but very few of those have been behind the line of scrimmage. I believe he can do a much better job with diagnosis and his pursuit angles. In 2025, he had nine missed tackles—but his sub-8-percent missed tackle rate is slightly better than average for the position. For whatever reason, I’ve seen Roberts ranked as a Day 3 prospect on a lot of consensus boards. That seems pretty wild. I’d wager a four-year starter that has played at an incredibly high level with his traits and production will be a Top 64 selection in the ‘27 NFL Draft—even with the rough edges and flaws that need rounding out. If you’re still banging the “Broncos need to draft an inside linebacker!” drum, you can catch Roberts in action when the eleventh ranked Red Raiders host Sam Houston this morning. It’ll be a cakewalk game for them, and I expect Roberts to put on a dominant performance.

title: Davis Webb did exactly what he needed to do to get Broncos back on track
summary: The regular season is already flying by it seems. We’re already heading into Week 3 and the Denver Broncos will be in prime time again — this time on Sunday Night Football to host the Los Angeles Rams. For both teams, the start to the season began with disaster and segued into a strong performance. […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Offensive coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos reacts to a penalty called against his unit during the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The regular season is already flying by it seems. We’re already heading into Week 3 and the Denver Broncos will be in prime time again — this time on Sunday Night Football to host the Los Angeles Rams. For both teams, the start to the season began with disaster and segued into a strong performance. In Denver, that first week was met with some serious meltdowns from fans over new offensive coordinator Davis Webb and him seemingly getting outplayed at every turn by Kansas City Chief defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. In hindsight, going up against a multi-decade experienced defensive coordinator like Spags was probably not a great way to start ones career as a new offensive coordinator. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked this week when calling plays began to feel natural to him and he sure wasn’t sure how to answer that one which makes me think maybe a coach can never get too comfortable when they are the play caller. “There’s a learning curve, always, and then I think the most important thing is it’s not plays within the scheme, it’s players,” Payton said. “So you’re constantly moving relative to what you have. I can look at ‘06 New Orleans, I can look at ‘09, 2013, 2017 and you would be like, ‘Man, there’s some…’ But there were a lot of changes too relative to who and I think the same here or there’s some fundamental things that we want to do and yet you also move in the direction of what the skill set allows.” It seems like he just likes to remember the good seasons when he had the most fun calling plays. I suppose that would make it feel more natural when everything is going the right way. That answer did lead to another question about Davis Webb directly and whether or not he was evaluated unfairly after that first week. “Yes, I think every scenario is different,” Payton said. “I think just being yourself in the process during the week and getting to the things that we think are going to fit. I think all those things go into it, but I think in each case they’re all somewhat a little different.” And his response leads back to the whole going up against a guy like Spags in your first game as play caller. Not the ideal situation, but how Webb handled the black eye and followed it up with a stellar performance calling plays in the team’s win over the Jacksonville Jaguars is a huge check in the box for him. Of course, at the end of the day the players executed last week and did not the previous week. As fans we can point to that, but again it would be on the coaches to have the players prepared in the first place. I personally think Webb is going to be just fine and so will the Broncos. title: Detroit Lions place S Thomas Harper on IR, elevate 2 defenders for Week 3
summary: The Detroit Lions’ injury woes at safety continue to worsen, as they announced Saturday that they placed safety Thomas Harper on injured reserve. Additionally, the Lions announced the elevation of two defensive players for their Week 3 game against the New York Jets, giving the unit more depth for the game. Harper finished the Lions […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Thomas Harper (12) warms up during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions’ injury woes at safety continue to worsen, as they announced Saturday that they placed safety Thomas Harper on injured reserve. Additionally, the Lions announced the elevation of two defensive players for their Week 3 game against the New York Jets, giving the unit more depth for the game. Harper finished the Lions game against the Bills in Week 2, but suffered an ankle injury that required a walking boot. When practices began on Wednesday, Harper still needed the walking boot for support, but told Detroit News’ Rich Silva that he was “just trying to stay off of it” and that it “shouldn’t be (a) long-term” injury. Things were apparently more significant than Harper anticipated because he couldn’t practice the rest of the week, was ruled out for Week 3 on Friday , and was placed on IR on Saturday. Harper will be required to miss the next four weeks and will not be eligible to return to the roster until Week 7, at the earliest. Avonte Maddox was also placed on injured reserve this week—his injury will require surgery and is season-ending —and Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph remain on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, meaning that the Lions are now down four of their top five options at safety. So what’s the plan moving forward? For Week 3, the Lions will shift Christian Izen from his starting nickel role to a starting safety role, lining up opposite veteran Chuck Clark. “Izzy’s been working a lot back there and had a full week. And he’s gotten a ton of work and this week a ton of reps, full-speed reps,” Campbell said on Friday. “‘This is what you’re going to do, these are the calls,’ and just dousing him with full-speed reps, and he’s done a good job this week. […] Izzy’s going to be a huge part for us.” As for their reserve roles, the Lions have three potential options, the most immediate being the game elevation of veteran safety Jalen Mills. Earlier this week, Mills re-signed with the Lions’ practice squad to bolster the team’s depth at safety. Mills is entering his 11th season in the NFL and spent time on the Lions roster late last season, playing in three games down the stretch. His familiarity with the defensive coverage scheme should help him get up to speed quickly and provide an immediate role against the Jets in Week 3. The Lions’ next option is rookie corner Keith Abney, who was getting “sprinkles back there a little bit as a reserve,” according to Campbell. While he’s primarily played nickel in Detroit, Abney has the intelligence and ability to work at safety in a pinch. “For a rookie, he’s a pretty dang smart, conscientious, aware football player that’s got a ton of room to really take off,” Campbell said of Abney on Friday. “So, that’s a good sign. […] He just needs reps and reps. But if we need it, that’ll be a guy who may have to go in for us.” Lastly, the Lions also poached rookie Bishop Fitzgerald off the Steelers’ practice squad earlier in the week, and while he’s surely not versed enough in the playbook to get meaningful snaps right now, he’ll be an option in their safety depth moving forward. Fitzgerald is an ideal free safety in the Lions scheme because he can ballhawk from center field and be a willing tackler in run support. He’ll need time to acclimate, but he has plus developmental upside. In addition to Mills, the Lions also elevated linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga from the practice squad for this game. With rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder slowly returning from a hamstring injury and Joe Bachie recently released from the active roster, Ogbongbemiga will provide the Lions with LB6 depth and a role on multiple phases of special teams.
author: Erik Schlitt

title: New York Jets vs. Detroit Lions Week 3 preview: 6 key stats
summary: It’ll have been a long ten days for the Detroit Lions fan base between games against AFC East foes, and they’ll gladly welcome the challenge of taking on old friend Aaron Glenn. His New York Jets nearly started 2-0 before coughing up a fourth-quarter lead to the Green Bay Packers last week. Glenn’s Jets—who haven’t […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 18: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions throws the ball during the first half against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on December 18, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’ll have been a long ten days for the Detroit Lions fan base between games against AFC East foes, and they’ll gladly welcome the challenge of taking on old friend Aaron Glenn. His New York Jets nearly started 2-0 before coughing up a fourth-quarter lead to the Green Bay Packers last week. Glenn’s Jets—who haven’t made the playoffs since Dan Campbell was in his first year of coaching in 2010—appear ready to put up more of a fight than some expected throughout the offseason. It’ll be a good challenge for the Lions to continue improving and should be anything but a penciled-in win. Below are my six-pack of key stats and matchups for the Lions’ return home looking to make improvements from their mini-bye. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Precious Cargo After finishing in the bottom half of the league with 23 giveaways last year, the Jets—and especially their signal caller Geno Smith—have suddenly stopped making the costly mistakes that give opponents the football. Smith finished second in the NFL in giveaways and threw a league-high 17 interceptions in only 15 miserable starts last season. Through two weeks, that has completely flipped. Only two offenses in the NFL have yet to turn the ball over: the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. Creating those takeaways is more challenging for the Detroit Lions defense without turnover machine Kerby Joseph. Still, they started the season by forcing three turnovers against the Saints in Week 1, tying their most in a game under defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. The Lions have now forced three turnovers in four different games under Sheppard, but obviously weren’t able to take the ball away from Josh Allen and the Bills offense last week. Since Sheppard took over as defensive coordinator at the start of last season, the Lions are 9-3 when forcing at least one turnover and a perfect 6-0 when forcing two or more . When they haven’t been able to force a turnover and play complementary football, they’re just 1-6. Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell have displayed a prowess for punching the pill out, but the question remains: Who else on this Lions roster can prove to be a playmaker and take the football away? This defense may not be able to consistently stop the Jets offense—or other offenses this season—and simply force them off the field. That makes generating turnovers imperative, starting against one of only two offenses that has yet to give the ball away. Jettsetting Smith Keeping the Jets grounded will be a challenge. Turnovers are one thing, but the Lions also need to find areas where they can clip Geno Smith’s wings. In three games against the Lions as Seattle’s starting quarterback, Smith averaged nearly 350 passing yards per game alongside a 60.3% passing success rate, 8.2 yards per attempt, and a 107.2 passer rating—all figures that would have ranked top three among quarterbacks last season. One area where the Detroit Lions might struggle to contain Smith is if they remain dead-set on throwing the kitchen sink at him instead of being more selective. The Lions’ blitz rate has jumped from 31.7% (8th) last year to 42.2% (5th) this season, and that aggressiveness could cost them against Smith. While the Packers were able to generate a little heat on Smith late in the game, for the most part, the Jets offense has succeeded when defenses bring extra rushers. Against the blitz this season, Smith is 14-for-18 passing for 177 yards, with a 77.8% completion percentage (4th), 9.8 yards per attempt (3rd), +0.18 EPA/dropback (8th), a 61.1% passing success rate (5th), and a 16.7% explosive pass rate (3rd). The last thing the Lions defense should do is take defenders out of coverage and help turn the Jets into a top-10 passing attack. Their best bet may be to try to win with four up front and allocate more ammunition to the back end. Red-Eye Zone The Detroit Lions defense has had its well-broadcasted struggles this season, and the red zone has been no different. They have allowed touchdowns on nine of ten red-zone possessions, with their 90% red-zone touchdown rate ranking fourth-highest in the NFL. The Jets offense has scored a touchdown on four of six red-zone possessions so far this season, but when you double-click into the numbers, they’ve been even better when the field shrinks and the defense essentially gains a 12th defender with the back of the end zone. In the red zone, the Jets offense has successfully moved the ball with +0.37 EPA/play (5th) and a 60.0% success rate (4th), finding success in the margins by bulldozing its way to a top-three yards-before-contact mark in the run game while also ranking top 10 in yards after catch. Holding Smith, Breece Hall, and Garrett Wilson to three points—or even forcing a turnover—on just one trip inside the 20 would be huge. So far, about the only thing that has consistently stopped the Jets’ operation in the red zone has been itself, with three penalties, the second-most in the NFL. Prior to last year, the Lions defense had developed a bend-but-don’t-break identity, winning situational football in the red zone and on third down under defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. Week 3 provides an opportunity for Kelvin Sheppard’s unit to start taking a step back in that direction. Protecting the Pilot For the third straight week, the Lions defense will face a formidable, well-built offensive line. The banner players are the bookend recent first-round offensive tackles, Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou, but the Jets also added one starter this offseason who caught my attention: left guard Dylan Parham, a player I highlighted as a potential bargain-bin option for the Detroit Lions in free agency and my favorite available guard in terms of value. The former high school tight end and triple jumper moved all across the offensive line at Memphis and with the Las Vegas Raiders, but is now able to concentrate on left guard. Through the first two weeks of the season, he is off to a career-year start. Parham is PFF’s highest-rated guard with a 92.8 PFF offensive grade through two weeks. Parham has always been a strong run blocker and appears to be putting it all together next to Fashanu, while also excelling as a pass protector. He has allowed only six hurries across 78 pass-blocking repetitions without surrendering a sack or quarterback hit, while also avoiding any penalties. Parham playing at this high of a level will challenge Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams, and Skyler Gill-Howard to outperform him and win on the interior for the Lions defense. Shutting down the Jets’ inside run game and generating pressure on Smith up the middle will be two areas of focus, and Detroit’s defensive tackles will have their hands full trying to disrupt the protection around the pilot. Early Departure The Jets defense, now with Aaron Glenn calling plays and bolstered by the reunion with stalwart linebacker Demario Davis and the addition of second-overall pick David Bailey, has surprisingly been much improved through its first two games—even while extending its streak without an interception to 19 straight games. The Jets defense ranks second in yards per play allowed (4.0), tied for fourth in EPA/play (-0.25), ninth in success rate (39.4%), and third in defensive DVOA (-29.7%). They’ve done it while, interestingly, playing nickel defense at a top-five rate on nearly 78% of their snaps, using the second-lightest average box in the league, and playing the third-fewest snaps with eight or more defenders in the box. Even with that lighter personnel usage—a stark contrast from Glenn’s tenure with the Lions—they’ve beaten the pulp out of the…

title: Discussion: Who will be the Detroit Lions’ MVP vs. the Jets?
summary: The Detroit Lions will be the first to tell you that good, fundamentally sound football requires the effort and skill of 11 players working in harmony. That was painfully obvious last Thursday night, when just about every play had one or two players not doing their assignment, and it made the entire team look disjointed […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta (87) makes a catch against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, November 2, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions will be the first to tell you that good, fundamentally sound football requires the effort and skill of 11 players working in harmony. That was painfully obvious last Thursday night, when just about every play had one or two players not doing their assignment, and it made the entire team look disjointed against the Bills. Obviously, in order to turn things around this week against the New York Jets, the Lions need to get everyone on the same page. But even if they do, it will still require heroic efforts from individuals to move Detroit to 2-1 through three weeks. So today’s Question of the Day is: Who will be the Lions’ MVP against the Jets? My answer: I think this could be a big Sam LaPorta game. This week Scottie Montgomery basically said that teams were surprisingly not double-teaming Amon-Ra St. Brown, and they were totally fine just feeding the All-Pro receiver until someone tried to stop them. “When Saint continues to play at the level that he plays at, we will start to see something that we haven’t seen quite as much this year—maybe because of the training camp that Jameson (Williams) had—we haven’t seen as much double (teams) on Saint, which is allowing him to get some one-on-one situations,” Montgomery said. But what he said next is where I’m going with this. Montgomery knows Jets coach Aaron Glenn knows how St. Brown can take over a game, and he’s betting he won’t let him. “I know that that’s the last thing that he wants to see, Saint running around,” Montgomery said. Whether the Jets will be able to contain St. Brown is a matter of opinion, but I do believe that will be their focus this week—especially considering how leaky the Jets’ middle of the defense is. Now, that may open up opportunities for Williams deep this week, but personally, I think LaPorta will benefit most. If the Jets’ best linebackers and safeties are providing bracket coverage for St. Brown, that should leave LaPorta to operate over the rest of the field. On top of that, I still believe LaPorta’s impact in the run game is underappreciated. The offensive line may need some extra help with a pretty strong Jets offensive line, and LaPorta could be the key to help Jahmyr Gibbs break a big run or two that could shift the game. title: MarShawn Lloyd on pace to be one of Packers’ least productive leading rushers
summary: The Packers’ ground game has been bad through three weeks. Historically bad. In three games, the Packers have produced just 146 rushing yards as a team, an average of just over 48 yards per game. MarShawn Lloyd has produced the lion’s share of that total, piling up a staggering 68 yards so far this season. […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: MarShawn Lloyd #32 of the Green Bay Packers runs with the ball during the first quarter of the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers’ ground game has been bad through three weeks. Historically bad. In three games, the Packers have produced just 146 rushing yards as a team, an average of just over 48 yards per game. MarShawn Lloyd has produced the lion’s share of that total, piling up a staggering 68 yards so far this season. He’s a very small lion. 68 yards through three games puts Lloyd on pace for 385 yards this year, and if you guessed from the setup and headline, that would be one of the worst totals any player in Packers history has produced as the season leader. Pro Football Focus has stats on the Packers dating back to 1932, and although the numbers may be a bit fuzzy in the especially old days of football, that still gives us nearly a century of football to look at for context. The contest isn’t good. A player has led the Packers in rushing with under 400 yards on the season 15 times since 1932, and Lloyd’s projected 385 is only the 12th worst on that list. That is to say, there have only been 11 times since 1932 when a player has led the Packers in rushing yards with fewer than what Lloyd is projected to produce. That would be bad enough, but it gets worse. Of those 11 seasons, only one took place after 1958: Michael Haddix led the Packers with 311 yards in 1990. But basically, once Vince Lombardi arrived in 1959, you could put the Packers down for a player with at least 400 yards, and often a lot more. Not so in 2026, though, where the Packers can hardly buy a yard! Most of the comps on the list are from the World War II era or earlier, when the Packers were only playing 14 games a season and offenses were a far cry from the sophisticated machines they are today. Outside of the 1990 season, virtually no Packers fan alive today has seen a rushing attack this inept. But wait! I can make it look even worse. It’s bad enough that Lloyd (and, really, the Packers as a whole) are finding themselves compared to what amounts to primordial football, but it’s worse when he ranks behind everybody but Haddix in one stat: rushing yards per game. Projected over 17 games, Lloyd’s 385 yards would be an average of just 22.65 yards per game. Only Haddix, whose 19.44 per game is the actual worst in our sample, ranked behind Lloyd. Clark Hinkle, the next player above Lloyd on the list, still managed 25.46 yards per game. The Packers’ ground game is indeed historically bad. And it may not be Lloyd’s fault, but he’s certainly emblematic of the team’s struggles.

title: Packers Film Room: Christian Watson gets into the end zone
summary: Last week I joked that we may have a weekly article that simply broke down the Christian Watson TD that week. Since Watson got into the end zone again for the Green Bay Packers – bringing his total to 4 on the season – I guess we need to keep the bit going. We’re actually […]
full_text: (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week I joked that we may have a weekly article that simply broke down the Christian Watson TD that week. Since Watson got into the end zone again for the Green Bay Packers – bringing his total to 4 on the season – I guess we need to keep the bit going. We’re actually going to look at two plays today: the play that preceded the TD, and the TD itself. Play 1: 2nd & 1, 6:03 remaining in the 1st quarter The Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR). Tucker Kraft [85] is in-line on the right, making that the strength of the formation. Christian Watson [9] is in a tight split on the right. At the snap, Watson quick-motions under the line into the role of an Insert blocker (under the line, positioned between the TE and the RT). Doing that allows for another blocker to that side. Watson misses the block in the hole (unfortunately, a bit of a trend this year), but the Packers get what they need. They get the defender over that Insert position flying downhill to get into the backfield. Though the interior of the line is collapsing, Marshawn Lloyd [32] is able to drive forward to pick up the 1 yard needed for the 1st down. Play 2: 1st & goal, 5:17 remaining in the 1st quarter The Packers come out the next play in the same personnel grouping and the same formation. Once again, the formation strength is the right and Watson is in a tight split outside. Once again, Watson quick-motions into the role of the Insert blocker, and once again there’s a step by the defender to play the run. Not quite the same response as the previous play, but it’s enough. At the snap, Watson releases vertically through the line and breaks to the corner. The defender who has initially stepped to the line ends up picking up Kraft, who is releasing to the flat. The boundary defender is already doing that, so the Falcons have two men on Kraft and no one on Watson. Instead of continuing his route, Watson slows down and settles in behind the flat defenders. Love is rolling out and hits Watson in the end zone for 6. Albums listened to: M83 – I Wrote You A Letter ; Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats – Shapes of Midnight

title: Packers sign guard Laken Tomlinson from Cowboys’ practice squad
summary: After three weeks and three disastrous performances from the offensive line, the Packers are finally adding some help. According to a joint report from Ian Rapoport and Mike Clemens, the Packers are signing guard Laken Tomlinson from the Cowboys’ practice squad. A first round pick by the Detroit Lions in 2015, Tomlinson has a wealth […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 02: Laken Tomlinson #75 of the Houston Texans runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at NRG Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After three weeks and three disastrous performances from the offensive line, the Packers are finally adding some help. According to a joint report from Ian Rapoport and Mike Clemens , the Packers are signing guard Laken Tomlinson from the Cowboys’ practice squad. A first round pick by the Detroit Lions in 2015, Tomlinson has a wealth of NFL experience. At 34 years old, Tomlinson has appeared in 173 regular season games, starting 162. He’s also appeared in seven playoff games, including wins over the Packers in 2019 and 2021 as a member of the San Francisco 49ers. Unfortunately, Tomlinson’s best days appear to be behind him. Though he was a Pro Bowler in 2021, he’s been in the journeyman phase of his career since then. He spent 2022 and 2023 with the Jets, 2024 with the Seahawks, and 2025 with the Texans before landing with Dallas this year. He has yet to appear in a game in 2026. Though not a perfect metric for evaluating player performance, his Pro Football Focus grades show the reason for his diminishing roles. He hasn’t graded higher than a 62.5 overall in any of the last four seasons, and in 2025, he was the 63rd ranked guard (out of 90) among players who were on the field for at least 200 snaps. Hardly a force to be reckoned with, and it’s telling that Houston, hardly awash in offensive line talent, was willing to move on when Tomlinson could be had for as little as a practice squad salary. Still, the Packers have even less to go by on the offensive line at the moment. Pick any metric you choose and their line will rank at or near the bottom. Perhaps even under the bottom. You wouldn’t be out of line hiring a team of archaeologists to dig down into the depths to which the Packers’ offensive line has sunk. It’s been bad, suffice it to say. And speaking of the practice squad, since the Packers are signing Tomlinson off the Cowboys’ practice squad, they have to commit to him being a member of the 53 man roster for at least three weeks, per CBA rules. That’s not going to be a problem, though; with Zach Bako-Bewele assuredly heading to injured reserve, they’ll have a free spot for Tomlinson. It’s just a matter of lasting beyond those three weeks, and it’s hard to see him not being at least as good as the options the Packers have now, which really isn’t saying much, but you get it. If Tomlinson, who stands 6-foot-3 and weighs 323 pounds, can at least provide a healthy body and relative competence, that puts the Packers in a much better place than they’ve been to this point. It’s worth asking if it’s too little, too late, but beggars can hardly be choosers when you’re looking for offensive line help in late September. Tomlinson hasn’t taken a snap anywhere other than left guard since 2016, when he made a 65 snap cameo at right guard over the span of two games (62 snaps in one game, three in the other). The Packers are willing to play anyone, anywhere, anytime on the offensive line, so it’s hardly a guarantee that’s where Tomlinson will end up, but it’s a good bet. There’s no indication Aaron Banks is going to be ready to go any time soon, Jager Burton has moved around a bit, and Donovan Jennings clearly isn’t the answer on the left side. You might as well start with Tomlinson there and see what happens. Things look pretty bleak for the Packers right now, and Tomlinson might not be the answer to anything that ails them. But at least it’s something, and the Packers aren’t in position to turn down any help at all.

full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: An Indianapolis Colts fan holds a sign reading "Week One is a Liar" during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a heartbreaking road loss on primetime to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Indianapolis Colts now sit at 0-2 with a close to must-win game this Sunday hosting the Houston Texans (also winless at 0-2) (-1.5). For what it’s worth, only seven 0-3 teams have rebounded to make the playoffs in NFL history, and only five such teams since 1990. Right now, the issue is on defense. Offensively, the Colts rank tied for 10th in most points scored at 26.5 average points scored through two games. However, on defense, they rank dead last at 32nd, having surrendered a whopping 37.0 points per game respectively. Indianapolis has surrendered back-to-back outing of allowing 500+ offensive yards, which is a streak they assuredly would like to snap with their AFC South rival, the Texans and quarterback C.J. Stroud coming to town. Right now, it’s both the Colts passing and run defense which have been problematic, which makes it hard to shore up either side of the ball on short notice right now. In particular, new starting defensive end Arden Key has struggled in run defense, the linebackers have collectively struggled, and opposing passers are picking on debuting cornerback Justin Walley in the slot. The Colts could also use more pass rushing as a unit as a whole. Only 15% of Colts fans are confident that the team is headed in the right direction (and it’s hard to blame them!): With top football lieutenants, longtime general manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen, already on the hot seat entering the season, where “the sense of urgency has never been higher” was already proclaimed from team ownership, and those seats have only gotten hotter—and we’re only two weeks into the 2026 season.

title: Colts officially place WR Alec Pierce on IR and add wideout reinforcements to active roster
summary: The Indianapolis Colts announced on Saturday that wideout Alec Pierce, as expected and reported earlier in the week, has been placed on injured reserve—which means he’ll miss at minimum, the team’s next four games. Having recently returned from his ankle/heel injury that cost him largely all of the offseason, Pierce re-injured the ankle/heel in the […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 20: Alec Pierce #14 of the Indianapolis Colts before an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs on Sep 20, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts announced on Saturday that wideout Alec Pierce, as expected and reported earlier in the week, has been placed on injured reserve—which means he’ll miss at minimum, the team’s next four games. Having recently returned from his ankle/heel injury that cost him largely all of the offseason, Pierce re-injured the ankle/heel in the late first quarterback last Sunday night against the Kansas City Chiefs. He was unable to place his body weight on his latest injury and went to the medical blue tent along the sidelines, before being carted off the field. Pierce was seen post-game in a medical boot and on crutches within the player concourses. Even though Pierce could theoretically return as soon as Week 6, the initial reports were that a return could realistically be closer to midseason, which could mean closer to Week 8 or 9 for Pierce’s availability again. Through two starts, Pierce has 5 receptions for 72 total receiving yards, having initially been on a pitch count—working his way back from the initial ankle/heel injury, which required minor cleanup offseason surgery. As a potential Pierce interim replacement, the Colts promoted Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from their practice squad for Sunday and signed fellow wideout and special teams returnman Anthony Gould respectively. As you may recall, the Colts signed wideout Nick Westbrook-Ikhine (6,’2”, 211 pounds) as their original big bodied Michael Pittman Jr. possession wideout earlier this past offseason. Even though Westbrook-Ikhine flashed at times during training camp, the Colts ultimately signed veteran wideout Keenan Allen late in training camp, which made Westbrook-Ikhine’s skill-set a bit redundant. Westbrook-Ikhine became a roster casualty, as he was among the team’s final 53-man roster cuts, before being re-signed to the team’s practice squad. However, he was recently elevated and added to the active roster today for Sunday.

title: Could Lou be the first domino to fall, should the Colts’ D not show better?
summary: In a “Heads will roll” season, could Anarumo be the first head on the chopping block? I know that the general consensus is that CIG should be firing everyone, starting with Ballard, but what if we have another game where the offense looks good to potent, while the defense continues to be unable to do […]
full_text: In a “Heads will roll” season, could Anarumo be the first head on the chopping block? I know that the general consensus is that CIG should be firing everyone, starting with Ballard, but what if we have another game where the offense looks good to potent, while the defense continues to be unable to do nearly anything that a defense needs to do to contribute to wins? Sure, Lou doesn’t have a Linebacker that anyone heard of a year ago, aside from Carlies, who had seldom seen the field, but he does have some pieces. Moves were made to allow Lou to feature a strong DB room, with the additions of Bynum, Ward, and Gardner and using day two draft picks on Walley and Haulcey. This is a crew that was supposed to allow Lou to implement a defense that could adjust from week to week and handle a variety of offensive systems, while using a “Mad Scientist” approach. We have even brought in players that played for him, who theoretically knew what the defense was designed to do. Taylor-Britt and ADG have arrived, but those who have came in the past, have already left after being ineffective. The plan was to de-emphasize the LB position. We were told that we likely only needed two in Lou’s system, maybe just one at times. Carlies was supposed to be just the kind of guy that would fit well. Nope. We found out that guys who are good against the run like Franklin and Pratt, are huge liabilities against the pass. So, enter ADG and a couple of premium draft picks. The most premium of these is C.J. Allen, who has a total of six snaps over the first two games. He probably isn’t ready, as we saw it in the preseason, but we haven’t seen much better from anyone else. While I would say he is probably would make mistakes, the bar is not at all high. It would be a little different if we had witnessed a truly effective D, for more than a game or two stretch. Prior to this year, we blamed most of our problems on the lack of a pass rush. It looks a bit better to me, but numbers may not even back that up. Part of the frustration from this comes from our tendency to drop our best pass rusher into coverage. We also still have that hole in zone that makes pitch and catch on 3rd down too easy for offenses. Lastly, his head coach appears to let Lou do as he sees best, given that he does not have a defensive background. It sounds like the entire staff if joined at the hip, but to quote Yogi Berra, “It’s getting late early”. I don’t know what voice you would choose, if you decided that Lou’s was not resonating, but you would be nearly at the “Somebody needs to do something, even if it’s wrong!” threshold. Some of the bad we are seeing is poor tackling and poor angles to the ball. Maybe someone else would offer a return to basics? It has been called a “Must win”, so if not, are there changes coming? Some random thoughts: Keeping with the poor defense narrative, Tankathon has us taking Clemson LB Sammy Brown, early in the 2nd round. I hope Slayton has something for us. He was cut and the Giants are on the hook for most of his salary, so it seems like he might have been pretty attractive for any team in the market. You need to use Burks as more than a jet sweep guy. He had three snaps last game, and he ran the ball on two of them. I would think you lose the element of surprise, if you continue that usage. Houston is not as down as appearances suggest. We know the D is stout, but they are also 9th in YPG at 377. The good news is that the betting public has moved the line +2.5 to +1.5, so there’s that. Would anyone else like to wipe that smug smile off of Strouds mug? They have won the last five meetings, with only the last one being by more than one score, but to look at him, it would suggest that he owns us.

Knowing the party was coming to town I sat down with Scott Barzilla of Battle Red Blog , SB Nation’s Houston Texans blog. We swapped questions and answers about both the Texans and the Colts and what follows is what I’ve learned about this week’s enemy. You can find my answers to his questions here. Chris Shepherd: Based on the first two weeks of the season, if you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to attack the Texans defense, what does your plan look like? What areas of the field are you attacking, what weaknesses are you targeting? How do you beat this Texans defense? Scott Barzilla: I think you attack the interior of their defense with Jonathan Taylor. The edges are the strength of their defense and it keeps you ahead of the chains. If you get behind the sticks it’s going to be a long day. Chris Shepherd: From weeks one to two we saw a big improvement from the Indy defense. Granted that improvement went from lockout replacement players level to simply very bad NFL defense level, in what ways could the Colts defense prevent the Texans offense from righting the ship after a disappointing outing last week? Scott Barzilla: You stop the running game and make the Texans one dimensional. If Stroud has to win he won’t have Nico Collins to bail him out. You can pressure him and create some turnovers. Chris Shepherd: Through two games CJ Stroud is averaging nearly 314 passing yards per game but is only completing 60.2% of his passes, he has also only thrown for 2 touchdowns. What exactly has been the biggest problem with an offense that seems to be passing the ball so well? Scott Barzilla: The Texans have been playing from behind so they have been pass happy. The problem has been a lack of the running game and break downs in communication. Stroud had five drops last week which killed his percentage. Otherwise he’d be having a great season.. Chris Shepherd: Can you give me one player on offense and one on defense that Colts fans might not be familiar with who you expect to have an impact on Sunday night? Scott Barzilla: On defense I’d say we are due for some turnovers so I’d say Calen Bullock or Jalen Pitre could be the guys there. On offense I’d look for Marlin Klein to get a key catch or two with the receiving core undermanned. Chris Shepherd: How do you predict this game will play out? What does each team do well, where will they struggle and what’s the final score? Scott Barzilla: The Texans have won five in a row in this matchup and I’d expect a sixth. It will be a close game but I think a key turnover will make the difference late. Taylor worries me on the defensive end but nothing the Colts defense does scares me that much. And with that, ladies and gentlemen, our week three preview with the enemy is in the books. As always I want to thank Scott for working with me and giving us a a look into what the Houston Texans will bring to Indianapolis this weekend. Here’s to an injury free game. As always, go Colts.
author: Chris Shepherd

title: Jaguars vs. Patriots: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 3
summary: Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! Today, we’re previewing Week 3’s matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and New England Patriots at EverBank Stadium. Question 1: Which Patriots player could further expose the flaws Jacksonville showed in its Week 2 loss at Denver? Dillon Appleman: Patriots DL Christian Barmore can create a similar interior nuisance that Zach Allen […]
full_text: London, England - October 20: New England Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez tackles Jacksonville Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. in the second quarter at Wembley Stadium. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! Today, we’re previewing Week 3’s matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and New England Patriots at EverBank Stadium. Question 1: Which Patriots player could further expose the flaws Jacksonville showed in its Week 2 loss at Denver? Dillon Appleman : Patriots DL Christian Barmore can create a similar interior nuisance that Zach Allen did in Week 2. He can win inside quickly and disrupt the timing of any play, so the team needs a concerted game plan to prevent Barmore from doing what Allen did a week ago: making life absolute hell for the guards. I’m hoping to see more boots and sprint outs for Trevor in Week 3 to mitigate that budding problem. Travis Holmes : Last week’s core problem began with the interior offensive line, with left guard Emmanuel Pregnon and right guard Ezra Cleveland both struggling to handle Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen. This week’s matchup doesn’t get much easier for those two, with Christian Barmore and Milton Williams on deck. While most may key in on Pregnon vs. Barmore, I’ll be focused on Cleveland vs. Williams, who had three sacks in the Patriots’ three playoff games last year. However, both Jacksonville guards will likely hold the key to how successful this team will be passing the ball on Sunday. Gus Logue : Without A.J. Brown available, the Jaguars won’t have an alpha receiver to worry about, but one of their other kryptonies will still be in play: a mobile quarterback in Drake Maye. Jacksonville is generally stout against QB runs but they can sometimes allow a back-breaker in critical situations. As much as the Jaguars will want to apply pressure to Maye, they’ll have to be sure to contain him in the pocket, as well. Henry Zimmer : I’m not exactly sure this Patriots roster is one to be super feared at current, but probably someone along the defensive front, maybe Christian Elliss, could give the Jags some trouble on Sunday. The interior defensive line did not play well at Denver, so I would venture to guess New England would want to keep the pressure up. Question 2: Which Jaguars player needs to start stacking good performances immediately? Dillon : I’m not sure any skill player in the league needs to stack good performances more than Brian Thomas Jr. Last season, BTJ drew heavy scrutiny for his persistent drops, and that problem reared its ugly head again last Sunday. He dropped a couple of routine balls and missed chances to make game-changing plays for Jacksonville. If he can’t start making the routine plays look routine — and occasionally bring in a tough, contested catch — his usage in this offense could plummet, and he could even become a trade candidate before the deadline because there is a certain former Heisman winner who would probably love to eat into his targets going forward. Travis : A clear answer for me is wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. The leading thought throughout Jacksonville this offseason was that 2026 would be a rebound season for BTJ following his promising offseason play. However, just two games into the regular season, we’re back to renewed questions about his future on this Jaguars team. Following a 2025 season that featured Thomas being near the top of the league in wide receiver drops before the team’s bye week, already having two drops on only 11 2026 targets is understandably alarming. Gus : If you think Dillon and Travis are on the same wavelength now, just wait until their score predictions. Anyway. I’ll go with Bhayshul Tuten, because him taking a step forward as a playmaker would be massive for the rushing game. Liam Coen needs to find a way to lean on him so that defenses don’t just key in on Trevor Lawrence and the passing game. So far this season, Tuten ranks third among all NFL running backs in missed tackles forced (11) and PFF grade (85.2). Henry : I want to see a big performance out of Josh Hines-Allen. It’s no secret that he and Travon Walker get the best matchups along opposing offensive lines, double teams and chips but a sack or two would put a great feeling within not just the team but the fanbase. Will Campbell and Morgan Moses should be solid matchups for the Jags. Question 3: What’s a matchup you’re looking forward to watching on Sunday? Dillon : Drake Maye vs. Travis Hunter. Jaguars fans are desperate at this point to witness a splash play from Travis Hunter, and Sunday could be the perfect opportunity. Maye has already thrown four interceptions this season, and the Jaguars’ secondary should have a real advantage on paper. Let’s just hope the coaching staff makes Hunter a primary piece of the game plan so he gets a fair chance to make an impact on defense. Travis : With New England’s propensity for man coverage (48% of snaps in Week 2), the matchup I’m most intrigued by is the Jaguars’ running backs in the passing game against the Patriots’ linebackers. With the potential that Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins both may not play, similar to Jacksonville’s 2025 matchup against the New York Jets, this could shape up to be a game that consistently highlights one specific defensive vulnerability. For me, that vulnerability is running the passing game through the backfield, tight ends, and middle of the field this week. Gus : I’m eager to see the Jaguars’ pass rush go after Patriots right guard Greg Van Roten. He’s replacing Mike Owenu, who fractured his ankle in Week 2. Van Roten, who was a Jaguar for a short stint in 2017, played 40 snaps last week and finished with a 25.9 PFF grade. It’s a great opportunity for Arik Armstead to accumulate some stats, but I’m also hoping to see Anthony Campanile attack with Travon Walker stunts and Ventrell Miller blitzes. Henry : Let’s stick right with Hines-Allen and see if he can’t win his matchups on the outside. Drake Maye has taken six sacks already and thrown four picks. This offensive line is below average at best, which has caused early issues for the Patriots. Coupled with some offensive injuries at the skill position, pressure (aka sacks) from Hines-Allen could see Jacksonville through to a fairly simple victory. Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 24, Patriots 20 Travis : Jaguars 24, Patriots 20 Gus : Jaguars 17, Patriots 13 Henry : Jaguars 24, Patriots 17 What are your Week 3 predictions, Jaguars fans? summary: On Sunday, the (2-0) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road at Hard Rock Stadium, taking on the (0-2) Miami Dolphins. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. First quarter The Miami Dolphins received the opening kickoff and battled through adversity, picking up three third-down conversions. De’Von Achane, on a toss-out […]
full_text: On Sunday, the (2-0) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road at Hard Rock Stadium, taking on the (0-2) Miami Dolphins . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here. First quarter The Miami Dolphins received the opening kickoff and battled through adversity, picking up three third-down conversions. De’Von Achane, on a toss-out left, went 26 yards to the Kansas City Chiefs’ four-yard line. Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill stopped Achane for a four-yard loss, and on third down, Alohi Gilman stopped Achane in the backfield with a tackle for a loss of his own. The Dolphins would have to settle for a field goal on an extremely promising touchdown drive. The Chiefs were able to reach midfield, but the drive stalled, and Matt Araiza punted. End of first quarter: Dolphins 3, Chiefs 0 Second quarter Patrick Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice, who was able to avoid being tackled and gained 15 yards to scoot across midfield and into Dolphins territory. Kenneth Walker was involved again, picking up a crucial third-down conversion through the air on a six-yard pass for a first down. On the next set of downs, the Chiefs were trying to convert on another third-down attempt, but this time, pass rusher Chop Robinson got to Mahomes for a five-yard sack. Harrison Butker was good on his field goal attempt and tied the game at three apiece. Malik Willis was chased down by George Karlaftis on third down and sacked for a loss, forcing the Dolphins to punt back to the Chiefs with a minute left in the quarter. Mahomes found Rice for 19 yards, getting the Chiefs within field-goal range. Butker would drill a 56-yard field goal to give the Chiefs their first lead of the game. End of second quarter: Chiefs 6, Dolphins 3 Third quarter Head Coach Andy Reid wanted to continue his slow pace of grinding out first downs. On third-and-6 from the Dolphins’ 29-yard line, Mahomes passed to Tyquan Thornton, who was inches short of converting the first down. Coach Reid kept the offense on the field on fourth-and-inches. Mahomes, in shotgun, didn’t like what he saw and took off, but was sacked by Zach Sieler for a turnover on downs. The Dolphins would go three-and-out and punt back to the Chiefs. End of third quarter: Chiefs 6, Dolphins 3 Fourth quarter The Chiefs were on the Dolphins’ 7-yard line, facing third down and four. Walker ran a screen pass but was immediately stopped by the Dolphins’ defense. Butker connected on his third field goal of the afternoon. On the ensuing drive, Chris Jones sacked Malik Willis for a seven-yard loss to begin the drive. The Dolphins’ offense managed only 14 yards and punted back to the Chiefs. The Chiefs ran one play before the two-minute warning, and Sieler was able to sack Mahomes for the second time of the day, forcing the Chiefs to punt to the Dolphins with two minutes left. Stone Cold Jones got to Willis one more time to help seal the door shut on the Dolphins’ offensive afternoon. End of the fourth quarter: Chiefs 9, Dolphins 3 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 22 for 25 passing, 182 yards, 4 rushing attempts, 18 yards. Kenneth Walker: 12 rushing attempts, 55 yards, 3 receptions, 8 yards. Rashee Rice: 7 receptions, 73 yards. Tyquan Thornton: 6 receptions, 60 yards. Emmett Johnson: 2 receptions, 9 yards. Travis Kelce: 1 reception, 5 yards. George Karlaftis: 3 tackles for a loss, 1 sack. Chris Jones: 3 tackles for a loss, 1.5 sacks. Felix Anudike-Uzomah: 0.5 sack Harrison Butker: 3-for-3, 56-yard longest. Malik Willis: 7 for 15 passing, 77 yards, 2 rushing attempts, 24 yards De’Von Achane: 9 rushing attempts, 35 yards. Chris Bell: 2 receptions, 39 yards. Malik Washington: 2 receptions, 32 yards. Zach Sieler: 4 tackles for a loss, 2 sacks. Chop Robinson: 3 tackles for a loss, 1 sack. Riley Patterson: 1-for-1 on field goals, 27-yard longest. Next week is Raiders Week as the Chiefs will be at Arrowhead West in Las Vegas. Until then, we will see how it is played out inside the EA Universe!

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 keys to a Chiefs victory over the Dolphins in Week 3
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will play the first road game of the season on Sunday afternoon against the Miami Dolphins. Kansas City enters the matchup 2-0 after defeating the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 in overtime. Miami is 0-2 after losing its first two games by a combined 36 points, including a 35-13 loss to the San […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will play the first road game of the season on Sunday afternoon against the Miami Dolphins . Kansas City enters the matchup 2-0 after defeating the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 in overtime. Miami is 0-2 after losing its first two games by a combined 36 points, including a 35-13 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2. The Chiefs will be double-digit favorites, but the Dolphins will be playing their home opener as their season is already approaching a critical point. Kansas City must match that desperation while building on the offensive identity it established in its first two victories. Here are three keys to a Chiefs victory in Week 3: Offensive key: Maintain a balanced attack A balanced offense does not necessarily mean finishing with the same number of rushing and passing attempts. It means forcing the defense to respect everything the offense can do. Through two games, the Chiefs have attempted 67 runs and 74 passes while averaging 186 rushing yards and 283 passing yards per game. That balance has prevented defenses from focusing solely on quarterback Patrick Mahomes while creating opportunities for the play-action passing game. That was especially evident against Indianapolis. Mahomes completed 14 of 17 play-action passes for 137 yards and two touchdowns. That many completions off play action were a career high. Kansas City’s improved rushing attack is making those concepts more effective. When linebackers and safeties have to respect running back Kenneth Walker III, even a brief hesitation can create openings behind them. The Chiefs used that against Indianapolis, including a play-action pass to Xavier Worthy immediately after Walker opened the game with a 19-yard run. Miami has already shown that its defense can be attacked in multiple ways. The Dolphins allowed Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty to rush for 102 yards in Week 1. In Week 2, Miami committed additional defenders to stopping San Francisco’s rushing attack, and quarterback Brock Purdy responded by completing 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns. He completed all 10 of his passes that traveled at least 10 yards downfield. Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy and head coach Andy Reid should continue moving formations, using misdirection and operating from under center. If the Dolphins play lighter boxes, Kansas City can lean on Walker and rookie back Emmett Johnson. If Miami brings its safeties forward, Mahomes should attack the vacated space downfield. The Chiefs should not decide beforehand that this will be a running game or passing game. They should allow Miami’s defensive response to determine which part of their offense does the damage. Defensive key: Contain De’Von Achane Miami’s offense revolves around running back De’Von Achane. His production has been modest through two games: 110 rushing yards on 31 carries, with another 49 yards on seven receptions. He has averaged only 3.5 yards per carry and has yet to score a touchdown, but those numbers should not cause Kansas City to underestimate him. Achane led the NFL with 5.7 yards per carry last season, finishing with 1,350 rushing yards and 1,838 yards from scrimmage. He also caught 67 passes for 488 yards, demonstrating how dangerous he can be as both a runner and receiver. The Chiefs’ defensive ends must remain disciplined and set firm edges. Achane is at his best when he gets outside, finds open space and forces defenders to pursue him laterally. Kansas City’s edge defenders cannot crash inside and give him an open path to the sideline. Maintaining outside leverage will force Achane back toward the interior of the defense, where Kansas City’s defensive tackles and linebackers can rally to the football. The defense must also locate him when he releases into the passing game, particularly on screens, checkdowns and misdirection concepts designed to get him isolated in space. Edge discipline will be important against quarterback Malik Willis as well. Willis has enough mobility to take advantage when defenders lose contain; Kansas City cannot become overly aggressive while pursuing either player. The goal does not have to be completely stopping Achane. It should be keeping him from creating explosive plays. If the Chiefs contain him and force Willis to consistently beat them from the pocket, they will put Miami’s offense in a difficult position. X-factor: Avoid the trap Everything about this matchup points toward Kansas City. The Chiefs are undefeated, while the Dolphins have lost their first two games by double digits. Miami is averaging only 13 points and 271.5 total yards per game, and its offensive line has already allowed nine sacks. San Francisco scored touchdowns on each of its first five possessions against Miami last week. That is exactly why the Chiefs must be careful. Historically, approximately 75% of teams that begin a season 3-0 have reached the playoffs. By comparison, only about 2.5% of teams that have started 0-3 since 1990 have recovered to reach the postseason. The Dolphins will understand what is at stake. Kansas City cannot arrive expecting Miami to play like a team that has already accepted its fate. The Chiefs should attempt to take control early. Offensively, that means finishing drives with touchdowns rather than letting Miami stay within one possession. Defensively, it means preventing Achane from producing an early explosive play that energizes the home crowd. On special teams, it means avoiding mistakes that create short fields or easy scoring opportunities. Kansas City needed overtime to defeat an 0-1 Colts team at Arrowhead last week. The Chiefs cannot allow another winless opponent to remain within striking distance deep into the fourth quarter. The bottom line The Chiefs must approach Miami with the same urgency the Dolphins will bring to their home opener. Offensively, Kansas City needs to maintain the offensive balance it has through two games. Defensively, the Chiefs must set the edge and contain Achane. Most importantly, Kansas City must remain focused and avoid giving an 0-2 team reasons to believe it can win. If the Chiefs accomplish those three things, they should be able to avoid the trap, win their first road game and improve to 3-0.

title: Rams keeping close tabs on Texas draft prospects?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were one of four teams to have multiple team representatives on hand for Saturday’s college football game between top-ranked Texas and Tennessee. Although the Rams are highly unlikely to be scouting Heisman candidate Arch Manning for anything more than fun, the Longhorns do have multiple day two prospects who could definitely […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams were one of four teams to have multiple team representatives on hand for Saturday’s college football game between top-ranked Texas and Tennessee. Although the Rams are highly unlikely to be scouting Heisman candidate Arch Manning for anything more than fun, the Longhorns do have multiple day two prospects who could definitely interest Les Snead and company in the 2027 NFL Draft. That includes a receiver, a tackle, and a linebacker. 10 NFL teams that are in attendance for Texas-Tennessee: ATL, BUF, CHI, CLE, DEN, DET, GB, LAR, MIA, NYG Bears, Browns, Giants, and Rams all have multiple representatives on-hand. — Jordan Reid (@Jordan_Reid) September 26, 2026 The Rams could be interested in Texas receiver Cam Coleman, a potential second or third-round pick in 2027. Because L.A. traded their first-round pick to the Cleveland Browns for Myles Garrett, the Rams won’t be picking on day one unless they part with a premium player like Puka Nacua. The 6’3, 201-lb Coleman is described as a “Long, fluid boundary target who high-points and adjusts outside his frame” per NFLDraftBuzz. Catches like this one on Saturday show that to be true: Cam Coleman 😳 pic.twitter.com/neIb3JCry9 — SleeperCFB (@SleeperCFB) September 26, 2026 Coleman would not necessarily be as good as Nacua, however. He is said to go down on first contact too often and has problems securing the football. That may not sound like a “Rams receiver” type to me. Texas has two tackles who could be drafted in the top-50 next year, including Melvin Siani and Trevor Goosby. Which of them goes first is still a matter of debate. Goosby is said to be stronger, whereas Siani is more flexible. The Rams are going to have an offensive line issue to address after the season, as four of the five starters are free agents. If Warren McClendon leaves in free agency, L.A. will definitely be thinking of taking a tackle with their first pick. That or a tackle who could move to guard. Keagen Trost is still just an idea, not a player who is even healthy. The Ohio State pass rush wasn’t great… but Trevor Goosby and Melvin Siani are also EXTREMELY good Just 2 pressures allowed combined between them against in Texas’s huge win over the Buckeyes pic.twitter.com/YlyiAgstFV — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 15, 2026 Finally, what about linebacker Rasheem Biles? The biggest need on the Rams defense would be addressed. Biles had 13 tackles, a sack, and two tackles for a loss against Tennessee. RASHEEM BILES COMES IN CLUTCH pic.twitter.com/ymNcZN92IV — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) September 26, 2026 If the Rams are drafting, say, 64th, they might need to trade up for Biles. And it could be worth it. There are plenty of other players worth scouting from this game. Running back DeSean Bishop, receiver Mike Matthews, and linebacker Arion Carter are all players on Tennessee who could draft interest in the draft next year. But if I had to guess, the Rams were there to see the Longhorns.

title: Rams put lengthy AFC winning streak on the line against Broncos
summary: The Los Angeles Rams take a lengthy AFC winning streak into the Mile High City when they face the Denver Broncos Sunday night. LA has an eight-game winning streak against the conference, which dates back to the 2024 campaign. The last time the Rams lost to an interconference foe came in 2024 at home against […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 26: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos shakes hands with head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams after the preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 26, 2023 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams take a lengthy AFC winning streak into the Mile High City when they face the Denver Broncos Sunday night. LA has an eight-game winning streak against the conference, which dates back to the 2024 campaign. The last time the Rams lost to an interconference foe came in 2024 at home against the Miami Dolphins. Miami won it 23-15. Since that loss, here are the results of the Rams’ last eight wins over AFC opponents: Nov. 17, 2024 – at New England Patriots (28-22) Dec. 8, 2024 – vs. Buffalo Bills (44-42) Dec. 22, 2024 – at New York Jets (19-9) Sept. 7, 2025 – vs. Houston Texans (14-9) Sept. 14, 2025 – at Tennessee Titans (33-19) Sept. 28, 2025 – vs. Indianapolis Colts (27-20) Oct. 12, 2025 – at Baltimore Ravens (17-3) Oct. 19, 2025 – at Jacksonville Jaguars in London (35-7) Turf Show Times’ Kenneth Arthur pointed out before last season that the Rams have a winning record against the AFC in the 17-game era . Their record is 17-8, which includes a perfect 5-0 mark against the conference in 2025. LA is 9-1 in its last 10 matchups against the AFC. Overall, the Rams have quite a strong interconference record under Sean McVay, going 29-13 since he took over in 2017, including the Super Bowl win over the Bengals. Broncos similarly have a lengthy interconference win streak on the line The Rams aren’t the only ones riding a long interconference win streak heading into Sunday’s game. Denver is looking to win its 10th straight against the NFC, which caught Broncos coach Sean Payton off guard during media availability earlier this week. While the Broncos and Rams don’t face off very often, Denver has struggled to beat LA no matter who’s coaching. In the McVay era alone, the Broncos lost to the Rams in 2018 with Vance Joseph roaming the sidelines as head coach, and then again on Christmas 2022 with Nathaniel Hackett. Hackett was fired shortly after the game, undoubtedly merrying up the holiday for Broncos Country that year. The Broncos are on a five-game losing streak in the series and haven’t beaten the Rams since 2002. That could change, as Denver quarterback Bo Nix simply doesn’t lose to NFC opponents. Okay, he has once — in his NFL debut against the Seattle Seahawks. After that, the Oregon product has gone through the conference with relative ease, save for a few comebacks here and there. This week’s game is a test for both the Rams and Broncos as the two Super Bowl contenders have a lot on the line regarding interconference supremacy.
