title: Don’t expect a repeat performance from Davante Adams
summary: Davante Adams gashed the New York Giants last week with eight catches, 195 yards, and two scores. The Los Angeles Rams travel to face the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football. Fans and fantasy football owners are likely still riding the high from Adams’ big night; however, we should not expect a repeat performance. The […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after winning the game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Davante Adams gashed the New York Giants last week with eight catches, 195 yards, and two scores. The Los Angeles Rams travel to face the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football. Fans and fantasy football owners are likely still riding the high from Adams’ big night; however, we should not expect a repeat performance. The first reason to be pessimistic on Adams’ opportunity to put up big numbers is the matchup he will face in Patrick Surtain. Puka Nacua is doubtful to play Sunday night. That allows Surtain to be narrowly focused on slowing down Adams. While Trent McDuffie is making the debate difficult , Surtain still has the strongest case as the NFL’s best shutdown corner. Then if we pop the hood there are advanced metrics that suggest Adams could be in for a long night even if Nacua was healthy and in the lineup. Adams has been one of the best separators in all of football through the first two weeks of the season, according to FantasyPoints data, it doesn’t seem to matter whether Adams faces man or zone coverage. He’s going to get open. More ASS data! Average Separation Score versus Man & Zone Coverages – Josh Downs, Parker Washington, Christian Watson, and Dontayvion Wicks in the top right is a thing of beauty For those of you wondering whether ASS is predictive, it is in itself, and when combined with a… pic.twitter.com/dIfeg3PDdT — Kyle (@KyleM_FF) September 24, 2026 But while Adams is averaging 11.1 yards per target against cover one (man coverage with single high safety), the Broncos with Surtain are allowing just 4.9 yards per target . Surtain isn’t the only threat in Denver’s secondary. Riley Moss is severely underappreciated and the Broncos have been better than expected with their slot players. The signs are pointing towards Adams facing an uphill battle on Sunday night. With the Rams’ passing game underperforming through two weeks and with Nacua likely out, LA needs surprise contributors from lower on the depth chart. Who is most likely to step up to take the burden off Adams’ shoulders? Terrance Ferguson, TE Ferguson had his coming out party last week against the Giants. Matthew Stafford targeted the second-year tight end nine times, resulting in six receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown. It was the most significant workload of Ferguson’s career so far. Ferguson is the key to unlocking the Rams’ 13 personnel package. He’s not a good enough run blocker to put on the field in 11 or 12 personnel. 13 allows LA to threaten in the run game while Ferguson effectively functions as a receiver who is primarily a vertical threat. He’s McVay’s ace up his sleeve that hasn’t been fully tapped into. Ferguson may be able to catch Denver by surprise yet. Jordan Whittington, WR Whittington is Nacua’s primary backup, but they both missed Week 2. I’d expect Whittington to significantly eat into the workloads of Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. The third-year receiver is best with the ball in his hands. He can do damage after the catch point. Whittington has been productive when given the opportunity—he’s just usually stuck behind Nacua on the depth chart. I’d expect a relatively high volume of touches for him on Sunday night. The running game According to SumerSports, the Broncos are currently allowing 5.08 yards per carry which is the third-worst mark in the NFL ahead of only the Panthers and Colts. Denver has allowed seven 10+—yard runs while only stuffing nine rushes. The Broncos are averaging 0.13 EPA per rush, which also ranks third-worst. Inversely, on offense the Rams are averaging an impressive 5.0 yards per carry which is good for 10th. LA doesn’t have the volume or scoring production in order to register in a positive way on an EPA basis, although it’s early and the touchdowns can come in bunches. The Rams could easily be a run-first offense on Sunday night. Victory might run through Kyren Williams and Blake Corum rather than via the air attack.

summary: According to the link/story below one of the weaknesses for the Los Angeles Rams is Kevin Dotson in pass protection. full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 10: Kevin Dotson #69 of the Los Angeles Rams is seen during a Los Angeles Rams NFL media availability at Marvel Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to the link/story below one of the weaknesses for the Los Angeles Rams is Kevin Dotson in pass protection. Though Dotson has been stout with run blocking (according to the info below), he’s been less dominant as a pass blocker (according to the info below). It’s so early in the season that trends can seem there, but it doesn’t mean they are, but they could be, so it’s worth exploring. It’s fun. Regardless of Dotson, whether it’s run or pass blocking, the Rams need to do well in both. They have a quarterback who isn’t exactly mobile (though he was moving a bit in Week 2), and they don’t have the type of running backs who can just have bad blocking and make something happen time and time again. The Rams offense needs to click in sync to be as successful as fans and the team want. That’s my take for this team at this juncture, and I don’t think it’s a hot one. Please comment on whatever you want and thank you for checking out Turf Show Times! Rams’ Biggest Strengths—and the Weaknesses Broncos Can Exploit on SNF (si.com) “Dotson is that clear weak spot. He’s a great run blocker, but his pass protection is shaky at best. That is where Zach Allen comes in, who has been getting moved around the defensive line far more this season than in previous years. Allen was largely unblockable against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and his pass-rush ability gives him such a massive advantage over Dotson. Against the Rams’ rushing offense, Denver needs its defensive line to demand double teams, and Dotson is one of the hardest ones to do that against. He is the biggest weakness to target strictly due to his pass protection. “ Rams vs. Broncos: Turning up the pressure | Game Trailer (rams.com) “The Los Angeles Rams are hitting the road in Week 3 to face the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football. Watch this week’s game trailer in preparation for Sunday’s kickoff at 5:20pm PT on NBC.” Rams WR Puka Nacua is listed as doubtful for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Broncos (milehighreport) “Nacua is dealing with a hip/groin injury and was trending this way all week and now is listed as doubtful and seems unlikely to play on Sunday Night. This is a major break for the Broncos, who will avoid playing star edge rusher Myles Garrett and star wide receiver Puka Nacua. Both players are among, or in the case of Garrett, the best player in their position group, so the Broncos will need to capitalize on this opportunity against a Rams team that will not be 100%.” Rams targeting Week 4 return for WR Puka Nacua (espn.com) “McVay said Nacua will not practice Friday and will be listed as doubtful to play Sunday night against the Denver Broncos . Nacua has not practiced since Sept. 17. The next day, he was added to the injury report with a hip injury, and he did not play in Monday’s win over the New York Giants . “If he doesn’t go this week, the expectations are, unless there’s a setback, that he’ll be good for next week,” McVay said.“ Mile High Stakes: Los Angeles Rams Look to Build Momentum Against the Denver Broncos (lastwordonsports) “Also 1-1, the Broncos are coming off a successful season last year finishing in the AFC Championship game after losing to the New England Patriots. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix and the team played poorly in Week 1 losing to the Kansas City Chiefs but bounced back in Week 2 with a victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. While the Broncos are a good team, the Rams must prepare to face another potential playoff foe.“ Rams will elevate preseason standout RB from practice squad in Week 3 (ramswire) “On Friday, Sean McVay said the Rams will elevate Connors for their Sunday night contest. Connors impressed during the preseason after signing as an undrafted rookie out of the University of Houston. During his presser, McVay spoke on the decision to elevate Connors, stating that his work will be on special teams and that the running back carries will be split between Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The only way Connors will see offensive snaps is if Williams or Corum gets hurt.“ Leading the NFL in passes defensed entering Week 3, Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake credit calm demeanor, maximizing opportunities and trust in teammates (therams.com) “For McDuffie, one of those was an interception on an underthrown deep ball by Giants quarterback Jameis Winston intended for wide receiver Malik Nabers. McDuffie also had a critical pass breakup on a Winston deep right pass intended for Nabers early in the third quarter, that, had it been completed, would’ve put New York in Los Angeles territory. “For me, I think of it as DBs, we don’t have truly that many plays in a game that you’re getting the ball thrown your way, and so we always talk about, when the ball’s in your way, you gotta make a play because that’s your one opportunity,” McDuffie told therams.com. “And I feel like over the years, there’s been a lot of talk about just the comfortability when that ball’s in there, especially a deep ball. When me and the receiver are sprinting down the down the field, it’s a 60-yard ball, how calm, how patient can I be so that I don’t scramble and now it’s a PI (pass interference), or I don’t turn my head and now flags are being thrown. Like how comfortable am I just turning around, seeing the ball and becoming the receiver? And I think that’s kind of showing up this year in terms of just really thinking about when the ball is in the air of making a play instead of just being like, okay, let’s have a PBU.” The Rams built an NFL super team, but the key toward another Super Bowl run remains the same in Los Angeles (sports.yahoo) “Down their top receiver and top pass rusher, they still had Davante Adams turning back the clock with 197 yards and two touchdown passes caught, and a resurrected Aaron Donald continuing his streak of never having a game without at least one pressure. The Rams’ depth of star power is real, and it creates a fascinating question about how far this roster can go. A super team that shouldn’t exist in football The Rams are operating like a super team, and that concept just doesn’t translate to football the way it does in basketball. Think of it this way: this is less like the Golden State Warriors stacking talent in their prime and more like the 1996 Bulls all rejoining Michael Jordan on the 2001 Wizards. These stars are older. Aaron Donald stepped away, then came back. Adams has been around the league.“ NFL news roundup: Bills sign WR Greg Dortch from practice squad; Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) questionable (nfl.com) “ NFL.com keeps you up to date with all of the latest league news from around the NFL. Visit NFL.com’s transaction hub for a daily breakdown. READ : Week 3 injury report ” Rams’ Puka Nacua doubtful to play Sunday night vs. Broncos (nfl.com) “Sean McVay said Wednesday that the Los Angeles Rams would err on the side of caution with Puka Nacua ’s health. That cautious approach has equated to Nacua drawing a doubtful designation for the Rams’ Week 3 Sunday night tilt against the host Denver Broncos. A non-participant in practice through the week, Nacua is slated to miss his second straight game dealing with what’s been listed as a hip injury, but McVay characterized as a groin issue. The Rams coach said earlier in the week the ailment is not a long-term concern, and on Friday, the Rams coach told reporters that barring a setback, Nacua should be able to play in L.A.’s Week 4 game against the Eagles. One of the game’s preeminent wide receivers, Nacua was sidelined for six games in 2024 and one in 2025.“ Comment of Day: “I do see this game as a defensive battle. Stafford will probably see a lot more pressure in this one. Don’t throw the ball up like last weeks interception. Need to have a turnover…

Mike LaFleur on getting Marvin Harrison Jr. easier completions: “Everyone's kind of got their role." pic.twitter.com/MG0pIriqwy — Bo Brack (@BoBrack) September 21, 2026 Starting at left out LaFleur, is essentially saying that Marvin Harrison Jr. is just a role player in his offense. He is the third receiver in line and the fourth pass catcher overall. Now keep in mind LaFleur inherited this Cardinals roster from a defensive minded coach. Johnathan Gannon failed in his first opportunity as a head coach with an abysmal offense. LaFleur has no ties to Harrison whatsoever. He didn’t draft him, he doesn’t want to develop him, and he barely wants to give him the ball. Consequently, Harrison is putting bad film of himself on the field because he’s going through the motions. Which is a character flaw on his part, whether he’s frustrated or not. We have seen the practice drops from a lack of focus, we have seen the half speed routes he’s running. All of suggests internally. Harrison is screaming get me out of here. Listen to former NFL WR TJ Houshmandzadeh talk about the Marvin Harrison Jr situation and Mike Lafleur’s comments on it👀 TJ used to train his Cardinals teammate Michael Wilson and says he was actually supposed to workout with him and plans on reaching out to Marv. Worth a… pic.twitter.com/ZsKcb24dG9 — K1SinceDay1 (@KSzn2021) September 22, 2026 Throwing lifelines He simply has too much talent to be this unwatchable. When locked in and engaged Harrison can and will make plays. As a rookie, Harrison caught 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns from Kyler Murray in a piss poor offensive scheme. On the Raiders, Kubiak will undoubtedly scheme up plays to get the ball in his hands in space where he could do great things. Harrison would instantly be the best receiver on the team while still not having to be the primary pass catcher. Brock Bowers expected return to the lineup in week 3 would keep the onus off of him still. The rest of the Raiders receivers would enjoy proper matchups against other teams second or third defensive backs. Providing them with more winnable situations. Further opening up the playbook Kubiak is already dazzling defenses with. What would it take? Ideally, John Spytek would offer anywhere from as high as a third-rounder to as low as a fifth-rounder and possibly Jalen Nailor in return. Since signing with the Raiders in free agency, Nailor has left a lot to be desired. To take it a step further, New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury could help facilitate a trade for Aidan O’Connell. Perhaps Spytek could offload O’Connell, trade for Harrison and still be in a position to either add to his receiver room in the 2027 draft. Giving the 2026 Raiders a legit opportunity with a playoff caliber roster and prepare them for greatness at minimal costs to his precious draft picks.

title: Brock Bowers’ return will make Klint Kubiak’s offense even more dynamic
summary: Optimism is abound, but it’s not quite clear whether the Las Vegas Raiders will have Brock Bowers on the field against the New Orleans Saints this coming Sunday. In what’s expected to be a very challenging road game, having the elite tight end would be a fortuitous turn of events for Klint Kubiak’s football that […]
full_text: (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Optimism is abound, but it’s not quite clear whether the Las Vegas Raiders will have Brock Bowers on the field against the New Orleans Saints this coming Sunday. In what’s expected to be a very challenging road game, having the elite tight end would be a fortuitous turn of events for Klint Kubiak’s football that generated back-to-back wins in the first two games of the 2026 season. While the elite tight end returned to practice this week, it’s listed as in “limited” fashion over the course of the daily injury report, and Kubiak noted in his press conference the team his absence from Friday’s practice was part of the plan . Bowers is recovering from a meniscus trim surgery for an injury during training camp resulting in the the 23-year-old missing the first two games of the Kubiak era — which makes the 2-0 start all the more impressive. When Bowers went under the knife and everyone speculated on his return, I’ve been of the mindset that Week 4 is a good time for him to get back in the lineup as that’s the Raiders’ next home game. That October 4 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs would be about four weeks from when Bowers went under the knife on September 9 (and selfishly, I want to call the that month “Brock-tober Fest”). That all said, what’s clearly not in debate here: Just how much Bowers impacts not only the Raiders offense, but the opposing defense, too. #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak on how optimistic he is for Brock Bowers🏴‍☠️ Brock will also not workout pregame. So #Saints DC Brandon Staley will not know what to expect til the first offensive snap. #Raidernation #checkmate ♟️ pic.twitter.com/xmNJqLsreJ — Optimistic Raider  (@planetraider) September 25, 2026 But as matter-of-fact as Kubiak is, he was straight and to the point when asked about what Bowers’ adds to his offense. “Whoever’s up each week is the guys that are expected to go help us win the game. So, whether it’s Brock, doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter who it is. The goal remains the same,” Kubiak said. Neither offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko nor quarterback Kirk Cousins divulged any specifics on how Bowers can make the Raiders offense more effective. “I think it gives everybody confidence that everybody can go in, do their job in the way we see fit,” Janocko said. “That they can go in, they can play different guys, can play different positions. We can maximize different skill sets in different ways and execute the offense.” “Yeah, I mean, I think anybody, no matter what the position they have as a skill guy, you can use them to attack a defense,” Cousins said. “And again, that’s a little more coaches problem; again, my job is to just kind of execute what they’re designing up, what they’re calling, and go where my reads take me. But you want to have your best players on the field, and I think Brock coming back gives us gives us that.” Forgive the coy nature of Kubiak, Janocko, and Cousins. First, they’re not the types to divulge much information. And second, that trio are no strangers to one another which affirms the first point. And third, when he’s been on the field, it’s quite obvious the impact Bowers Makes in Silver & Black. Standing 6-foot-4 and 235 pounds, Bowers maybe a tight end by position group, but he’s a multi-position playmaker who can line up in any wide receiver spot, in-line and split tight end, and even as a fullback in the backfield. With his tight end size and the speed and sharp router running of a wide receiver, Bowers can out-jump and out-race a variety of defenders. No flash. No talk. Just Brock Bowers tape. 😤 @Raiders | @brockbowers17 pic.twitter.com/EesFFoOvNx — NFL (@NFL) June 9, 2025 It’s such a nightmarish matchup for opposing defensive coordinators that they’ve placed their No. 1 cover cornerback on Bowers in hopes of stopping the 13th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. While former Raiders head coach Dennis Allen — who is now the Chicago Bears defensive coordinator — spoke about being multiple, it’s Kubiak who not only talks the talk, but walks the walk. And the newest Raiders head honcho is all about keeping defenses guessing and exploiting the multitude of ways he can get the ball in his playmaker’s hands. Whether it’s as a traditional tight end or on the perimeter where a wide receiver usually lines up, or the chaos caused when Bowers is in the backfield, his presence alone forces defenses to adapt how they plan to defend the Raiders offense. Instead of being able to load the box or attack the ground game by corralling running back Ashton Jeanty, linebackers and defensive backs get that tingly feeling in their neck when they see Bowers in the lineup. Yes, it may be a run, but getting boat raced by a pass catcher because you stacked the box isn’t an inviting notion. And Bowers’ ability to run an entire route tree and get open whether its short, intermediate, or deep routes is truly frightening. It’s not fun to get beat horizontally and vertically by a premiere tight end. The Raiders have long suffered this being in the AFC West that featured a slew of productive tight ends from Tony Gonzalez (Kansas City Chiefs), Shannon Sharpe (Denver Broncos), Antonio Gates (San Diego Chargers), and Travis Kelce (Chiefs), to name a few. Oh, and Bowers is no slouch as a blocker. He’s an asset in both pass protection and run blocking and when he does finally take the field — be it this Sunday against the Saints or in Week 4 — Kubiak will be able to deploy an even more sinister 12 personnel package (that features two tight ends).

title: Raiders Mailbag: How should Rob Leonard handle cornerback rotation with Hezekiah Masses’ emergence?
summary: The phrase “big test” gets overused in the NFL because every week/game can fall into that category. So, the Las Vegas Raiders have a “significant exam” with their Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints, who have been a rising team in the league dating back to the second half of the 2025 campaign. […]
full_text: (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The phrase “big test” gets overused in the NFL because every week/game can fall into that category. So, the Las Vegas Raiders have a “significant exam” with their Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints , who have been a rising team in the league dating back to the second half of the 2025 campaign. But before that, let’s preview the game with this week’s mailbag! Q: With Hezekiah Masses emerging, Darien Porter playing well in Week 1, Eric Stokes already having one side locked down, and throwing Jermod McCoy in the mix, how would you go about the cornerback rotation? Would you consider trying Porter, McCoy or Masses at nickel to get them on the field more, especially with Taron Johnson struggling a bit in coverage? A: While I like what Porter brings to the table, and he played well in the season opener by allowing just one catch on five targets per Pro Football Focus , I think Masses has to start in New Orleans. The rookie has better ball skills and has already created two turnovers in one start with his interceptions last week. Meanwhile, Porter has yet to record a pick in 11 starts. Plus, it was a pleasant surprise, but Masses also provided some run support with a couple of defensive stops last week. That’s another area of the second-year pro’s game that could use some improvement. Now, I don’t think that means Porter has to ride the bench for the entire Saints game. Jermod McCoy saw the field on two series last week (one in the second quarter and another in the fourth) and ended up playing in 18 snaps, per PFF . So, I wouldn’t be surprised if there’s a similar rotation between Masses and Porter this week, and the split could be closer to 50/50 to see who can be the starter moving forward. When it comes to putting someone at nickel, I dove into that in more detail toward the end of training camp (see the related article below). I’m a little skeptical of how that could work given Porter’s, Masses’ and McCoy’s skill sets. But it’s worth a shot since Taron Johnson isn’t playing particularly well in coverage. Also, part of my logic with Masses is that he can struggle against the run, but he already showed growth in that department. I’ll throw this idea out there since the news about Treydan Stukes being out was announced as I’m writing this: put Johnson at safety, Masses at nickel and Porter on the outside on third-and-longs or in passing situations. With Stukes out, the other options at free safety are Isaiah Pola-Mao or Tristin McCollum, so I’ll take my chances with Johnson back there (LOL!). He has been rotating into the back end of the defense post-snap, and was working with the safeties a bit during training camp. Circling back to McCoy, I’d be surprised if he’s still in the rotation if Porter is fully healthy. McCoy looked like he was spinning a bit last week with a handful of rookie mistakes that didn’t get exposed by the Chargers, but could be something the Saints target now that they have some film on the rookie. It seemed like the game was a little too fast for him last week. That’s fine; it was his first regular-season football game since 2024. But if the Raiders are trying to stay undefeated, the smart move is to keep him sidelined for now. All of this being said, it’s not out of the question that Masses and Porter are the outside corners while Stokes is the odd man out. I don’t think that happens this week, but it’s something to monitor for the future if the young guys continue to play well. Stokes was a shutdown corner last year, but he’s struggling a bit right now. To put it in perspective, Stokes has been targeted 10 times and given up six completions for 73 yards and a touchdown , and hasn’t forced an incompletion through two games. Two of the incompletions were off-target throws (where the receiver was open) from Malik Wills, one was a batted pass by Tonka Hemingway, and the other was the play where the Chargers tight end had PBU on a pass that was intended for a Chargers wide receiver (yes, you read that correctly). Again, I don’t think it happens in the next week or anytime soon. However, if the young corners are playing well, the veteran has to pick it up to justify staying on the field. Q: What do you think is driving the significant improvement in performance on the back end when you consider that a reasonable amount of these players were on the roster last year, and Joe Woods was also on the coaching staff working with the DBs last year too? A: Rob Leonard. I was skeptical of Leonard as the defensive coordinator because I didn’t know what types of coverages he’d run since his entire resume has been working with the front seven. I was also skeptical of the notion that he’d run Mike Macdonald’s defense because Leonard only worked under Macdonald for one year in Baltimore. I was wrong. The Raiders are running a variation of the Seahawks’ defense where there are so many moving parts and complex pattern-matching coverages. On top of that, and this was something I did expect from Leonard, he’s calling a lot of stunts, simulated pressures, creeper blitzes, etc., to manufacture pressure. He got promoted to defensive run game coordinator last year, and Vegas was able to create so many negative plays in the running game because of the stunts and twists the defense was running, which wasn’t as prevalent in years past. So, the combination of complex coverages and manufactured pressure leads to quarterbacks holding onto the ball longer, which gives the secondary more time to get to their responsibilities (a man or an area on the field) and helps the pass-rush hit home. I said this on the post-Chargers Tape Don’t Lie : The Raiders have a pair of mad scientists calling plays on both sides of the ball right now. Q: What can we expect from Cody White for this next game? Also, if the confidence is there, can we expect more resting for Brock Bowers? A: I wish I had a better answer for you about White, but I’m honestly not sure. I thought he’d get promoted after scoring two touchdowns last week, but he reverted to the practice squad. Now, the coaching staff gets one more call-up before they have to add White to the 53-man roster if he’s going to get elevated for a fourth time, so there is still a chance the wideout gets some action on Sunday. However, White only has three targets and has only played 18 offensive snaps in both games combined. So, it’s not like he had a big role on the offense; he’s just made a couple of splash plays. Whether or not the latter is enough for him to get more playing time moving forward remains to be seen. As far as Bowers goes, it seems like all signs are pointing to him playing this week . At this point, I’d be more surprised if he doesn’t play than if he does. I’m not saying I agree with that — in fact, I disagree with it, LOL — but I’m just reading the tea leaves from the last couple of weeks. Q: Do you think John Spytek takes a shot at landing Marvin Harrison Jr.? Especially if Spytek can get Harrison for pennies on the dollar, I’m all in on making that trade. Obviously, it hasn’t worked out in Arizona so far. But if you can get a guy who was the fourth overall selection two years ago who fills (or could potentially fill) a big need for a third- or fourth-round pick, go for it! Look at it this way: round three has been Spytek’s Achilles heel so far. Porter is his best third-round selection but might have just had his starting spot taken. Caleb Rogers, Charles Grant and Trey Zuhn III aren’t seeing the field right now, and Keyron Crawford is injured. Sure, you can’t predict injuries, but Crawford probably wasn’t going to play very much this year anyway. Why not take a flier on a first-round talent who would be under team control for the next three years with the fifth-year option and was a highly touted receiver prospect? Especially since the position is expected to be the Raiders’ biggest offseason need, and if they keep winning games, they’re not going to be…

title: Chiefs vs. Dolphins preview: Kansas City insider look at Eric Bieniemy, Patrick Mahomes, and Chris Jones
summary: The Miami Dolphins host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday as the NFL schedule moves into Week 3. The Dolphins come into this game 0-2 on the year as they try to turn a rebuilding team into one that can compete each week. The Chiefs enter the weekend 2-0 and looking like a team that […]
full_text: GLENDALE, AZ - FEBRUARY 12: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs speaks with Eric Bieniemy against the Philadelphia Eagles after Super Bowl LVII at State Farm Stadium on February 12, 2023 in Glendale, Arizona. The Chiefs defeated the Eagles 38-35. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday as the NFL schedule moves into Week 3. The Dolphins come into this game 0-2 on the year as they try to turn a rebuilding team into one that can compete each week. The Chiefs enter the weekend 2-0 and looking like a team that will be in contention to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl. This could be an ugly game from a Dolphins’ fan perspective. But how ugly? To get a better idea of who the Chiefs are this season and who Miami will be facing on Sunday, I had a chance to talk to Maurice Easton from SB Nation’s Chiefs site, Arrowhead Pride. Easton was kind enough to answer my Chiefs questions, including a look at what the return of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy means for the team, Patrick Mahomes finding his form, and a surprise breakout player. Thanks to Easton for taking the time to answer my questions. You can check out my answers to his Dolphins questions on Arrowhead Pride. 1. Eric Bieniemy returns to the Chiefs as their offensive coordinator this season after spending a year each with the Washington Commanders, UCLA and the Chicago Bears. What have you seen that is different from his 2018-2022 stint as the Chiefs’ offensive coordinator? What has been the biggest change from Matt Nagy’s offense to Bieniemy’s system—or is it status quo since Andy Reid is the play caller? What Eric Bieniemy brings to the Chiefs’ offense is accountability and discipline. He is a motivator by nature. He will get in a player’s face when that player makes a mistake, but he will also be just as animated when someone does a great job. He is always going to make sure the players understand what they need to improve. It is almost like having your dad as your coach, if that makes sense. That is what separates him from Matt Nagy. From the outside looking in, Nagy appeared much more laid-back and relaxed in his approach. Bieniemy brings that fired-up, get-in-your-face style of motivation. Andy Reid is still the play caller, so I do not think this is a completely different offense schematically. However, Bieniemy is a former running back who is not afraid to lean on the running game. Beyond the scheme, the biggest difference is the level of accountability he brings to every player in the offense. 2. The Dolphins’ offense this year must go through running back De’Von Achane if they are going to have any success moving the ball. While the focus with Achane is the ground game, he is a good receiver who can do damage once he has the ball in his hands through the air as well. The Chiefs are a top-10 team against the run early this year, giving up just 90 yards per game on the ground. How would you design Miami’s offensive attack to ensure Achane can find success in this game? De’Von Achane is an amazing running back and, in my opinion, one of the five best in the NFL. In the running game, I would look at what Indianapolis did against Kansas City with its outside-zone and stretch concepts. Those plays could help Miami get Achane to the edge, where his speed can really become a problem. The passing game might offer Miami an even greater opportunity. Achane is such a dangerous receiving back that the Dolphins should use motion and different formations to create one-on-one matchups between him and the Chiefs’ linebackers. If Miami can consistently get Achane isolated against a linebacker in coverage and give him room to operate, he is going to win that matchup more often than not. That would be my primary plan for attacking this Kansas City defense. 3. From the outside looking in, quarterback Patrick Mahomes is looking more and more like prime Mahomes as he starts trusting the repaired ACL in his knee. Is that a fair assessment? Is there something you are seeing that tells you he is not all the way back yet? That is a fair assessment. Mahomes looked much more settled in Week 2 than he did in Week 1. He appeared to trust both his knee and the pass protection more, and we started to see more of the Mahomes that everyone is accustomed to watching. I would not say he is completely back yet. That is something that will take time, but I expect him to improve every week as the knee gets stronger and continues responding positively. There are still some plays on which the old Mahomes might have taken a chance or extended the action, but right now he appears to be protecting himself and avoiding unnecessary hits. He is not quite all the way back, but his confidence in the knee is clearly growing. I think we will continue to see more of the old Mahomes as the season progresses. 4. Miami’s defense—like the team as a whole—is incredibly young and prone to making mistakes, especially when it comes to communication in the secondary. We have seen multiple times already this year where two defenders cover the same player, leaving another receiver wide open. You are the coach tasked with helping simplify the game and make the Dolphins’ defense grow. If you were giving advice on the number one area Miami’s defenders have to execute this week to have any success against the Chiefs, what would it be? Young defenses often struggle with zone assignments and the communication required to pass receivers from one defender to another. I would simplify those responsibilities and trust Miami’s defenders to play more man-to-man coverage with clear assignments: Here is your man—cover him. The Chiefs’ wide receivers have struggled at times against man coverage, so that could also work in Miami’s favor. The challenge is that the Dolphins must generate pressure without blitzing. If Miami can play tight man coverage while consistently pressuring Mahomes with four rushers, that is probably its best chance of slowing down the Chiefs. Miami cannot afford coverage busts against Andy Reid and Mahomes. Keeping the assignments simple and winning up front without sending extra defenders would give this young defense its best opportunity to succeed. 5. Is there a player who has fired out of the gates at the start of the season who has been the biggest surprise for Chiefs fans? Is there someone who is unexpectedly struggling early this year? Nohl Williams has been a pleasant surprise. I would not call his success completely unexpected because many Chiefs fans believed he could become a good cornerback. However, the way he has played on the outside through the first two weeks has been impressive. With Mansoor Delane dealing with an injury, Williams has stepped into a larger role and has done an excellent job of locking down his side of the field. As for someone who has started slowly, Chris Jones has been much quieter than Chiefs fans are accustomed to seeing. I would not say he has played poorly, but he has not produced the game-wrecking performances we normally expect from him. Jones has also been dealing with a calf injury, so that is probably contributing to his lack of production. For now, I would attribute it more to the injury than to his age or any serious decline in his ability.

title: NFL draft prospects 2027: Players to watch TCU vs. UCF
summary: We are on to Week 4 of the 2026 college football schedule. After spending last week in the SEC with a look at some of the draft prospects from LSU and Ole Miss, this week we move over to the Big XII as TCU visits UCF. Kickoff in Orlando is set for 3:30 p.m. Eastern […]
full_text: FORT WORTH, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Jaden Craig #1 of the TCU Horned Frogs looks to throw against the Arkansas State Red Wolves during the first half at Amon G. Carter Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Fort Worth, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are on to Week 4 of the 2026 college football schedule. After spending last week in the SEC with a look at some of the draft prospects from LSU and Ole Miss, this week we move over to the Big XII as TCU visits UCF. Kickoff in Orlando is set for 3:30 p.m. Eastern this afternoon and brings us another possibility to find players who could be on the Miami Dolphins’ radar when the 2027 NFL Draft kicks off in the spring. We are going deeper into the prospect list today, with several day three prospects being added to our review. As we have for each week of the college football schedule this year, we take a quick look at some players to watch for each team in today’s game. TCU 2027 Draft prospects Jaden Craig, quarterback (Grad student) – Craig transferred from Harvard to TCU this year to replace Josh Hoover, who transferred to Indiana. He has this year to prove he can play at the Big XII level before trying to move on to the NFL after four seasons in the Ivy League. He is a good decision maker and anticipates well, with enough army strength to make long throws with the ability to add touch to the ball when needed. He is not a surefire prospect, but he will be a good late-round developmental project for a team as he grows into the NFL game. Ben Taylor-Whitfield, tackle (Senior) – Taylor-Whitfield is a big tackle who can move. He established himself as a starter as a freshman and has been locked into the starting lineup ever since. Playing at left tackle, Taylor-Whitfield could play either tackle position in the NFL or slide inside at guard. He moves well for someone his size and could be a pulling option. He has a ton of potential, but he will need some development time. He is a day-three prospect. Jordan Dwyer, wide receiver (Redshirt senior) – After two years at Idaho, Dwyer transferred to TCU last year, where he caught 54 passes for 730 yards and seven touchdowns as the second option in the passing attack. He moves into the number one position this year, but has been sidelined by an injury through the start of the season. He is expected to make his 2026 debut against UCF and should immediately give Craig a proven target. He has good hands and can be a reliable target for a high-volume passing attack. He could find himself playing outside or sliding into to the slot at the NFL level. He is probably a day-three prospect right now, but could improve his draft stock with a strong season. Markis Deal, defensive tackle (Redshirt junior) – A gap filler, Deal is bringing power to the defensive line. He is probably not going to be a dominating pass rushing threat, but he can eat blocks, create confusion, and bull-rush his way into the backfield. He is a solid nose tackle prospect who can be a rotational player, but he is not going to be an immediate impact player for an NFL team. He is probably a day-three prospect who could slide into undrafted territory. Paul Owewale, edge (Redshirt junior) – A versatile option for the defensive line, Owewale is probably not a pure edge rusher. He already has rip and swim moves and can use power rushes as well. He just does not have the bend and athleticism to put him out on the end by himself and expect to have elite results. He flashes at times, but he does not do it consistently. He is, however, a very good run defender. He can be physical and he knows how to set the edge. He is probably another day three prospect. UCF 2027 Draft prospects Jayden Bellamy, cornerback (Redshirt senior) – A Syracuse transfer, Bellamy has experience and has proven to have solid instincts as a cornerback. He is most comfortable in a zone-heavy scheme and he plays the ball well to breakup passes. He is limited in size, so he could be bodied off the ball by bigger NFL receivers. He will be a special teams option. He is likely a day-three prospect. Horace Lockett, defensive tackle (Redshirt senior) – A transfer from Georgia Tech, Lockett is a massive player who can lock down as a nose tackle. He is a gap-filling, block-eating lineman who can be the foundation of the defensive line. He was limited last year due to injury, so this year will be about building the resume. He is going to be an early run stopper in the NFL, who can continue to add to his pass rush ability. He is a day-three prospect. Dylan Wade, tight end (Senior) – A move tight end, Wade brings versatility to his game, able to line up in the backfield, on the line, or out as a wide receiver. He is a good possession receiver type who can fight for yards after the catch. He probably needs to improve as a blocker to be a true tight end in the NFL, but that seems true of most tight ends coming out of college right now. He would be a day-three option. Tackett Curtis, linebacker – Curtis started at USC, then moved to Wisconsin, and is now at UCF. He started as a freshman at USC but was benched midway through the 2025 season at Wisconsin, leading to his decision to transfer. He is a non-stop machine on the field, fighting his way the ball, especially as a run-stopper. He has special teams value, but could end up as an undrafted free agent signing. R.J. Jackson, Jr., defensive tackle (Redshirt junior) – A Tulsa transfer, Jackson is a penetrating defensive tackle who stands up against the run, but can get into the backfield and muddy the pocket so well. He will likely start as a rotational depth player, but could find himself growing into a bigger role in the NFL as he adapts to the game. He is probably a late day-three or undrafted prospect.

title: Can Kyler Murray fix the 31st-ranked Vikings passing offense?
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are 2-0 and heading to Tampa Bay to face a desperate 0-2 Buccaneers team — and the only crisis in Minnesota is Kevin O’Connell’s 31st-ranked passing offense. While Brian Flores’ defense plays like the ’85 Bears on a budget, the offense can’t crack 200 yards through the air. Kyler Murray returns from […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 10: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings is forced out of bounds by Carlton Davis III #24 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the second quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 10, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are 2-0 and heading to Tampa Bay to face a desperate 0-2 Buccaneers team — and the only crisis in Minnesota is Kevin O’Connell’s 31st-ranked passing offense. While Brian Flores’ defense plays like the ’85 Bears on a budget, the offense can’t crack 200 yards through the air. Kyler Murray returns from concussion protocol to make his first real start, and the stakes are simple: can KOC finally deliver? This week on Two Old Bloggers, Dave Stefano was joined by fill-in co-host Drew Bunting (filling in for Darren Campbell, who’s traveling in Nova Scotia). The show, a Vikings 1st & SKOL production, broke down the Vikings’ Week 3 matchup at Tampa Bay with the depth and snark longtime listeners expect. Key Points in Bullet Points Offensive struggles are real: The Vikings rank 31st in passing yards over their last 19 regular-season games, with a negative EPA of -0.5 per play. As Dave put it: “This team was third in the league for three straight years, and now they can’t crack 200 yards.” Flores is carrying the team: Brian Flores boasts a defensive EPA of +11.9 — the best in football. Drew’s wife Ruby summed it up perfectly: “You mean Brian Flores is 2-0.” Kyler Murray returns: Murray is out of concussion protocol and gets the start. Dave expects KOC to open up the playbook; Drew predicts a conservative approach, saying: “I think he’s gonna take the same conservative approach, and then in the second half we’ll be texting each other going, ‘Can we let Kyler Murray throw it down the field?'” Drew’s 17-point challenge: Drew challenged KOC to score at least 17 points in the first half. His research showed the Vikings have hit that mark only twice in their last 14 games — both with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. Snap count risers: Caleb Banks (20 snaps, up from 16), Levi Drake Rodriguez (60 snaps, up from 34), and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins are all seeing increased roles. Harrison Smith’s snap count is climbing (26 to 29). Myles Price over Tai Felton: With Jauan Jennings out, Price took 50% of offensive snaps as WR3 while Felton got zero. Drew called Price “a gamer” with “a little bit more gonads or onions than Tai Felton does.” Buccaneers are battered: Rueben Bain Jr. and Josiah Trotter are out. Alex Anzalone has been “terrible.” Vita Vea is a disappointment. Drew warned: “Desperate teams are dangerous teams.” Turnover battle is everything: The Vikings are 37-4 under O’Connell when they win or tie the turnover battle. They’re +3 on the season; Tampa Bay is -4. Prediction: Both hosts picked the Vikings. Dave: “I believe the Vikings are gonna win and win handily.” Drew unveiled his new “prediction horn” — and it landed on the Vikings. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Listen or watch to Two Old Bloggers on Vikings 1st & SKOL / Bleav. Flores has this team 2-0. Sunday in purple at Ray Jay is when the offense has to stop being the hitchhiker. If you’re a Vikings fan looking for unfiltered, insightful, and hilarious analysis every single week, Two Old Bloggers delivers. Dave Stefano and Darren Campbell (with Drew Bunting filling in) break down snap counts, stats, matchups, and storylines with the kind of straight talk you won’t get from mainstream outlets. Search for Two Old Bloggers on your favorite podcast platform, subscribe to Vikings 1st & SKOL on YouTube, and join the live chat every week. SKOL! Fan With Us! We have your Minnesota Vikings talk amongst the Two Old Bloggers , Darren @KickassblogVike , and Dave @Luft_Krigare along with our numbers guy, Drew Bunting. Join the conversation! Fan with us at Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL on the Bleav Network @BleavNetwork . Questions for you: Will Kyler Murray be the spark that finally ignites this offense, or are we in for another conservative, field-goal-filled afternoon in Tampa? If Murray still looks like 11 snaps of nothing against an 0-2 Bucs team missing two defensive starters, how long before “quarterback whisperer” becomes a punchline?

title: Vikings Make Several Roster Moves Ahead of Buccaneers Game
summary: Ahead of tomorrow afternoon’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Minnesota Vikings have made a handful of roster moves that we will get you caught up on here. First, the Vikings have signed punter Johnny Hekker to the 53-man roster. Hekker was added to the practice squad earlier this week and will handle the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Johnny Hekker #5 of the Minnesota Vikings punts the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of tomorrow afternoon’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Minnesota Vikings have made a handful of roster moves that we will get you caught up on here. First, the Vikings have signed punter Johnny Hekker to the 53-man roster. Hekker was added to the practice squad earlier this week and will handle the punting and holding duties this week, with Brett Thorson having been declared out with a hamstring injury. To make room for Hekker on the active roster, the Vikings placed offensive lineman Nick Samac on injured reserve, meaning that he will miss the team’s next four games. Samac was claimed off waivers from the Carolina Panthers after this year’s final cuts and has been inactive for both of the Vikings’ first two games this season. The team has also elevated outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and safety Tavierre Thomas to the active roster from the practice squad. This is Van Noy’s third elevation of the season, meaning that if the team wants him to be able to play going forward, they will have to sign him to the 53-man roster. A player can be elevated from the practice squad no more than three times during a season. Van Noy has played 30% of the Vikings’ defensive snaps so far this season. This is the first elevation of the season for Thomas. It should also be noted that linebacker Ivan Pace did not travel with the team to Tampa due to a personal issue and has now been listed as questionable for tomorrow’s game. No word on who would get his snaps if he were unable to play, but it could open up an opportunity for rookie Jake Golday to see his first defensive snaps of the season if Pace is unable to make it to Tampa in time to play. Those should be the final moves for the Vikings ahead of Sunday’s game. If they do anything else, we will pass that news along to you as soon as we are able.

title: Minnesota Vikings Week 3 Rune Reading
summary: A Quick Synopsis The Minnesota Vikings are going into Week 3 with two major victories over divisional opponents. Hopefully, after Sunday’s matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, our favorite football team is 3-0. On another note, the divisional rival Green Bay Packers were absolutely embarrassed by the 0-2 Atlanta Falcons, at home, on international livestream […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Carson Wentz #11 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts after a sack by the Chicago Bears during the second quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images A Quick Synopsis The Minnesota Vikings are going into Week 3 with two major victories over divisional opponents. Hopefully, after Sunday’s matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, our favorite football team is 3-0. On another note, the divisional rival Green Bay Packers were absolutely embarrassed by the 0-2 Atlanta Falcons, at home, on international livestream (lol). I have to say I am LOVING this new era of Packer football. The years of Hall of Fame quarterbacks are over! I foresee a fired head coach in the near future. In week 1, the Vikings were able to hang in the game long enough for the Packers to do Packer things and blow a lead to end up losing by 17 points. In week 2, the Vikings reigned victorious on a drenched Soldier Field with a 9-3 field goal bonanza extravaganza. Minnesota did this with backup quarterback Carson Wentz. Divisional wins are always important, especially early in the season, when the division is known as one of the most competitive in football. However, Green Bay’s abysmal performance on Thursday night has me wondering: are the Vikings actually good, or have we played weak opponents? Only being two games into the season, it is difficult to know whether the current path is sustainable. I think this defense is legitimately a top-tier unit. After showing weakness in game one against long passes to Christian Watson, Flores really clamped down, and Minnesota closed out the home opener holding Green Bay to zero points in the second half. If we ignore the first half of that game, the Vikings are looking great. We know what this defense is capable of. What we still don’t know is how effective this offense can truly be with Kyler Murray behind center. We have so far seen an offense that is committed to the run, which has helped with the time of possession battle and, I believe, has been a huge contributor to the success in these first two wins. However, with Aaron Jones banged up, and in the later phase of an NFL running back career, I anticipate we will see significantly more passing plays and Kyler scrambling for a million yards. Jones needs a break this week, and if Deejay Dallas and Demond Claiborne are the alternative options to hand off to, I’d say passing the ball is the best option. Shall We Consult the Gods? Now that I’ve gotten some of my thoughts and feelings out of the way, it’s time to base the rest of this piece on the eternal wisdom of Odin and Co. Last week was the first rune reading I did for the Minnesota Vikings, where I asked if the Vikings have a path to the playoffs . The answer that I received was a rousing: “Yes, maybe, depending on what challenges the team faces and how they approach those challenges.” This practice does not generate results in a yes-or-no fashion; instead, it is meant to guide your actions to achieve the outcomes that you desire. It is about gaining insight into the past and present. I asked the Daily Norseman faithful to propose some questions in the feed . There were definitely some interesting ones, but what I want to focus on involves the quarterback position. Here is the question I posed: “Is Kyler Murray going to be a successful starting quarterback for the Vikings this season?” I did a three-rune reading for this. This type of reading is informed by the past, present, and future. Alternatively, it examines the situation, challenge, and outcomes. Here’s the Run(e) Down The first rune that presented, which represents the past/situation was Algiz ( al-geez) , which translates to elk/protection. It acts as a shield to ward off negative energy. The way I am interpreting this is in regard to the narrative around Kyler Murray. His tenure in Arizona didn’t end on the highest note, and there are many detractors who think he is “overrated” or “washed.” Algiz presenting itself tells me that Murray has not lost his confidence. This rune perfectly encapsulates Kyler’s transition to the present in that he is in a prove-it year on a vet minimum salary. He is here to play and win football games (I hope). The second rune is an interesting one. The rune that presented is Perthro ( pear-throw) , which translates to fate, with an emphasis on rebirth. There is also a shroud of mystery that accompanies this rune. The challenge for Murray seems to entail reinventing himself to maximize his output. Perthro is rife with hidden knowledge and “secrets yet to be revealed,” as well as the unpredictability of life and certain outcomes. The challenge for Minnesota’s starting quarterback is going to be navigating through many obstacles and challenges with a growth mindset. I think Kevin O’Connell is the coach to bring the best out of him, as growth is a major aspect of his coaching philosophy. We could see a rebirth for Kyler Murray, but it won’t happen in one or a few games. This evolution is going to run its course throughout the duration of the season. The final rune presented, which represents the future/outocmes, is Hagalaz ( hawg-ah-laz) . This one is incredibly interesting. It translates to “hail” and represents the wrath of nature, uncontrolled forces, and destruction. Now, the runes present themselves in a certain way, and it is my job to interpret them. This rune presented itself upright and in its normal position. I talked in my Rune article last week about how anything can happen in the NFL season, and that theme is continuing with today’s reading. The wrath of nature seems to be referring to the nature of the NFL season, which, as we all know, has its ups and downs with uncontrolled forces creating unpredictable situations. However, my focus here is on the word destruction. What is being destroyed? I choose to believe that there are two answers to this. The first is the destruction of the current narrative surrounding Kyler Murray. A player who had a great start to his career, who maybe didn’t make football his primary focus, and who ended up fizzling out with the team that drafted him. I think the fact that he is playing this season for pennies on the dollar shows his willingness to prove himself. The other destruction I foresee is that of our enemies. We have already vanquished the Packers at home and Chicago on the road. What other enemies will we conquer? My hope is for a revenge playoff game against the anointed NFC favorite LA Rams. Before they get there, however, the Vikings need to conquer the division and destroy perceptions of them as the team that fizzles out after great regular seasons. I am leaving this reading feeling positively about what the season has in store for Kyler Murray. The game in Tampa Bay will reveal a great deal of what that journey is going to look like. If the defense can keep playing the way it has, and Murray can protect the football, I envision a fruitful Sunday. Until next Skol!

title: SB Nation Reacts Results: Ugly Win Gives Vikings Fans Big Confidence Boost
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears in Week 2 wasn’t exactly one that anybody would put in the Louvre as far as its beauty is concerned, but it was effective enough to get the Vikings to 2-0 on the young season, as well as put them at 2-0 in the NFC North […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Byron Murphy Jr. #7 of the Minnesota Vikings and James Pierre #23 react against Chicago Bears during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings’ 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears in Week 2 wasn’t exactly one that anybody would put in the Louvre as far as its beauty is concerned, but it was effective enough to get the Vikings to 2-0 on the young season, as well as put them at 2-0 in the NFC North division race. According to our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week, that’s enough to give the confidence of Vikings fans a significant boost heading into their Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We had two questions for Vikings fans to answer this week, with the first one being the usual query as to how positive fans are about the direction of the team. After last Sunday, the number took a big jump upward. According to those who responded to our poll, 75% of you believe that the team is now heading in the right direction. Given the fact that the number sat at just 46% following the Week 1 win over Green Bay, that’s a pretty big leap. It was at 60% going into the season opener, so one big drop was followed by an even larger increase. Hopefully, we’ll just continue to see that number going upward as the season progresses. Speaking of the season progressing, our other question for this week was what you thought the Vikings’ record would be going into their bye week, which will happen in Week 6. Their three games between now and then are this week’s game at Tampa Bay, next week’s home game against the Miami Dolphins, and their Week 5 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. Most of you feel that the Vikings are going to be sitting pretty heading into the bye. We did get a majority for this one, with 51% of our respondents saying that the Vikings will have one stumble between now and the bye to go into their off week sitting at 4-1. Another 33% believe that they’ll go into the bye with a perfect 5-0 mark, while 13% believe that they’ll drop two of the next three games before they take a week off. Lastly, 4% of those who responded to this week’s poll are, apparently, angry Chicago and Green Bay fans who feel the Vikings are going to hit a three-game losing streak between now and Week 6 and go into the bye staring at a 2-3 record somehow. I’m not saying that last one can’t happen. . .I’m just saying I don’t think the chances of it happening are very high. Those are your SB Nation Reacts results for this week, folks! title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Emphasis on fast start in Jacksonville
summary: The New England Patriots will look to build their first winning streak of the 2026 season. To do so, they will have to take down the Jaguars in Jacksonville. Naturally, most of our attention this week was on that particular game. However, there is a lot going on at One Patriot Place these days, so […]
full_text: The New England Patriots will look to build their first winning streak of the 2026 season. To do so, they will have to take down the Jaguars in Jacksonville. Naturally, most of our attention this week was on that particular game. However, there is a lot going on at One Patriot Place these days, so let’s clean out the notebook. Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes. Starting fast The Jacksonville Jaguars have turned EverBank Stadium into a difficult place to play under new head coach Liam Coen. Jacksonville is 8-2 at home since Coen took over, with the Jaguars frequently establishing control early in games to put opposing teams in difficult positions. “They play well at home,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “They’ve been getting great first half leads. I think they have been outscoring their opponents at home in that stadium by probably 10 points in the first half, so that’s something that really sticks out.” The Jaguars did just that in their home opener this season against the Cleveland Browns. With the defense forcing two turnovers, Jacksonville opened up a 24-0 first-half lead to a 34-10 victory. “They feast off turnovers. They’ve been creating turnovers and turning those into points,” Vrabel said. “From what I could tell from Cleveland, I think that there were 42,000 [fans], but they were into it, and they were loud for what it was recorded as from an attendance standpoint. So, I think that those fans are football fans. They crave football. Just like us, if they give them reasons to cheer, they’ll be loud.” As the Patriots get set to kick off in Jacksonville this Sunday, avoiding a similar early deficit will be critical. New England appeared to be on its way to a fast start last week against the Steelers. Drake Maye found DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry for completions on the opening drive, quickly moving the ball across midfield. But after Maye passed up an open Eli Raridon down the field and checked the ball down to Rhamondre Stevenson in the flat, Stevenson fumbled, ending the drive with a turnover. “I feel like we had a good jump last week of starting fast and had a chance right there to make a big play. We ended up having a turnover on the first possession,” Maye said. “So, I think one of the biggest things for us is starting fast, especially for myself.” Starting fast in Jacksonville will require Maye to find completions early and take what the defense gives him while remaining aggressive when opportunities arise. Decisiveness has been a key point of emphasis when discussing the quarterback’s struggles to open the season, and Maye knows the Patriots need to capitalize when there are opportunities to push the ball downfield. With warm conditions — Maye’s preference — and a Jacksonville defensive front that has not been as dominant as the ones New England faced against Seattle and Pittsburgh, Sunday could provide an opportunity for Maye and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels to get the offense moving in the right direction. “I think how we play and our mentality and going down there and trying to get off to a good start is going to be the most important,” McDaniels said. “Then trying to play the game for 60 minutes and have no big letdowns in the game.” Jacksonville environment Current forecasts in Jacksonville project the temperature to just be in the low to mid 80s at kickoff on Sunday with humidity levels around 40%. Josh McDaniels noted the team’s experience in Miami early last season will be something they can rely on as they will also have to rely on their depth more this week. His quarterback, however, looks forward to playing in the warm conditions. And after Jacksonville opened up 1,000 standing room only tickets for the game, Mike Vrabel is expecting a noisy environment. “It sounded like they were into it against Cleveland, and they certainly got off to a good start and gave them something to cheer about,” Vrabel said. “We’ll have to always be prepared for the environment and make sure that all our cadences are sound and ready to go.” Question marks The Patriots listed both safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) and tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) as questionable for Sunday’s game. Woodson appears to be trending in a positive direction after practicing in a limited fashion on Friday, although the team did elevate safety Mike Brown from the practice squad. Brown will be a candidate to fill in for Dell Pettus (injured reserve) as the personal protector and depth behind/in place of Woodson. As for Raridon, the rookie appears to be trending in the wrong direction after not practicing on Thursday and Friday. If Raridon is ultimately inactive, undrafted tight end Tanner Arkin will likely be back on the game day roster while Cameron Latu, who played 14 snaps in relief last Sunday, will assume the role behind Hunter Henry. Chicken wings Drake Maye hasn’t played to his usual standard through two games. That’s why he’s seen pictures of chicken wing bones on the screen in the Patriots QB room. “He’s someone that wants to chase perfection, and I think that is good,” QBs coach Ashton Grant said. “And I like try to feed into that a little bit because there’s always a little bit more meat on the bone. We joke around with, like chicken wings, and if you guys ever eat wings, and people throw them away, and there’s a little bit of meat left. “I try to show him pictures of bare bones of the meat just to be like, ‘there’s always more for us to do’.” Defending Lawrence Coaching the Tennessee Titans in the AFC South, Mike Vrabel often matched up against Trevor Lawrence. Ahead of Week 3, Vrabel noted the quarterback is more decisive and comfortable than he was early in his career and how opposing defenses can no longer count on Lawrence turning the football over. The Patriots will still look to force Lawrence into some mistakes on Sunday, and sticking with the blitz may be the best path. Lawrence currently ranks 27th out of 32 qualified quarterbacks in EPA vs. the blitz to go along with two turnover worthy throws. Jaguars skill group Lawrence operates in an offense loaded with skill talent around him. While the team drafted Brian Thomas Jr. in the first-round in 2024 and traded for old friend Jacob Meyers last season, wide receiver Parker Washington is the straw that stirs the drinks. On the year, Washington’s 36.7% target share trails only Jaxon Smith-Njigba. “He’s crushing it right now. He’s a great player,” defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr said. In the backfield, second-year running back Bhaysul Tuten has taken the lead role in Liam Coen’s West Coast offense. Tuten’s home-run ability is apparent, as he leads the league in runs over 15+ MPH with 12 — three more than Jahmyr Gibbs — and is third among qualified running backs in missed tackles forced. “He’s just got great contact balance, but he’s fast. I think he stretches and cuts. I think he’s got excellent vision. I think he runs hard, runs behind his pads,“ Vrabel said. ”I think the speed probably’s the biggest factor.“ OLB check-in After placing rookie Quintayvious Hutchins on injured reserve, the Patriots 53-man roster features just four outside linebackers: Dre’Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder, Gabe Jacas, and Jose Ramirez. With Jones (shoulder) out for Sunday, Ponder and Jacas will be relied upon heavily with Ramirez joining the rotation after signing from the practice squad this week. “He has been a really good practice player for us. I think he has improved since the time he has been here,” Vrabel said of Ramirez. “Multiple times being recognized by taking the reps that we talk about being on the show team and using those to his advantage. So, there will be an opportunity, we’ll see, for him to be able to help us this week when we get down to the 48-man roster.” End of half Through two games, Mike Vrabel and VP of game strategy and operations John Streicher have had some questionable end-of-half decisions. In Seattle, the Patriots’ defense recorded a third-down stop at the 22-yard line…
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots elevate veterans Mike Brown, Jeremiah Pharms Jr. from practice squad for Week 3
summary: The New England Patriots traveled to Duval County with two seasoned call-ups from the practice squad. The organization elevated safety Mike Brown and defensive tackle Jeremiah Pharms Jr. on the eve of Sunday’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Both are scheduled to revert following the road trip. Brown, 26, agreed to terms in Foxborough as […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Mike Brown #33 of the New England Patriots looks on against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots traveled to Duval County with two seasoned call-ups from the practice squad. The organization elevated safety Mike Brown and defensive tackle Jeremiah Pharms Jr. on the eve of Sunday’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Both are scheduled to revert following the road trip. Brown, 26, agreed to terms in Foxborough as the 2026 league year opened in March after not being tendered as a restricted free agent. He was released and retained on the practice squad at the end of August. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound Miami of Ohio product has appeared in 35 games since entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie in 2022. Following tours on the practice squads of the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Cleveland Browns, Brown joined the 53-man roster of head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans in 2023 and started five games while in the AFC South. The safety’s career includes 60 tackles and a pair of pass deflections through 503 snaps on defense and 760 snaps on special teams. Pharms, 29, signed to New England’s practice squad at its formation after being waived at the league’s cutdown deadline . The 6-foot-2, 300-pound defensive tackle stands 31 games and a handful of starts into his stay. After going undrafted in 2020 and making stops with the Champions Indoor Football League’s Wichita Force and USFL’s Pittsburgh Maulers, he made his way to Gillette Stadium ahead of training camp in 2022. Across 594 snaps on defense and 128 snaps on special teams for the Patriots, Pharms has totaled 45 tackles, two sacks and one fumble recovery. The former linebacker out of Sacramento City College, San Joaquin Delta College and Friends University finished the 2025 run to Super Bowl LX on the practice squad before re-upping on a futures contract. Two standard elevations remain for Brown and Pharms before 53-man roster transactions would be required to take the field. One active spot remains open for now. After the past week saw guard Mike Onwenu , outside linebacker Quintayvious Hutchins and safety Dell Pettus all land on injured reserve, the Patriots ruled out veteran edge rusher Dre’Mont Jones on the final injury report. But tight end Eli Raridon and safety Craig Woodson made the trip with questionable game statuses. Sunday’s kickoff at EverBank Stadium is set for 1 p.m. ET.
