title: Eagles-Bears Final Injury Report: DeVonta Smith will play, Jonathan Greenard questionable
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Saturday in advance of their Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Chicago Bears. The Eagles ruled three players OUT: Dallas Goedert, Hollywood Brown, and Fred Johnson. Goedert is expected to miss multiple games due to a knee injury. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 28: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball against Kevin Byard III #31 of the Chicago Bears at Lincoln Financial Field on November 28, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Saturday in advance of their Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Chicago Bears. The Eagles ruled three players OUT: Dallas Goedert, Hollywood Brown, and Fred Johnson. Goedert is expected to miss multiple games due to a knee injury. Prior to Monday at 4:00 PM Eastern, the Eagles are expected to temporarily elevate Zach Ertz from the practice squad to help fill Goedert’s absence. Ertz, Johnny Mundt, and E.J. Jenkins will be Philly’s three tight ends on Monday night. Will be interesting to see just how big of a role Ertz plays after returning to the Eagles earlier this week. Brown was unexpectedly added to the report on Friday with an ankle injury. He also wasn’t able to practice on Saturday. With Brown out, perhaps the Eagles will make Elijah Moore active for the first time this season. Fred Johnson is a new addition to the report. The veteran blocker missed Saturday’s practice due to a knee injury. With Big Fred out, rookie Markel Bell figures to serve as the swing tackle behind starters Jordan Mailata and Lane Johnson. Bell might’ve already been the top backup there anyway. The Eagles ruled one players QUESTIONABLE: Jonathan Greenard. Greenard was previously ruled out of the Eagles’ first two games, so, this is a step in the right direction for his eventual return. The veteran edge rusher was a full participant during Saturday’s practice and he said he feels “ pretty optimistic ” about his chances to play. Even if Greenard does suit up, Vic Fangio cautioned that he’s not ready to handle a normal workload of snaps at this point in time. But it could still be good for him to join a rotation that also features Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa. The Eagles’ pass rush could sure use a spark. It would be nice to see that unit come alive in Chicago. Players notably listed without a game status: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Jalen Carter, Andrew Mukuba, Tyler Steen, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley. Barkley was limited on Thursday before fully participating on Friday and Saturday. He’s ready to play despite suffering a stinger in Week 2. Smitty was upgraded to full participation on Saturday after being limited on Friday and not practicing on Thursday. Seems like the Eagles were managing his workload to help get him to Monday night. Carter, like Barkley, was limited on Thursday before being full go the last two days. He’ll continue to play with a cast on his hand due to an wrist injury. Mukuba is ready to start after fully participating the last two days. Steen was a full participant in practice all week. Bigsby and Shipley are set to play. Bigsby did not practice on Thursday before being upgraded to limited on Friday and upgraded again to full on Saturday. Shipley did not practice on Thursday before being limited on both Friday and Saturday. I wonder if Shipley could have a smaller role than usual due to being less than 100%. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES INJURY REPORT (SATURDAY) OUT WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) TE Dallas Goedert (knee) OT Fred Johnson (knee) QUESTIONABLE EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) … RESERVE/INJURED CB Jakorian Bennett TE Grant Calcaterra OG Landon Dickerson S Andre’ Sam TE Eli Stowers WR Johnny Wilson Bennett, Calcaterra, and Stowers are eligible to return to the active roster after Week 4. Dickerson is eligible to return to the active roster after Week 5. Sam and Wilson are out for the season. RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large CHICAGO BEARS INJURY REPORT (SATURDAY) The Bears ruled three players OUT: starting quarterback Caleb Williams, linebacker Noah Sewell, and defensive lineman Shemar Turner. Williams suffered a hamstring injury during the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings and was unable to participate in practice this week. Sewell and Turner are ineligible to be activated from injured reserve until after Week 4. The Bears ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Tyson Bagent. Bagent was a full participant in Saturday’s session after missing the previous two practices. Bagent has yet to officially clear the concussion protocol but it looks like he has a realistic chance to play against the Eagles on Monday night. If Bagent is unable to suit up, Chicago will be down to third-string QB Case Keenum. The Bears notably did NOT list starting cornerback Tyrique Stevenson with a game status. He was listed under did not participate on Thursday before being upgraded to limited on Friday. Stevenson was upgraded again to full go on Saturday. But the Eagles still might want to test out that hamstring injury he’s dealing with. Bears kicker Cairos Santos is also set to play despite missing practices earlier this week. He was full go on Saturday. title: NFL Week 3 games: Eagles rooting guide
summary: The third weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 3 games. EAGLES GAME PHILADELPHIA EAGLES at CHICAGO BEARS: The Eagles are favored to beat the Caleb Williams-less Bears. If they can manage to avoid losing to a backup quarterback, they’ll be […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 22: Quarterback Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys hugs quarterback Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens after agame at AT&T Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The third weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 3 games. EAGLES GAME PHILADELPHIA EAGLES at CHICAGO BEARS: The Eagles are favored to beat the Caleb Williams-less Bears. If they can manage to avoid losing to a backup quarterback, they’ll be 3-0. Go Birds. NFC EAST TENNESSEE TITANS at NEW YORK GIANTS: The Giants’ 2026 campaign is probably cooked now that Jaxson Dart is out for the season. The Eagles could like to see them pick up some meaningless wins so that New York doesn’t get a very high pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. But the G-Men have an easy schedule coming up and it could be preferable for them to not get any sense of building momentum with Jameis Winston filling in at quarterback. Root for the Titans. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS at WASHINGTON COMMANDERS: The Commanders’ outlook isn’t looking so great. They’re the worst kind of 0-2 you can possibly be with two division losses already. And Jayden Daniels is expected to miss multiple games due to injury. But in the off-chance he comes back and this team builds some momentum, better for them to be in a bigger hole to try to dig out of. Even if it means Seattle picks up a win that helps the Eagles as it relates to pursuing a top seed in the conference. Though that’s a nice silver lining to a Commanders upset here. Root for the Seahawks. BALTIMORE RAVENS at DALLAS COWBOYS: Given that this is the floating AFC opponent for the Cowboys, this is their least meaningful game this season in terms of impact on the standings. From a narrative perspective, Dallas will be feeling good about themselves with a win. Let’s hope that they’re instead feeling terrible after Lamar Jackson torches that defense to drop the Cowboys to 1-2. Root for the Ravens. If the Eagles win on Monday night and all of their division rivals lose, the NFC East standings will look like this: 1) Eagles: 3-0 2) Giants: 1-2 3) Cowboys: 1-2 4) Commanders: 0-3 Opportunity for the Eagles to have a nice little cushion entering Week 4. NFC PLAYOFF PICTURE CAROLINA PANTHERS at CLEVELAND BROWNS: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Browns. NEW YORK JETS at DETROIT LIONS: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Jets. ARIZONA CARDINALS at SAN FRANCISCO 49eRS: Hard to say which team is the bigger threat in the conference. Just kidding. Root for the Cardinals. MINNESOTA VIKINGS at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS: The Bucs winning the NFC South could be preferable to the Panthers or Saints taking the crown. Also need to see the Vikings drop some games at some point. Root for the Buccaneers. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at NEW ORLEANS SAINTS: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Raiders. LOS ANGELES RAMS at DENVER BRONCOS: The Eagles play the Rams in Week 4. LA still looms large as a threat in the conference, so, it would be good to see them lose here. Put more simply: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Broncos. WHAT’S LEFT CINCINNATI BENGALS at PITTSBURGH STEELERS: The Eagles play the Steelers later this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Steelers to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Steelers. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS: The Eagles play the Jags this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Jags to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Also, the Eagles own the more favorable of two 2027 fifth-round picks either from the Pats or Bears. Might as well root against New England. Root for the Jaguars. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS at BUFFALO BILLS: No Eagles impact. If you’re rooting for Jalen Hurts to win MVP, you’ll want Josh Allen to cool off from his red hot start in a loss to the Bolts. HOUSTON TEXANS at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS: No Eagles impact. Both of these AFC South teams are off to 0-2 starts. The Birds will face each of them later this season. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS at MIAMI DOLPHINS: No Eagles impact. Though it’s easier to root against the Chiefs.

PICK: 49ers -8.5 Loading… MINNESOTA VIKINGS (-1.5) at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS: I think the consensus is too high on the 2-0 Vikings and too low on the 0-2 Bucs. PICK: Buccaneers +1.5 Loading… BALTIMORE RAVENS (-3.5) at DALLAS COWBOYS: The Ravens’ Week 2 fourth quarter collapse doesn’t undo the promise they showed in Week 1 under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Dallas has struggled against mobile quarterbacks, so, expect a big day from Lamar Jackson in a Baltimore win. PICK: Ravens -3.5 Loading… LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at NEW ORLEANS SAINTS (-3): Fun matchup between two upstarts. I’ll lean with the Saints since Kellen Moore is cooking and Tyler Shough has been one of the NFL’s better passers early in the season. Even if the Raiders win, not going to regret betting against Kirk Cousins. PICK: Saints -3 Loading… LOS ANGELES RAMS (-2.5) at DENVER BRONCOS: The Rams should be favored by more here. Bo Nix doesn’t look good. The Rams had a rough go in Week 1 but they bounced back well in Week 2. They’re going to win this game as well. PICK: Rams -2.5 Loading… PHILADELPHIA EAGLES (-3.5) at CHICAGO BEARS: The 2-0 Eagles are 0-2 against the spread this season. As of me typing this sentence, the Bears’ quarterback situation is still up in the air. The Eagles were 4.5-point road favorites prior to Tyson Bagent returning to practice on Saturday. Prior to that development, I liked the Eagles to beat Case Keenum by a score of 23 to 19. But with Bagent potentially suiting up, I’ll give the Bears an extra point to make it 23 to 20. The Eagles stay on brand and refuse to win a game comfortably. PICK: Bears +3.5 Loading…

title: Nick Sirianni loves Jalen Hurts and everything the QB has done for the Eagles
summary: The Eagles are headed to Chicago this weekend for a Monday night matchup, but before hitting the road, head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters about Zach Ertz’s progression, how much he appreciates Jalen Hurts as the QB in Philly, and why there hasn’t been much play-action. When asked about the special teams loophole they […]
full_text: Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles are headed to Chicago this weekend for a Monday night matchup, but before hitting the road, head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters about Zach Ertz’s progression, how much he appreciates Jalen Hurts as the QB in Philly, and why there hasn’t been much play-action. When asked about the special teams loophole they utilized with Braden Mann, Sirianni said that everything they’re doing is within the rules of the game, and they’ll continue to do whatever gives them the best chance to win each week. Here’s what else the head coach had to say: On Zach Ertz’s progression “Zach [Ertz] had a good week. Tight ends in general had a good week. We’ll see where we are at the end of the day.” As for how the team is getting Ertz and also Kenny Moore ramped up throughout the week after the pair skipped any kind of training camp before joining the team. Sirianni explained that they look to see how the guys are moving, how they feel after practice, and whether they’re learning the system. “There’s habits that the guys that have been here have practiced over and over and over and over again, and you’re doing your best job to catch them up on those habits as fast as you can, whether it’s tackling, the way we go about that, the way we go about strip attempts, the way we go about protecting the football. That comes with time. Every situation’s a little bit different, and everybody’s situation’s a little bit different.” The head coach noted that there isn’t a specific checklist the go off of, but they have things they are looking at and questions they look to answer after every practice. On individual success “I want individual success for all our guys. Those individual goals don’t happen, though, without team success first. Everything we do is going to be to help us have the best chance to win.” He went on to talk about how rookie WR Makai Lemon is going to be a big part of that as they move forward, because they know he’s talented. The head coach said he’s growing more confident in the young receiver each week in practice. “Of course, I’d want him to have 10 catches for 100 yards, and Smitty [DeVonta Smith] and Tay [Dontayvion Wicks] and whoever. That’s just the way the season goes, and we’ll see where we continue to go. I think Smitty and Tay have had a good start to the season, and there’s things that Makai’s doing that a stat sheet can’t show, and we’re pleased with where he’s continuing to go. His touches will come because he’ll be out there because he consistently does the right thing when the ball’s not going to him.” On Jonathan Greenard returning Earlier in the week DC Vic Fangio said Greenard was closer to returning than he was last week, and Sirianni echoed that sentiment on Saturday. “[Jonathan Greenard]’s had a good week. It’s exciting to have him out there. We’ll see where we are at the end of today. Like I said, today’s a very important part of the process, but I feel like he’s had a good week. It brings good energy. I’ve really enjoyed, I mean, I’ve hated that he hasn’t been able to go in for him and for our team, but I’ve really enjoyed being around him on the sideline and what he’s like on a game day. He’s got a lot of knowledge, and he’s really good with his teammates, and that’s been very noticeable to me, and I’m excited when it’s the time to get him back out there. He’s worked his butt off to be able to get back out there as soon as possible. I’m excited to have that leadership that I’ve seen him show when not playing. Excited about him, and he’s had a good week, though.” On playing QB in the NFL Sirianni was asked about Jalen Hurts’ recent comments about how challenging it is to be a quarterback in the NFL and everything that goes along with that. The head coach agreed that it was tough to put it into words, but highlighted the hard work and responsibility that goes into it, and that it all comes with a lot of credit and a lot of blame. “It takes great mental toughness to be able to sustain the ups and downs that all these players go through on a weekly basis. I’m not sure I could put it into words, but there is immense responsibility to an organization and to a city in playing the most important position in sports. I’m sure glad we have Jalen Hurts playing the most important position in sports in Philadelphia because I love him and everything that he’s done for us and everything he’ll continue to do for us. I always say about Howie [Roseman], I couldn’t ask for a better partner in this and I feel the same way about Jalen. I couldn’t ask for a better partner in this journey.” On the lack of play-action Sirianni said that right now there’s a low sample size to really assess any kind of reasoning or pattern for the lack of play-action. He noted that they’ve been doing some no-huddle stuff, which affects that, as well, and they’ve faced situational hurdles, like being behind the sticks a bit and not being in first and second down and manageable. “We know that we’ve been behind the sticks a little bit. I think that’s a fair question. I think it’s just early and it’s early in a sample size, and [I] imagine we’ll have this conversation again or not. We’ll see where we are at that particular point. It’s a little early right now because we’re still figuring out who we are and what we do best and all those different things.” The plan was always to have some kind of mix of things they had done in the past and some of the new things that they wanted to do this year.

title: Bears’ backup quarterback returns to practice ahead of Eagles game
summary: Perhaps the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 3 opponent won’t be down to starting their third-string quarterback after all. Bears backup QB Tyson Bagent returned to practice on Saturday after clearing the concussion protocol, according to Chicago head coach Ben Johnson. But while Johnson said that Bagent has been cleared, that’s not actually possible just yet: Bagent […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears passes the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Perhaps the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 3 opponent won’t be down to starting their third-string quarterback after all. Bears backup QB Tyson Bagent returned to practice on Saturday after clearing the concussion protocol, according to Chicago head coach Ben Johnson. But while Johnson said that Bagent has been cleared, that’s not actually possible just yet: While Tyson Bagent was cleared to practice today, he needs to go consecutive days without symptoms after practicing before he is technically and fully cleared from concussion protocol. https://t.co/ucR2wGU4QM — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 26, 2026 Bagent did not participate in the Bears’ practices earlier this week, which meant Case Keenum looked to be in line to start against the Eagles. But now it seems like Bagent could fill in for injured Bears starting quarterback Caleb Williams. For what it’s worth, the betting line for this game has recently been adjusted. The Eagles originally opened as 3.5-point road favorites against the Bears. The spread grew to 4.5 points after news emerged that Bagent was in the concussion protocol. Now the line is back to having the Eagles as 3.5-point road favorites. Earlier this week, we asked Windy City Gridiron for some insight on Bagent , who hasn’t made a start since the 2023 season: As for Tyson Bagent, he remains in concussion protocol at the time of my answering this question, so I don’t think he will play on Monday, but you can’t say he is definitely out, especially with the extra day of rest. Bagent is what you want in a QB2. He has some mobility to get out of issues; he can operate an offense efficiently, and he doesn’t make a ton of mistakes. But make no mistake, he isn’t a starter. He doesn’t have a strong arm and doesn’t have a lot of dynamic attributes. There is a pretty large percentage of Bears fans that adore Bagent and think he can step in and the offense will barely miss a beat. I am not of that school. The offense takes a significant hit without Caleb Williams, but it shouldn’t be inoperable with Bagent. Whether it’s Bagent or Keenum starting on Monday night, the Eagles will need to prove they can stop the Bears’ run game. Doing so should theoretically be easier since Vic Fangio’s defense shouldn’t have to worry about Chicago’s passing attack to the same extent if Williams was playing. But after watching the Eagles’ defense get pushed away by the Bears in Philly last season, the onus is on the Birds to prove they’re up to the challenge of slowing down this offense.

title: Eagles thoughts: Grin and bear it
summary: Ben Johnson was touted as The Next Big Thing. He caused quite a stir when he turned down the Commanders in 2024, so the Bears landing him last year was no small feat. His first year was a huge hit, Chicago won a playoff game for the first time since 2010. But we’ve seen plenty […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears reacts against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ben Johnson was touted as The Next Big Thing. He caused quite a stir when he turned down the Commanders in 2024, so the Bears landing him last year was no small feat. His first year was a huge hit, Chicago won a playoff game for the first time since 2010. But we’ve seen plenty of coaches struggle in year 2. Second Album Syndrome Smash debuts are hard to follow up. The Bears first single was an incredible 59 point banger, but their next release was a 3 point dud. That was the biggest game-to-game drop off since 1973 when the Falcons scored 62 points, coincidentally in Week 1, and followed that up by being shutout. Ouch. A week after D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai each had over 100 yards rushing, they combined for 92. Certainly the poor weather last week contributed to the Bears offense coming to a screeching halt. But as was the case in Detroit, stop the run and you can stop Ben Johnson’s offense. Easier said than done, as the Eagles gave up over 125 yards to both Swift and Monangai last year in a 24-15 loss to the Bears. And that was with Caleb Williams, though he had only 13 yards on the ground. The Bears will be without Williams on Monday, and might not have Tyson Bagent too. Somehow, Case Keenum returned. Keenum has never been a threat to run and in four starts in 2023 Bagent ran for 105 total yards. Now we get to see how good Ben Johnson really is. Or how much this defense is struggling against the run. Bought a Lemon? 110 WRs have started a season with at least two catches that resulted in 4.5 or fewer yards per attempt. There are a few good players that had such bad starts, such as Doug Baldwin, Julian Edelman, Henry Ellard, and Tyler Lockett. But they didn’t recover that season: In 2012 Baldwin would play in 14 games and start 4, and finish with 29 catches for 366 yards, for 12.6 yards per reception. In 2011 and 2013 he had at least 50 catches and 778 yards for 15.5 yards per receptions. In 2010 Edelman would play in 15 games and start 3, but finished the season with just 7 catches. The year before, his first in the NFL after transitioning from QB, he had 37 catches. In 1992 Ellard had a nine year span where he caught at least 52 catches for at least 945 yards, the one he didn’t he had 47 for 727 yards. Last year Lockett got cut after 7 games last year, signed with the Raiders where he performed no better, and is currently a free agent. Most of the players with as bad a start as Lemon has had are a collection of forgettable players. It doesn’t get any better if you look at recent young players, we get an mostly uninspiring group of WRs: Luther Burden, Chase Claypool, Britain Covey, Chimere Dike, DeMario Douglas, D’Wayne Eskridge (twice), Brandon Johnson, Xavier Legette, Darnell Mooney, Josh Palmer, Tyquan Thornton, Cedric Tillman, KaVontae Turpin, Kadarius Toney (twice), Christian Watson, and Isaiah Williams. It would help if Sean Mannion didn’t telegraph screens that went nowhere to him. But there’s still time for Makai Lemon to turn the corner. Pennsylvania Lemon Law Protection lasts for 12 months. College Football Watch List 12:00 – Texas at Tennessee What version of Texas is going to show up? Probably all of them. Texas EDGE Colin Simmons is expected to be one of the top picks, but he’s also listed at 6’3” 246 lbs. That puts him at the near end of the spectrum of height and weight that teams like for high draft picks. If he comes in any smaller or lighter than that, he might drop. Sounds pretty similar to Nolan Smith. 3:30 – Ole Miss at Florida and Oklahoma at Georgia Riq Woolen has been a really good signing so far, and he’s not under contract for next year, so it’s probably a good idea to start looking for a replacement for when he gets paid in free agency. Georgia CB Ellis Robinson doesn’t have the size of Woolen (few do) but he plays like it. You can’t miss Florida EDGE Emmanuel Oyebadejo , he’s 6’7”. The transfer from Jacksonville State had 2.5 sacks last week against Auburn, let’s see how he follows it up. 7:30 – Oregon at USC Center and guard are suddenly issues. Oregon center Iapani Laloulu has also played left and right guard. At 6’2” he’s shorter than the Eagles like for interior linemen, but perhaps Willie Lampkin has them rethinking their priors. USC CB Jontez Williams , a transfer from Iowa State, had a strong season in 2024 and was looking like a day two pick but tore his ACL this time last year. He left last week’s shootout with Rutgers with an undisclosed injury, but should be good to go. Now a year removed from his ACL tear, Oregon should give him a good test.

Two of his seven highest-scoring games ever have been his first two games of 2026. His 2.8 yards per route leads all Eagles wide receivers and ranks seventh among WRs with at least 50 routes this season. His 14.7 yards per target leads all wide receivers with at least 10 targets. More than anything, Wicks has been a big-play weapon with four explosive plays (20+ yards) this season. On Monday night, he will face a Bears defense allowing the league’s fourth-highest explosive pass rate (22.4%). Wicks should be heavily involved in the offense, especially if Saquon Barkley can’t go due to his stinger injury. Eagles Injury Report: Good news on DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley – BGN The Eagles listed two player under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Dallas Goedert and Hollywood Brown. Goedert is expected to miss multiple games after suffering a knee injury in Week 2. The Eagles reportedly will NOT place Goedert on injured reserve, which suggests they’re expecting him to miss three games at most since putting him on IR would require him to miss at least four. With Goedert out, the Eagles will be relying on the trio of Zach Ertz, Johnny Mundt, and E.J. Jenkins at tight end. It’s not exactly clear how the snaps will shake out. Brown is a new addition to the report. He missed Friday’s session due to an ankle injury. Brown was active for Week 1 but did not play any snaps. He saw a few designed touches on offense in Week 2. Now he’s in jeopardy of being ruled out for Week 3. Eagles at Bears Q&A: Can Ben Johnson best Vic Fangio? – Windy City Gridiron The Chicago Bears welcome the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football for the first of several Chicago Bears primetime games in 2026. The Bears will almost certainly be without star quarterback Caleb Williams, and there isn’t even certainty whether it will be Tyson Bagent (concussion) or Case Keenum starting for the Bears on Monday. The Bears have several things in flux, but what situation are the 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles in? To find out more about their opponent, we sat down with Brandon Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation, SB Nation’s Eagles site, to find out a little bit more about what the Bears are going up against on Monday. Here’s that conversation: NFC East Mixtape Vol. 192: Cowboys in Brazil, Eagles on MNF, NYG/WAS moving forward – NFC East Mixtape A new week is upon us and this is a big one for the NFC East. The New York Giants and Washington Commanders are each set to navigate life without their starting quarterbacks… how possible is that really for them? Monday will see the Philadelphia Eagles visit the Chicago Bears who are also down their starter in all likelihood which should make for an opportunity to get to 3-0. The Dallas Cowboys are out of the country this week hosting the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil and to get the full Baltimore perspective NFC East Mixtape Alumna Raichele Privette joins on the audio side! RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton get into it all! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Four Vertz: Will Zach Ertz be Jalen Hurts’ new favorite target on his favorite play? – PHLY Eagles Zach Ertz is back and ready to make an impact while Jalen Hurts was in a reflective mood about the Eagles’ win in Tennessee as they turn the page to Monday night’s showdown with the Chicago Bears as Ertz tried to help replace Dallas Goedert and Sean Mannion tries to get the running game unstuck. Deniz Selman and Brandon Lee Gowton join Bo Wulf to discuss the matchup before EJ Smith checks in with news and notes from the Eagles’ facility. Eagles notebook: Zach Ertz ’embraces’ mentorship role with Eli Stowers; Jake Elliott weighs in on Harry Kane’s NFL pursuits – PHLY Eagles I’d be remiss if I didn’t take advantage of the international soccer world’s intersection with the NFL this week, so I asked Jake Elliott about The Athletic’s report that Harry Kane is hoping to finish his decorated playing both in Major League Soccer and as a kicker in the NFL. For those unaware, Kane is a 33-year-old soccer player from England, one of the best strikers of his generation and currently playing for Bayern Munich, one of the world’s biggest clubs. He probably has the power to compete against NFL specialists, but surely becoming one of the 32 best kickers available to the NFL is more complicated than that? “I think he has a shot,” Elliott told PHLY. “He’s obviously an incredibly unique talent. I think there’s going to be a unique learning curve as well. It’s so hard to say.” Elliott said Kane’s biggest challenge will probably be mastering the technique of kicking a football on a high trajectory rather than driving the ball on a line. The 31-year-old Eagles kicker said goalkeepers typically have an easier time switching from soccer to football because of the difference in technique, and even those players often take a few years to fully groove the motion. Enemy Intel – The Bears – Iggles Blitz Rome Odunze and Luther Burden are the key receivers. Burden is very dangerous after the catch. Odunze is averaging 19.0 yards per reception on the year. The Bears have an excellent group of TEs. Colston Loveland is the star. He only has one catch so far this season, but he is a big time talent. Cole Kmet is very good as well and Sam Roush gives them a good #3 TE. Coach Ben Johnson is going to be pissed off that his team only scored 3 points last week. He will be driven to show the rest of the league that the Bears can win without Williams as the QB. Expect a creative gameplan. Expect the unexpected. Chicago will need to score points because their defense isn’t great. DE Montez Sweat is the best pass rusher. DT Grady Jarrett can be disruptive, but he’s banged up right now. Devin Bush and TJ Edwards are the LBs. Neither guy is filling up the stat sheet so far this year. They have combined for 15 tackles, 1 TFL and 1 PD. Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman leads the team with 17 tackles. He has a good combination of size and speed. Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson are the corners. Stevenson is second on the team with 14 tackles. He is dealing with a hamstring injury. If Stevenson is out, there could be a shuffle in the secondary. full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Gennings Dunker #73 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during pregame warmups prior to a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers made a number of roster moves ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, highlighted by rookie offensive guard Gennings Dunker landing on injured reserve. According to insider Tom Pelissero , Dunker is expected to miss four to six weeks on IR with an MCL sprain. The third-round rookie first appeared on Pittsburgh’s injury report on Thursday with a knee designation. The Steelers announced the signing of running back Travis Homer to the 53-man roster to fill Dunker’s spot, opening up a slot on the Steelers’ practice squad. Also ahead of the Bengals game, the Steelers have temporarily elevated running back Lew Nichols and defensive back Doneiko Slaughter from the practice squad to the active/inactive roster. Both will revert back to the practice squad following the game. This marks Slaughter’s third elevation this season. He cannot be elevated again after Week 3 unless he is signed to the Steelers’ 53-man roster. The Steelers’ additions of running backs and a defensive back reflect Rico Dowdle being out for Sunday’s matchup, and both Jaylen Warren and Joey Porter Jr. being questionable. Porter is not expected to play versus Cincinnati.

title: Steelers vs. Bengals: Week 3 picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers enter Week 3 at 1-1 and looking to avoid a second consecutive loss. In order to get to 2-1, they’ll have to defeat the unbeaten Cincinnati Bengals. who are coming off a dominant 20-6 win over the Houston Texans. Will Pittsburgh bounce back? Here is how our staff sees things going down. […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks to pass against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers enter Week 3 at 1-1 and looking to avoid a second consecutive loss. In order to get to 2-1, they’ll have to defeat the unbeaten Cincinnati Bengals. who are coming off a dominant 20-6 win over the Houston Texans. Will Pittsburgh bounce back? Here is how our staff sees things going down. Mike Nicastro (2-0): Mike Nicastro: The Steelers face an early season critical juncture when their AFC North rival comes to town. So far through two weeks the offense has been less than inspiring, and the Bengals revamped defense looks to be for real. All signs point to Cincy, but nothing is given in this league. I think the return of Michael Pittman Jr. will allow Aaron Rodgers to have a safety blanket, as DK Metcalf has lost that title. Rico Dowdle’s injury will work as a blessing in disguise, as it’ll force them to use Jaylen Warren 80% of the time, which should have always been the case. Somehow the offense wakes up, just when they’ve been left for dead, and the front seven continues their reign of terror against Joe Burrow and his ailing back. Steelers 24, Bengals 23 . Ryan Parish (1-1) : Heading into the season, I was fairly certain these two teams would split the season series. While I still believe that, I initially thought Pittsburgh was more likely to win the first contest while the Bengals adjusted to their new look defense and the changes to their offense they proclaimed were coming. Now, though, the Steelers look like the team still needing to figure themselves out. I think it’ll be a better showing than last week, but I’m not ready to buy into the Steelers further until they can show a pulse and some semblance of a plan on the offensive side of the ball. Bengals 17, Steelers 9 . Ryland Bickley (1-1) : The Bengals’ offense is better than what the Steelers’ defense has faced this year, and I’d be worried about how the still-developing Pittsburgh offensive line handles game-wrecking nose tackle Dexter Lawrence. I fully expect the Steelers to be a somewhat improved team from last week’s painful loss, but it’s hard to be too optimistic. It’s an early-season divisional game — there could be some surprises — but I expect Cincinnati to emerge with the win. Bengals 24, Steelers 20 . Austin Bechtold (2-0): Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins will be too much to handle for the Steelers, especially with Joey Porter Jr. unlikely to play. Does anyone trust the offense right now? I certainly don’t. Mike McCarthy’s offense has scored fewer points in his first two games than Matt Canada and Arthur Smith’s offenses. Not great. Shuffling the offensive line and giving Max Iheanachor a shot is a good change. I want to see Germie Bernard continue to get comfortable with Aaron Rodgers after a good debut last week. The Steelers keep it close at times, but the struggles on offense will remain. Bengals 24, Steelers 17 . Joey Bray (2-0) : These teams appear to be on different timelines right now. Cincinnati is 2-0 with what looks to be a massively improved defense headlined by Dexter Lawrence with a high powered offense that hasn’t found its top speed yet. Pittsburgh seems to be sputtering and hanging on for dear life offensively. It’s hard for me to imagine this game goes well for Pittsburgh even though it’s an early season divisional matchup at home. Until Pittsburgh’s offensive line and run game shows serious improvement, it’s almost impossible to trust them to put up many points especially against a quality defense. Bengals 28, Steelers 10 . Jarrett Bailey (1-1): Everything says the Steelers will lose this game, and if you’re picking with your brain, you’d probably pick the Bengals. However, Pittsburgh’s defense has been tremendous through two games. And while Ja’Marr Chase and Joe Burrow hooked up for two scores last week, the Bengals put up just 20 points. In a low-scoring game, the Steelers find a way. Steelers 20, Bengals 17. Let us know what you think in the comments . Pat Freiermuth has a big game The Bengals defense has struggled to contain tight ends to open the season, with Houston’s Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau combining for 14 catches and 174 yards last week against Cincinnati. That’s a promising matchup for Steelers’ tight end Pat Freiermuth, who has averaged over 70 receiving yards in his last four games against the Bengals. And this year, Freiermuth has been a much bigger part of the Pittsburgh offense than in 2025; though two weeks this season, he’s already logged a team-best nine receptions. All signs point to another productive outing for Freiermuth on Sunday. The Steelers defense takes a step back While the Steelers’ defense hasn’t been without hiccups to start the season, it’s largely been one of the NFL’s best units, ranking top 10 in both yards and points allowed per game through two weeks. However, they haven’t faced an offense as strong as Cincinnati’s yet. In Week 1, the Steelers drew a favorable matchup against the Falcons with Cooper Rush at quarterback. And in Week 2, Pittsburgh performed solidly limiting Drake Maye and the Patriots, but New England was without its top receiver in A.J. Brown. This week, the Steelers won’t be facing a short-handed opponent. The Bengals feature quarterback Joe Burrow along with one of the league’s best wide receiver rooms in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Pittsburgh had some flaws in coverage and tackling last week, especially at the safety position, which will only be more tested against Cincinnati. Pittsburgh could really use Joey Porter Jr. this week, but even if he does play, it’ll be a difficult first assignment after being limited or a non-participant in practice since the summer. The Steelers have the league’s No. 3 passing defense through two weeks. Don’t expect the numbers to remain that elite against the Bengals. Jaylen Warren has more receiving than rushing yards With Rico Dowdle out against the Bengals, expect a heavy dose of Jaylen Warren at running back on Sunday. Warren himself is questionable, but seems likely to play. Steelers RBs coach Ramon Chinyoung on the RB rotation this week with Rico Dowdle likely being out: "With Rico being in the position he is now, Jaylen (Warren) is going to go out, he's going lead the group and when he needs a breather, we'll make sure he can receive that so he… — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) September 25, 2026 That said, don’t expect a productive rushing game from Warren. The Steelers’ offensive line has struggled through two weeks and might shuffle its lineup ahead of Week 3. And the Bengals have the league’s third-strongest rushing defense through two weeks of the season, largely due to elite nose tackle Dexter Lawrence. As a result, the Steelers might lean into Warren’s yards after catch ability as a dump-off option in the passing game, especially with quarterback Aaron Rodgers getting rid of the ball quickly against an improved Bengals pass rush this year. Warren hasn’t had the most productive start to the season, with just 89 total rushing yards and 61 as a receiver through two games. Still, he’s the team’s third-leading pass catcher thus far, and is due for more involvement on offense this week. What are your predictions for Steelers vs. Bengals? Join the BTSC comment section and let us know!

title: 5Qs, 5As: Seahawks-Commanders preview with Hogs Haven
summary: On their way to hoisting the second Lombardi Trophy in franchise history, the 2025 Seattle Seahawks steamrolled the Washington Commanders 38-14 in a primetime beating. This Sunday, the two teams will face off in Week 3 with the Seahawks looking to remain undefeated, while keeping the Commanders winless. To preview the game Field Gulls teamed […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 02: Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks talks with Dan Quinn of the Washington Commanders after an NFL football game at Northwest Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images On their way to hoisting the second Lombardi Trophy in franchise history, the 2025 Seattle Seahawks steamrolled the Washington Commanders 38-14 in a primetime beating. This Sunday, the two teams will face off in Week 3 with the Seahawks looking to remain undefeated, while keeping the Commanders winless. To preview the game Field Gulls teamed up with Hogs Haven , with contributor eboracum providing the answers to the five questions posed this week. Since readers are here to read the answers to the questions, there’s no point in wasting time and it’s right to the questions asked and the answers given. 1. The Commanders had an unexpected playoff run in Dan Quinn’s first season before injuries derailed the 2025 campaign. What is the feeling in terms of whether Quinn may be on the hot seat if 2026 doesn’t go well, or does the former Seahawks defensive coordinator have job security regardless of how the season plays out? I think Quinn will definitely be on the hot seat if the season goes poorly again. The biggest strike against him is that he’s supposed to be a defensive head coach, but the defense has looked terrible in his first two years coaching here. It may have improved this year with DC Daronte Jones bringing in the Flores-style defense from Minnesota, but even the new defense has given up too many explosive plays, largely from players seeming to execute poorly or making mistakes in coverage assignments. The team under Dan Quinn has also seemed to start the season a bit slow and sloppy and even in 2024 needed a few weeks before things seemed to come together. I worry that although he’s a great motivator, he might not be great at ensuring attention to detail. 2. The Jayden Daniels injury is obviously not great for either the team or the young signal caller. Where does fan sentiment stand in terms of Daniels durability after he missed nine games during the 2025 season? Are fans still excited, or is there worry this is a redux of the RG3 career arc? Jayden is different from RG3 in some important ways. RG3 was a limited QB who couldn’t play from the pocket and relied on his athleticism in a college-style read-option offense to make plays on the field. Injuries robbed him of some of that special athleticism and NFL defenses adapted to the read option, both of which forced him to play more from the pocket, which he simply couldn’t do at a high level. Jayden is the opposite in that he’s a very proficient pocket passer in addition to being a great scrambler; the running plays are just a bonus to his game, but he can still win from the pocket. However, he has had a lot of trouble staying on the field since last year and fans are certainly worried about it. In particular, he seems to keep re-injuring his left elbow, which has some wondering if the left elbow injury from last year never fully healed. Fans are a spectrum and some may already be willing to write Jayden off as too much of an injury risk, but I personally think the team needs to keep building around him. This team has been in the QB wilderness too long and franchise QBs are too hard to come by. Jayden seems to have all the requisite traits of a franchise QB, I think we’re more likely to have success figuring out how to keep Jayden healthy (and making sure he’s fully recovered from his previous injury) than going back into the QB wilderness. 3. Who is a player on offense and on defense for the Commanders whose name Seattle fans may not recognize, but who could have an outsized influence on the outcome of the game? On offense, rookie WR Antonio Williams was taken in the 3rd round of this year’s draft. He’s a great route runner and seems to already understand a lot of the nuance of the WR position. As a result, he’s been getting more and more time on the field and it’s clear the staff trust him. Williams caught 4-of-4 targets for 64 yards and a TD in week 1. He only caught 3-of-3 passes for 24 yards in week 2, but his route share jumped from 28.9% to 54.8% and they even designed a trick play for him in week 2, so I think it’s clear the coaching staff want to increase his role in the offense. On defense, I will go with CB Mike Sainristil, though not in a good way. Last week, it seemed like the Cowboys gameplanned to target Sainristil in coverage, sometimes preferring to throw into his coverage even when they had open WRs further down the field. I wouldn’t be surprised if the Seahawks find ways to match JSN up on Sainristil and direct the ball that way. 4. The Commanders have new coordinators on both sides of the ball this season. How much different do things look for the groups, or did the new coordinators bring some level of continuity within the system? The intent was to overhaul both systems. On offense, new OC David Blough actually brings some continuity in that he was the team’s assistant QB coach last year, so the players are familiar with him, but the offense he designed is supposed to be more of a Ben Johnson-style offense built around an outside zone run game and heavy use of under center formation and play-action passes (as opposed to the Kliff Kingsbury-style up tempo spread offense that was almost entirely out of shotgun). In addition to the Ben Johnson offense just being good, I think a big reason for this shift was to protect Jayden Daniels by keeping him in the pocket and using play action fakes to freeze opposing pass rush. On defense, new DC Daronte Jones was brought in to implement a Brian Flores-style attacking defense like he oversaw in Minnesota. This is an aggressive defense that relies on a high blitz rate, simulated pressures, disguised coverages, and lots of pre-snap defensive motion to confuse and pressure the QB. Through two weeks, it has seemed to be very effective at limiting the opposing run game, but has struggled with giving up explosive passing plays. I think the problems in coverage are partly due to players still learning their responsibilities, but also because this style of defense relies on pressure and confusion making the QB’s job difficult, so if that doesn’t happen, the coverage on the backend doesn’t have a lot of support. 5. What’s your prediction for the outcome of the game and why? Well, the Seahawks are currently 7-point favorites and I rarely go against Vegas for score predictions, so if I had to make a score prediction it would be something like 24-17 in favor of the Seahawks. The thing I am most worried about is the Commanders’ injury situation. As of Wednesday practice, the Commanders have 6 DNPs and 8 limited players due to injuries. It seems like last year’s crazy injury mess is rearing its head again and I have no idea why or what can be done about it. The biggest difference between Washington’s magical 2024 season and dismal 2025 season was injury luck, and if that’s already going against us, this is likely to be a repeat of last year. I actually have a lot of confidence in Marcus Mariota as our backup QB, but the OL was already down its best player LT Laremy Tunsil and now may be without its second-best player RG Sam Cosmi (concussion), which could hold back the entire offense. On the other side of the ball, if the secondary can’t get their communication and assignment issues sorted out, they could allow a lot of explosive passing plays. And now it’s on to the inactives on Sunday morning at 8:30 am Pacific Time.

Entering Week 3 of the 2026 season, there are many reasons for the Seattle Seahawks and their fans to be feeling great. After defeating the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2, the Seahawks set a franchise record with twelve straight wins (including playoffs). On top of that, one of those wins was a Super Bowl victory. With all of the winning, it would be a shock to see a large sample of fans feel that the team is not headed in the right direction. However, let’s find out what polled Seahawks fans thought. As to nobody’s surprise, a whopping 96% of polled Seahawks fans are confident the team is headed in the right direction. When the team keeps winning as they are, this makes a lot of sense. The only thing I remain curious about is why the four percent of polled fans are not confident in the direction the team is heading. For arguments sake, there could be some caution about the team’s recent injury news. Both starting safeties, Ty Okada and Julian Love, will be out against the Washington Commanders. However, neither of these injuries appear to be long term. On top of that, starting quarterback, Sam Darnold will be returning this week. The placement of right guard Anthony Bradford on injured reserve could be a potential reason for concern , however backups Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens both looked promising in their snaps against the Cardinals. Perhaps the four percent of polled fans are simply cautiously optimistic about the team rather than confident? Or maybe they just hit the wrong button as this author has accidentally done in the past. Moving into the Commanders game, the Seahawks enter the week as heavy favorites against the Marcus Mariota led team. Do Seahawks fans agree that the team will win this weekend? And if so, by how much? Of the polled Seahawks fans, the overwhelming majority believe Seattle will take care of business this week, and by a decent margin. 89 percent of polled Seahawks fans believe the team will win by at least 9 points, with 36 percent believing it will be a blowout of 17 or more points. Only six percent of polled Seahawks fans believe that the Commanders will pull off the upset. This is not a surprising result considering the results of the poll above, the Seahawks winning 12 straight games, and now with quarterback Sam Darnold returning. Likely for these same reasons, the national media all appear to believe the Seahawks take care of business this week as well. Time will tell if all of these predictions come true. title: Why it doesn’t make sense for the Seahawks to trade Drew Lock
summary: With Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold returning to the starting lineup this week against the Washington Commanders, Drew Lock recedes back to his backup position. With Lock performing very well in his limited time as a starter, as well as the flurry of injuries to starting quarterbacks this season, some have began to wonder if […]
full_text: With Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold returning to the starting lineup this week against the Washington Commanders , Drew Lock recedes back to his backup position. With Lock performing very well in his limited time as a starter, as well as the flurry of injuries to starting quarterbacks this season, some have began to wonder if he could be a potential trade chip for the Seahawks. Of the quarterback injuries this season, the longest injury seems to be to the New York Giants quarterback, Jaxson Dart, who will miss the rest of the regular season . The Giants also happen to be the team that Lock was with back in 2024. Of course, the Seahawks could trade Lock. However, doing so would be an awfully risky move for a legitimate Super Bowl contender. The argument for trading Lock would be that the team does not expect Darnold to be out of the starting lineup again this season, and that Lock is on an expiring contract. On top of this, Jalen Milroe is on the team and could be your backup quarterback. Because of this, you might as well get a draft pick for him before he likely leaves for another team next season. However, there are flaws with this line of thinking. Of course, the team would not expect Darnold to get hurt again. However, this is the NFL; injuries occur all the time. Yes, Jalen Milroe could serve as your backup quarterback. However, if Darnold were to get hurt, does the team really trust him to take legitimate quarterback snaps in an NFL game? Outside of the week three preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs last month, Milroe has looked very much like a developmental project rather than a true NFL quarterback. At least at this point. Maybe in 2027 he will be ready for that jump to be a true backup, one snap away from playing legitimate NFL snaps. However, for the Seahawks to put him in that position right now would be playing with fire for an otherwise Super Bowl ready team. Lock has proven to the Seahawks that he can lead this team to victories if forced into the lineup. Even national pundits like Daniel Jeremiah have said that the Seahawks can win a Super Bowl with Drew Lock . The argument about getting a draft pick now for Lock rather than allowing him to leave in free agency is also flawed. Yes you could get a draft pick for him now, however it likely will not be worth trading him away. A good trade example to look at was when the Cincinnati Bengals traded for Joe Flacco midway through last season. The Bengals sent the Cleveland Browns a 5th round pick for Flacco and a 6th round pick . Of course, Flacco is much older than Lock and looked abysmal in Cleveland. However, Lock (like Flacco was) is on an expiring contract, so the team trading for him would be trading for merely a rental on Lock. Because of this, it is highly unlikely that Seattle would get anything better than an early day three pick. The Seahawks also already have a plethora of draft picks for 2027 , even after the trade for cornerback Avery Smith earlier this season. On top of this, if Lock were to leave in free agency after the season, the Seahawks would likely get another draft pick anyway for him through the compensatory formula. If you look at the 2026 NFL compensatory picks , the Philadelphia Eagles got a third round pick for losing Milton Williams, who signed a contract with the New England Patriots for an average of $26 million per year . The San Francisco 49ers got a fourth round pick for losing Aaron Banks, who signed a contract with the Green Bay Packers for an average of $19.25 million per year . This shows that the Seahawks would have a legitimate shot at a 4th or even 3rd round draft pick if Drew Lock can sign for more than $20 million per year next offseason. That number is very realistic for Lock after his performance over the last two games. Two quarterback contracts that can be a guide for Lock are Jacoby Brissett and Malik Willis. Brissett recently signed a new deal with the Arizona Cardinals that puts him at an average salary of $15.5 million per year. Willis meanwhile signed this last offseason with the Miami Dolphins with an average salary of $22.5 million per year . There is an argument that Lock’s contract could look closer to Willis’s rather than Brissett’s based on the fact that Lock will be a true free agent and have a potential bidding war. On top of this, Lock at 29 years old is closer in age to Willis (27) than Brissett (33). All of this said is to illustrate that the Seahawks are likely to get a 3rd or 4th round compensatory pick for Lock when he likely leaves in free agency next offseason. Because of this, there is no reason to trade him away unless you can net a pick better than a 3rd round pick. There is a very slim to no chance that a team would trade Seattle a pick better than a 3rd round pick for a rental contract on Lock. For all of these reasons, it makes little to no sense for the Seahawks to trade away Drew Lock.
author: John Tapia

title: Seahawks vs. Commanders, Week 3 preview: Another Seahawks blowout win in Landover?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks head to Washington on Sunday with Sam Darnold back and a chance to move to 3-0 for the second time under Mike Macdonald. The Washington Commanders, meanwhile, are 0-2 and will turn to Marcus Mariota after Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow injury against Dallas. On paper, this is a game Seattle should […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 02: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks catches a pass for a touchdown against Tyler Owens #18 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter in the game at Northwest Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks head to Washington on Sunday with Sam Darnold back and a chance to move to 3-0 for the second time under Mike Macdonald. The Washington Commanders, meanwhile, are 0-2 and will turn to Marcus Mariota after Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow injury against Dallas . On paper, this is a game Seattle should be able to control. But that’s also what makes it so important for the Seahawks to remain focused. Here are the biggest things to watch. History, 3-0 starts and a familiar trip to Washington The Seahawks have started a season 3-0 eight times in franchise history, most recently in 2024. Before that, Seattle opened 3-0 in 2020 and 2013, with the latter eventually ending in a Super Bowl championship. The 2024 team went on to finish 10-7. Seattle also has plenty of recent history against Washington at Northwest Stadium. The Seahawks won 38-14 in their most recent trip there in 2025. Before that, Seattle won 20-15 in 2020 but lost 17-15 in 2021. The Seahawks also won 27-17 in Washington in 2014. Last year’s game is particularly relevant because Washington lost Daniels to an elbow injury in that matchup as well. Now Seattle gets another chance to leave Washington with a win — and another opportunity to start a season 3-0. The Seahawks’ biggest opponent might be the Seahawks If there is one thing that could make this game more difficult than it needs to be, it might not be Washington. It might be Seattle itself. The Seahawks were a little sloppy in their season opener against the New England Patriots, committing 10 penalties for 98 yards. They also allowed Drake Maye to extend plays with his legs and create problems outside the pocket. Last year’s game against Tennessee provides another useful reminder. The Titans entered that matchup as a significant underdog and still managed to put 24 points on Seattle, one of only a handful of teams to score more than 20 against the Seahawks all season. Seattle was dealing with injuries, including the absence of Ernest Jones, and the defense ultimately settled down and secured a 30-24 win. But Tennessee was able to create enough good moments to make a game that looked favorable on paper much more uncomfortable than expected. That’s the type of situation Seattle has to avoid against Washington. The Commanders are 0-2 and will be without Daniels, while Seattle’s defense has allowed only 17 points through two games. None of that means much if the Seahawks give Washington unnecessary opportunities through penalties, missed assignments or defensive breakdowns. There is also a much more difficult stretch coming immediately afterward, with the Los Angeles Chargers, San Francisco 49ers, Denver Broncos, and Kansas City Chiefs waiting in four of the next five weeks. Seattle has no reason to look beyond Washington yet. The Seahawks need to play this game on its own terms and show the difference between being the more talented team and actually playing like one. Keep Marcus Mariota in the pocket This is one of the biggest jobs for Seattle’s defense on Sunday. Mariota only threw for 111 yards after replacing Daniels against Dallas, completing 11 of 16 passes, but his value comes from what happens when the play breaks down. He can escape pressure, extend the play and force a defense to cover for longer than it wants to. Seattle has already dealt with that problem this season. Drake Maye ran seven times for 47 yards against the Seahawks in Week 1, and several of his most important plays came when he escaped the pocket and extended drives. Jacoby Brissett presented a very different challenge in Week 2. He was not the same threat as a runner, and Seattle’s defense was able to keep Arizona much more contained, holding the Cardinals to only 151 total yards. Mariota is much closer to Maye in that regard than Brissett. The Seahawks’ pass rush therefore needs to be disciplined. Getting pressure is important, but maintaining rush lanes and keeping Mariota inside the pocket may be even more important. Seattle needs to make him consistently win from the pocket rather than allowing him to turn broken plays into first downs with his legs. JSN, Shaheed, and Horton need to make Washington pay Jaxon Smith-Njigba has been spectacular through two games, with 17 catches for 277 yards and four touchdowns playing with Drew Lock. After his nine-catch, 155-yard, three-touchdown performance against Arizona, he will naturally attract plenty of attention from Washington’s defense. That’s where Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton become important. Shaheed has had a relatively quiet start, with 39 receiving yards through two games, and this could be an opportunity for him to make a bigger impact with his speed and ability to stretch the field. Horton was also relatively quiet in his first game, but he has already shown that he can hurt Washington, catching four passes for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Seattle’s 38-14 win over the Commanders last season. Seattle doesn’t need to force the ball to either receiver. But if Washington puts additional attention on JSN, the Seahawks need Shaheed and Horton to take advantage of the opportunities that come their way. Another test for the offensive line and running game Seattle has rushed for 259 yards through two games, averaging 4.2 yards per carry, and the running game has provided a useful complement to the passing attack. Washington’s run defense has already shown some vulnerability. Philadelphia ran for 136 yards against the Commanders in Week 1, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. That gives Seattle another matchup worth watching. If the Seahawks can establish the run early, they can make Washington’s pass rush less effective, control the tempo and force the Commanders to commit more defenders to the box. That, in turn, should create more favorable opportunities for Seattle’s receivers. It will also be another test for the offensive line. If Seattle can consistently create movement up front, the offense should have multiple ways to attack Washington rather than relying entirely on the passing game. Final thoughts This is a game where Seattle needs to avoid making things harder than they have to be. Washington is dealing with a quarterback change and enters the matchup without a win, but that doesn’t mean the Commanders can’t take advantage of mistakes. The Seahawks have already seen how quickly a mobile quarterback can extend drives, and they have also seen against Tennessee how an opponent can hang around much longer than expected when the circumstances allow it. A clean, disciplined performance would put Seattle in position to do what it should against an 0-2 opponent: control the line of scrimmage, limit Mariota’s ability to create outside the pocket, take advantage of opportunities in the passing game and keep Washington from finding a way back into the game. And with the 49ers, Broncos and Chiefs waiting over the next several weeks, this is an important opportunity for Seattle to show that it can handle the games it is supposed to handle before the schedule gets considerably tougher.

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks go on the road to wrap up September, going all the way from Washington state to, uh, close to Washington, DC. Landover, Maryland, to be exact. It’s the reigning Super Bowl champions against the win-less Washington Commanders in what is the home opener for Dan Quinn’s beleaguered side. Last season, Seahawks at Commanders was deemed worthy of Sunday Night Football . That ain’t happening this year, as FOX will be airing this game as a regional 10 am PT kickoff. Based on the coverage distribution outlined by the incomparable 506 Sports , Seahawks-Commanders is not going to see much attention outside of the local-ish markets. If you’re in the yellow, don’t be mellow, because Seahawks football will be on your local FOX network! Joe Davis and Greg Olsen, FOX’s No. 2 broadcast team, will be on the call for this game. Davis and Olsen worked two of the three Seahawks losses last season (vs. San Francisco 49ers, at Los Angeles Rams), as well as the 26-0 shutout of the Minnesota Vikings. While Davis and Olsen are high up the FOX charts, the distribution of this one is a measly 12 percent . Only the Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers (8 percent) is getting less attention. Check out the rest of the maps and game announcers on 506 Sports .

title: 49ers add 3 defensive linemen from the practice squad; work out 34-year-old Matt Judon
summary: The San Francisco 49ers promoted defensive lineman Viliami Fehoko Jr. from the practice squad and elevated defensive tackle Kevin Givens and Sebastian Valdez. To make room for Fehoko Jr. on the active roster, the 49ers placed wide receiver Demarcus Robinson on injured reserve. He’ll miss at least four games. Fehoko Jr. is listed at 6’5″, […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers promoted defensive lineman Viliami Fehoko Jr. from the practice squad and elevated defensive tackle Kevin Givens and Sebastian Valdez. To make room for Fehoko Jr. on the active roster, the 49ers placed wide receiver Demarcus Robinson on injured reserve. He’ll miss at least four games. Fehoko Jr. is listed at 6’5″, 267 pounds. The former San Jose State product came into the NFL at 276 pounds, suggesting he may have bulked up to play more of an interior role. Coming into the NFL, some of Fehoko Jr.’s athletic profile comparisons were Mason Graham and Walter Nolen—two defensive tackles. Fehoko’s ability to play multiple spots along the defensive line likely earned him a spot on the active roster, until the 49ers get healthier at the position. With Nick Bosa and Romello Height ruled out for Week 3, Fehoko could be the short-term solution at defensive end. Other options on the roster include Keion White, Khalid Kareem, and Ogbo Okoronkwo. That leaves White, a player the 49ers traded for last season, the most experienced edge rusher who will be active against the Cardinals. That may not be the case for long. According to the transaction wire, the 49ers were the only team to have tryouts on Saturday. Here’s who they hosted: Jamin Davis Matt Judon Julian Okwara Dawuane Smoot Davis is a true off-ball linebacker. The 49ers may want the former first-rounder to play in 5-man fronts. Judon, 34, needs no introduction. He last played a full season in 2024. Judon played in just over 300 snaps last season with the Dolphins. Okwara has the body type Morris seems to covet, with an arm length in the 83rd percentile. Cleveland released him after training camp in 2025. Smoot, 31, would be the veteran you sign, knowing he’d understand the assignment. He’s the most experienced, with nearly 2,400 career snaps. Until the 49ers make another move, their defensive line for Week 3 consists of: Keion White Osa Odighizuwa Gracen Halton Khalid Kareem Naquan Jones Ogbo Okoronkwo Viliami Fehoko Jr. Sebastian Valdez Kevin Givens That’s a far cry from what that list looked like heading into September.

title: Former NFL QB says ‘nobody is playing the way Brock Purdy is right now’
summary: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is enjoying arguably the best start to a season of his NFL career. Through two games, Purdy has thrown for 492 yards, five touchdowns, and an interception, while completing a league-high 80.8 percent of his passes and averaging 8.8 yards per attempt. Purdy has been very sharp with his […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is enjoying arguably the best start to a season of his NFL career. Through two games, Purdy has thrown for 492 yards, five touchdowns, and an interception, while completing a league-high 80.8 percent of his passes and averaging 8.8 yards per attempt. Purdy has been very sharp with his decisions and has made a number of impressive throws in both of the 49ers’ first two games, being the catalyst of the offense so far. Over his four-year NFL career, we’ve seen Purdy gradually take the next step, with turnover-worthy plays being his primary issue. Well, as he’s taken on more responsibility for the offense, Purdy has continued to flourish, and he’s in the early running for the MVP race. Several NFL analysts are taking notice. That includes former NFL quarterback and current ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky, who said this week that no quarterback in the NFL is playing like Brock Purdy so far. “Yeah, [anticipating throws is important] very much so in that Kyle Shanahan offense as well,” Orlovsky said on ESPN this week. “And Brock is the ideal guy to operate it. There’s no quarterback in the NFL playing football the way that Brock Purdy is right now. As fast as you can be up top and as calm and almost as slow as you can be neck down. “Josh Allen is playing remarkable football and there’s a lot of quarterbacks playing at a high level, NOBODY is playing the way Brock Purdy is.” — Dan Orlovsky Dan does a great breakdown on how well Brock sees the field 🔥 🎥: @ESPNNFL pic.twitter.com/0DMZrTe3mU — Coach Yac 🗣 (@Coach_Yac) September 25, 2026 “When I talk about seeing blindly, one underneath the center, 7-step drop, free runner essentially because McCaffrey’s got to go there. Look at his feet, slow to fast to slow. He sees somehow as he gets backside to really the number 4 that the dropped coverage releases George Kittle. There it is, beautiful. Underneath the center, drop back once again. Look at this, because no one’s accounting for that linebacker, here comes another free runner. Offensive line has got their 5. Quarterback has to beat it from underneath the center. This is not normal. There’s the soft spot in the defense, a little bit of congestion in the middle of the field between Evans and Juszczyk. Ball still comes out. He doesn’t see those guys. He just sees space. This is the fullback. Breaking down plays, Orlovsky pointed out how Purdy has been throwing to spots, anticipating well and processing at a high level, which is why he’s playing at a level of his own so far this season. “Okay, this play is absolutely nuts,” Orlovsky continued. “Short motion, the halfback out there. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 [step drop]. As he does that, the halfback pulls the underneath coverage. The receiver lifts the deep coverage. He’s throwing this ball to a fullback that is only about 6 feet. He doesn’t see Juszczyk. He just sees the vacated space right there in between those defenders. Josh Allen’s playing remarkable football, and there’s a lot of quarterbacks playing a high level. Nobody is playing the way that Brock Purdy is.” So far, Purdy is first in the NFL in QBR, first in completion rate, and he’s yet to take a sack, despite being pressured 15 times. That completion rate would be even better if not for four drops. Whether he’s been blitzed or not, Purdy has completed at least 80 percent of his passes. It’s been quite the start for him and the 49ers offense through two weeks. Now, of course, it’s only been two weeks. But Purdy is the top reason right now why the 49ers look like contenders.

title: Titans vs. Giants preview with Big Blue View
summary: Ed Valentine of Big Blue View was nice enough to answer 6 questions about his New York Giants ahead of this week’s matchup with the Tennessee Titans. 1 – How is morale with the news that Jaxson Dart is out for the season?  That depends on whether you are asking about the team or the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Jameis Winston #19 of the New York Giants talks to teammates in a huddle prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ed Valentine of Big Blue View was nice enough to answer 6 questions about his New York Giants ahead of this week’s matchup with the Tennessee Titans. 1 – How is morale with the news that Jaxson Dart is out for the season? That depends on whether you are asking about the team or the fanbase. Some in the fanbase have already tossed in the towel on the season. The Giants themselves? As John Harbaugh said on Wednesday, the story of the season has yet to be written, and there are still 15 chapters to go. Players have a job to do, and on Sunday they will be fired up and ready to do it. 2 – What are the early impressions of former Titans DC Dennard Wilson? I like Wilson. I like the aggressiveness he is trying to bring to the secondary. I think he is a very good defensive coordinator. I am less sure about the hand he has been dealt with the Giants’ defensive personnel. 3 – As you know, the Giants and Titans don’t play very often. Who are some of the under-the-radar players that we should keep an eye out for? Under-the-radar guys are sort of difficult right now. I will, though, give you a few players to pay attention to. Offense — Marcus Mbow. If Andrew Thomas can’t go at left tackle (groin/adductor) Mbow will likely be there. He is a second-year swing tackle who did well enough in spot duty last season. — Defense — I’m watching Abdul Carter and Arvell Reese. Both are top 5 picks in the draft, and I’m waiting for impactful, breakout games from both. — Special teams — PK Dominic Zvada is a rookie who has a big leg and has been impressive. 4 – If the Giants could steal one player from the Titans’ roster, who would it be and why? (Bonus points if it isn’t Jeffery Simmons, but I’m not sure where else I’d go if I were you) I love bonus points. Simmons would be the clear choice if I wasn’t playing for the bonus. Great player who would fill a massive need for the Giants on their defensive line. My “bonus points” choice? I’m taking Carnell Tate. I did not want to see the Giants draft Tate at No. 5, and the Titans made sure that didn’t happen. The Giants, though, need more explosive plays, and they need a big-time wideout to pair with Malik Nabers. Thus, Tate. 5- What’s the biggest matchup in the Titans’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? In the Titans’ favor is probably Jeffrey Simmons against the middle of the Giants’ offensive line. In the Giants’ favor — the fact that John Harbaugh is the head coach and Brian Daboll isn’t. 6 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 2.5-point favorites, what’s your score prediction? The Giants win. The Dart loss is a blow, obviously. Thing is, even without Dart I think the Giants are closer to the good team they looked like Week 1 against Dallas than the bad one they looked like in Week 2 against the Rams. I think they play an inspired, determined, physical game and win a close one. Giants 20, Titans 17

This week, we did ask if you expect the Titans to win, and 63% of you said you do: It’s hard to say what that percentage would have been if Jaxson Dart wasn’t out for the year, but it’s safe to say it would have been significantly less.
