title: What to expect from the much-anticipated Giants-Daboll reunion
summary: All eyes will be on former Giants coach Brian Daboll, who returns to New York as the Titans' offensive coordinator.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- There will be a lot of familiar faces in new places when the Tennessee Titans and New York Giants face off at MetLife Stadium on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

 All eyes will be on former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who returns to New York as the Titans' offensive coordinator. Former Giants assistant coaches Shea Tierney and Carmen Bricillo, along with players Wan'Dale Robinson , Austin Schlottmann , Daniel Bellinger and Cor'Dale Flott , will also make the return to their former team's field. Waiting for Tennessee will be Giants quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan, who was the Titans' head coach before Robert Saleh was hired, and former Titans, now Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Although there will be so much familiarity scheme-wise, the Titans believe the deciding factor will be the players' execution.

 "It really comes down to the Jimmys and Joes," Robinson told ESPN. "You don't really worry about the X's and the O's so much, it's more about the matchups and who you know you can go after, and I'm sure on their side, they're doing the same thing."

 Daboll said he's grateful for the Giants giving him his first opportunity to be a head coach in 2022. He spent just over three seasons there, leading the Giants to a 20-40-1 record, including a divisional playoff game appearance in his first season. The Giants fired Daboll in November 2025 after a 2-8 record. But Daboll said there are no hard feelings and he's treating this like any other game as he prepares to return to MetLife Stadium.

 "It's a one-week season every week, so you got to put everything you got into it," Daboll said Thursday. "That's what it is every week in the National Football League. I have a ton of respect for the people in that organization. From top down to the bottom, really good people in that building. I've been on a number of teams that played my former teams before. But it's about our players."

 Robinson signed a four-year, $70 million deal to follow Daboll to Tennessee. Robinson echoed Daboll's sentiments, saying there's no bad blood between him and the Giants. Similar to Daboll, Robinson is excited to face his former team but insists it's "just another game at the end of the day."

 

 The Titans' receivers should get opportunities to make plays against a Giants secondary decimated by injuries. Rookie cornerback Colton Hood was thrust into a starting role last week and allowed four completions on five targets for 42 yards and two touchdowns, primarily matching up with Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams , a future Hall of Famer. Under Wilson, New York has resorted to man defense an NFL-high 18.8% of its snaps this season. Regardless of who's in the secondary, Saleh, who's very familiar with Wilson's defenses, is expecting a battle.

 "He [Dennard Wilson] and I have had a lot of conversations," Saleh said. "I think he's a hell of a football coach. His defenses reflect his personality in that they play their tails off. The back end and the detail at which he coaches from a schematic standpoint is up there with anybody in football." 

 Giants safety Tyler Nubin said he has observed similarities in the Titans' offense under Daboll. 

 "You know what type of coach Dabs [Daboll] is," Nubin said. "He wants to be aggressive and likes to use tight ends." 

 Titans quarterback Cam Ward has attempted only one pass that traveled 20 yards or more. The tight ends have a total of seven targets in two games this season.

 One of the main players around whom Wilson's defense in Tennessee revolved was  Jeffery Simmons , who said he's more than willing to be a resource for the offense if the unit wants tips. After watching Wilson's defense on Monday night, Simmons believes the Giants' style of defense hasn't changed from what Wilson did in Tennessee. Daboll said he and some of the coaches joked about watching previous years of Titans film as well as the Giants this year to get tendencies from Wilson's defenses.

 Similar to the Giants, Tennessee's secondary is banged up. CB Flott missed last week's game because of a quad injury. Flott has been a limited participant in practice this week but said he's trending toward playing Sunday, just in time to face his former team. But Flott has no ill will toward the Giants, who he said allowed him to showcase his talent enough to earn a three-year, $45 million deal with the Titans. 

 While with the Giants, Flott got to line up against wide receiver Malik Nabers in practice. Getting to face Nabers in a game when it counts will be one of the highlights of the week for Flott.

 "It's going to be fun," Flott said. "I can't wait to see him talk s---, have fun and compete. That's just what me and Malik do."

 Of course, winning the game will be the biggest goal for everyone traveling to New York. But Schlottman, who spent two years with the Giants, is looking forward to something else.

 "I'm excited to get a bagel from up there," Schlottman said. "That's about the only thing I'm super excited about. This is another opportunity for us to go out there and execute and win. It's nothing more than that, nothing less than that. It's just that's what it is: the next game."

title: Giants' offense about to 'shift' with Jameis Winston
summary: The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as QB, but now Winston has to take over for the rest of the season.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- It was several weeks into training camp for the New York Giants when offensive coordinator Matt Nagy mentioned that only half the team's plays were installed. At the time it seemed disconcerting, but it makes sense considering the Giants eventually practiced and installed close to 300 plays, according to offensive lineman Jon Runyan .

 All that extensive work is poised to pay off. The offense greenlit by new coach John Harbaugh isn't only Jaxson Dart -specific. 

 "Probably the biggest thing is -- one of the things with this offense when we first got started is we wanted to be able to be prepared to have multiple styles of offense," Nagy said. "And so, if something like this does happen, it doesn't put you in a hole where it changes everything."

 The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as the quarterback before he suffered a knee injury in Week 2 and was placed on IR. His legs and ability to run were a big part of the run game. He had 54 yards in an impressive season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys .

 Backup QB Jameis Winston had two rushes for one yard in a Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and that came trying to escape a sack.

 "All those plays are plays that we have, that we've been practicing and running, it's just kind of more like a shift maybe over a little bit as opposed to ... maybe a lane change as opposed to changing direction or anything like that," Harbaugh said. "More of a lane change."

 The most notable change with Winston at quarterback will be the lack of QB runs. Winston, 32, isn't anywhere near the same threat as a runner as Dart.

 

 The run-pass options are unlikely to be as big a piece of the Giants' offense.

 "We did have a lot more Jaxson-driven-type quarterback runs," Runyan said. "It wasn't necessarily something that we were going to major in like we kind of did last year most of the time. So, unfortunately, a lot of that is out. I mean, could be here and there.

 "Jameis is a gunslinger, obviously. So we're going to run our offense from a run point how I expect we have been through those two games. From a [quarterback] standpoint, I mean a little bit different. I don't think he's going to get the option to run a lot, but you never know."

 Harbaugh has insisted since he arrived that the Giants are going to be a big, physical team. That is what they want to be. They are expected to continue to establish the power run game, try to make it effective and then take shots downfield.

 This is where it could work with Winston.

 "Well, he can throw it," Harbaugh said. "I mean, he's a big, strong, passing quarterback. He can throw the ball. Everybody that follows football has certainly seen Jameis play, and his strengths are evident. So that's what you build around."

 It all bodes well for the Giants' running backs. They are now the focus of the Winston-led offense, beginning with starter Cam Skattebo . He has definitively become the team's No. 1 option while handling 67% of the running back carries the first two weeks.

 The running back pecking order also appears to have taken shape. It's Skattebo followed by Devin Singletary , then Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr .

 Expect to see more Skattebo and fullback Patrick Ricard moving forward.

 "[Ricard] needs to play more. He's a great weapon for us," Nagy said. "Sometimes when you get into these games, whether it's a certain package that you have, none of it's intentional. Some of it just kind of happens.

 

 "It's the same thing, too, with [Skattebo] down inside in the red zone there with carrying the football and stuff."

 This works for Skattebo. He had 16 touches Monday night in the 28-6 loss to the Rams and felt good physically coming out of the game.

 He's open to a bigger workload and more responsibility on his shoulders.

 "I don't look at it as I need to do more," Skattebo said. "It's I get to do more."

 The tight end position could also get affected with Winston at quarterback. Isaiah Likely had quickly become Dart's go-to receiver and security blanket. He caught a team-high eight passes on eight targets in the opener, including a pair on third down on the game-ending drive. It looked to be continuing with a third-down catch on the opening drive against the Rams.

 Likely's targets seem destined to dip with Winston. Tight ends had a target rate of 24% with Dart as the quarterback since he entered the league last season. Winston has targeted the tight end on 19% of his passes over the course of his career.

 "My job remains the same," said Likely, who noted the routes he runs won't change. "Just make the quarterback's life as easy as possible is really my main focus."

 Likely will have to develop chemistry with Winston. He and star wide receiver Malik Nabers spent the entire summer working with Dart to get on the same page. They didn't work at all with Winston.

 It's no wonder that Winston was on the field after practice Thursday getting in extra work with many of his receivers. Among those out there -- Nabers.

 The Giants' No. 1 receiver should be a beneficiary of Winston's desire to push the ball downfield. Speedy wide receiver Darnell Mooney , too. Winston's 9.9 air yards per target is the most by any quarterback since he entered the league as the No. 1 pick of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2014.

 "I mean, he believes in his receivers to go make the plays for him. And we plan out to do that," Nabers said. "And when the opportunity comes, you've just got to go ahead and snatch the opportunity. The fact that he gives us opportunity, that means he believes in the good work that you put in in practice. He believes that you're going to make the play for him, and I trust that he trusts me. So we'll make the play."
